props.name: Time from push to a settled stance
props.bandReference: B1: land pop-up took 1.20 s (SD 0.19) in 23 experienced male surfers: push-up about 0.71 s, reaching about 0.48 s

props.name: Distance between the feet on landing
props.bandReference: B1: feet about 0.63 m apart (SD 0.10) on landing in adult men; scale for juniors and smaller surfers is a gap (SF-01)

props.name: Kicks where the legs do not move together
props.bandReference: G1 SW 7: leg movements must be simultaneous

props.name: Median glide time after each kick
props.bandReference: A short, streamlined glide between kick and pull; depends on race pace. Provisional band

props.name: Strokes where the hands come back past the hip line (after the first stroke)
props.bandReference: G1 SW 7: hands not brought back beyond the hip line during the stroke, except the first stroke after the start and each turn

props.name: Cycles not in the order one arm stroke then one leg kick
props.bandReference: G1 SW 7: the stroke cycle must be one arm stroke and one leg kick, in that order

props.name: Median time for one full stroke cycle (both arms)
props.bandReference: B2: about 1.6 s per cycle (0.63 Hz) at sprint speed in competitive men; cycle time changes with pace (B3). Provisional band for steady swimming

props.name: Distance covered per stroke cycle (÷ standing height)
props.bandReference: Long, efficient strokes; stroke length changes with pace (B3). Provisional band

props.name: Head lift during the breath (÷ standing height)
props.bandReference: Turn the head to breathe rather than lifting it; provisional band

props.name: Peak shoulder roll each side (median across cycles)
props.bandReference: B1: swimmers roll the shoulders more than the hips, and faster swimmers rolled the shoulders less over 200 m. Provisional band

props.name: Bend between upper body and legs in the streamline
props.bandReference: A long, straight body line from fingertips to toes; provisional band

props.name: Distance from the wall when the head breaks the surface
props.bandReference: G1 SW 5, 6, 8: in freestyle, backstroke and butterfly the head must break the surface at or before 15 m after the start and each turn

props.name: Elbow angle in the streamline just after push-off (mean of both arms; 180 = straight)
props.bandReference: Arms straight overhead, hands stacked; provisional band

props.name: Bat in front of the body at contact (÷ standing height)
props.bandReference: Meet the ball in front of the body, centred; provisional band

props.name: Playing elbow in front of the trunk at contact (÷ standing height)
props.bandReference: Elbow forward, away from the body; provisional band

props.name: Knee bend at contact (mean of both legs; 0 = straight)
props.bandReference: Slightly bent knees, weight forward; provisional band

props.name: Bat travel from the end of the backswing to contact (÷ standing height)
props.bandReference: Short, compact swing for the backhand drive; provisional band

props.name: Bat in front of the body at contact (÷ standing height)
props.bandReference: Contact in front of the body, not beside or behind it; provisional band

props.name: Time from the end of the backswing to contact
props.bandReference: B3: advanced players' racket acceleration peaks about 0.1 s before impact; provisional band

props.name: Hip (pelvis) turn from the end of the backswing to contact
props.bandReference: B2: pelvis rotation range 53-76 deg in national-level men; B3: lower-trunk rotation adds racket speed. Widened

props.name: Knee bend at the end of the backswing (mean of both legs; 0 = straight)
props.bandReference: Low, balanced stance to load the legs; provisional band

props.name: Times the ball drops below the playing surface before it is struck
props.bandReference: G1 Law 2.6.4: from the start of service until struck the ball must be above the level of the playing surface

props.name: Times the ball goes in front of the end line before it is struck
props.bandReference: G1 Law 2.6.4: from the start of service until struck the ball must be behind the server's end line

props.name: How far the ball rises after leaving the palm
props.bandReference: G1 Law 2.6.2: the ball must rise at least 16 cm after leaving the palm

props.name: Toss direction away from vertical
props.bandReference: G1 Law 2.6.2: projected near vertically upwards; numeric band is provisional

props.name: Front (non-dominant) arm bend at contact (0 = straight)
props.bandReference: Arms extending through the ball rather than cramped; provisional band

props.name: Contact point in front of the front hip (positive = in front)
props.bandReference: Contact in front of the body; provisional band

props.name: Knee bend at the end of the backswing
props.bandReference: Provisional band

props.name: Shoulder turn at the end of the backswing (angle of the shoulder line to the baseline)
props.bandReference: Shoulders turned past side-on in the backswing; provisional band (no published backhand values found)

props.name: Contact point in front of the front hip (positive = in front)
props.bandReference: Contact out in front of the body; provisional band

props.name: Head movement from backswing to contact
props.bandReference: Steady head through contact; provisional band

props.name: Hip-shoulder separation at the end of the backswing
props.bandReference: B3: shoulder-pelvis separation 20-30 deg in mature forehands

props.name: Knee bend at the end of the backswing
props.bandReference: Load the legs before swinging; provisional band

props.name: Shoulder turn at the end of the backswing (angle of the shoulder line to the baseline)
props.bandReference: B3: mature forehands turn the shoulders about 110 deg to the baseline

props.name: Knee bend on landing
props.bandReference: Soft, athletic landing; provisional band

props.name: Time from landing to the first step
props.bandReference: Push off straight out of the landing; provisional band

props.name: Stance width on landing (feet apart ÷ shoulder width)
props.bandReference: Land a little wider than the shoulders; provisional band

props.name: Contact height consistency across serves
props.bandReference: A repeatable toss gives a repeatable contact point; provisional band

props.name: Hitting-elbow bend at contact (0 = straight)
props.bandReference: B1 meta-analysis: 30.1 +/- 15.9 deg

props.name: Foot on or over the baseline before contact (rule)
props.bandReference: G1 Rule 18: during the service motion the server must not touch the baseline or the court with either foot

props.name: Front knee bend at the trophy position
props.bandReference: B1 meta-analysis: 64.5 +/- 9.7 deg at the trophy position

props.name: Contact height (ball height ÷ standing height)
props.bandReference: B2: about 2.61 m for women about 1.70 m tall (about 1.53 x height); provisional band

props.name: Hitting-arm elevation at contact
props.bandReference: B1 meta-analysis: 110.7 +/- 16.9 deg

props.name: Trunk inclination at the trophy position
props.bandReference: B1 meta-analysis: 25.0 +/- 7.1 deg

props.name: Sideways drift from the starting position to the slide (÷ standing height)
props.bandReference: G2: walk a straight line to the target; the first step crosses only slightly. Provisional band

props.name: Deliveries that do not use the usual number of steps
props.bandReference: G2: four- or five-step approach, the same every time; provisional band

props.name: Variation in step timing during the approach (coefficient of variation)
props.bandReference: Smooth, building rhythm with the last step and slide quickest; provisional band

props.name: Ball height at the top of the backswing (÷ standing height)
props.bandReference: B1: top of backswing about 1.69 m in elite men; B3: peak ball height about 1.43 m in elite bowlers. Wide band for all levels

props.name: Ball-arm elbow at release (180 = straight)
props.bandReference: B1: ball speed fell over a session as wrist and elbow bend at release increased (6 elite men)

props.name: Ball-hand drift off a straight swing line (÷ standing height)
props.bandReference: G2: the arm swings in a straight line towards the target; provisional band

props.name: Time holding the finish still after release
props.bandReference: G2: finish balanced, body facing the target, opposite arm out, ball-side leg behind; settle quickly. Provisional band

props.name: Touches on or beyond the foul line
props.bandReference: G1 Rule 2.8: any part of the body on or beyond the foul line during or after the delivery is a foul; the ball scores no pins

props.name: Slide-knee bend at release
props.bandReference: Low, balanced slide; B2: the knee and hip extend slightly just before release in elite bowlers. Provisional band

props.name: Forward trunk lean at release
props.bandReference: Chest over the slide knee, back long; provisional band

props.name: Passes thrown forward
props.bandReference: G1 11.1: no forward pass, knock or throw; G4 4c: a forward pass gives a free pass

props.name: Hands finishing towards the receiver (÷ standing height)
props.bandReference: Follow through with the hands to the target. Provisional band

props.name: Time from a tag to the pass (tag rugby)
props.bandReference: G3, G4 6e: in tag rugby the ball carrier must pass within 3 seconds (or about 3 strides) of being tagged

props.name: Shoulder turn towards the receiver at release
props.bandReference: B3: turning the pelvis towards the target made rugby passes far more accurate. Provisional band for a running pass

props.name: Body turned away from the opponents' try line at the rollball
props.bandReference: G1 13.1: stand on the mark facing the opponents' try line, parallel to the sideline. Provisional band

props.name: Rollballs not taken on the mark
props.bandReference: G1 13.2: the rollball must be performed on the mark

props.name: Distance the ball rolls back (m)
props.bandReference: G1 13.1: the ball may be rolled back no more than 1 m

props.name: Time from stopping to completing the rollball
props.bandReference: G1 13.4: perform the rollball without delay; a quick rollball beats the retiring defence. Provisional band

props.name: Knee moving inside the line of the foot at the plant
props.bandReference: S1: knee alignment on landing and cutting; movement-quality feedback only. B2: carrying a ball increased knee adduction in side-steps

props.name: Plant-foot contact time
props.bandReference: B1: about 210 ms (planned) and 233 ms (reacting) in elite women; provisional band for all levels

props.name: Plant-knee bend at the step
props.bandReference: Sink onto the plant leg to change direction sharply. Provisional band

props.name: Trunk lean away from the new direction at the plant
props.bandReference: Chest over the plant foot, ready to drive the other way. Provisional band

props.name: Times the marker comes within one disc diameter of the thrower's torso
props.bandReference: G1 Rule 18.1.1.3: a marker less than one disc diameter from the thrower's torso is a disc-space infringement

props.name: Marker's knee bend (mean of both legs)
props.bandReference: G2: knees bent, hips low, on the balls of the feet; provisional band

props.name: Marker's feet apart (÷ standing height)
props.bandReference: G2: feet about shoulder-width; provisional band

props.name: Times the pivot foot lifts or slides before release
props.bandReference: G1 Rule 18.2.2: the thrower keeps the pivot point until the disc is released; G3: dragging the pivot is a travel

props.name: Delay between peak shoulder and peak elbow speed
props.bandReference: B1: a shorter shoulder-to-elbow delay (mean about 40 ms) went with faster discs (r = -0.71) in 5 male players

props.name: Step out from the pivot at release (÷ standing height)
props.bandReference: G3: pivot across and hold the disc away from the body; provisional band

props.name: Trunk turn from wind-back to release
props.bandReference: B2: the backhand relies on trunk and pelvis rotation (trunk range about 151 deg in 5 men, measured in 3D). Lower provisional band for 2D video

props.name: Trunk turned away from the target at release
props.bandReference: G3: hips and chest face the receiver; a side-on stance curves the throw. B2: trunk about 28 deg at release. Provisional band

props.name: Times the pivot foot lifts or slides before release
props.bandReference: G1 Rule 18.2.2: the thrower keeps the pivot point until the disc is released

props.name: Step out to the throwing side at release (÷ standing height)
props.bandReference: G3: step wide and sink into the pivot; provisional band

props.name: Wrist movement from cocked to release
props.bandReference: B2: the forehand used a wrist range of about 79 +/- 7 deg in 5 male players; G3: flick the wrist like a whip

props.name: Hitting-hand height at ball contact (÷ standing height)
props.bandReference: Hit the ball at the top of the reach; provisional band

props.name: Hitting hand in front of the hitting shoulder at contact (÷ standing height; towards the net is positive)
props.bandReference: Contact in front of the hitting shoulder; provisional band

props.name: Time in the air (jump height ≈ 1.23 × flight time² in metres)
props.bandReference: B1: 630 ms (elite) and 560 ms (recreational) in women; B4: jump heights 0.51 m (women) and 0.71 m (men)

props.name: Knee angle at the end of the approach (180 = straight)
props.bandReference: B1: about 110 deg at the end of the approach in elite and recreational women (angle convention not stated in the paper); provisional band

props.name: Knee moving inward on landing (frontal-plane projection angle)
props.bandReference: B3: elite women landed between about 5 deg varus and 5 deg valgus; movement-quality feedback only. Provisional band

props.name: Peak knee bend after landing (0 = straight)
props.bandReference: B4: peak knee flexion 71-73 deg after a spike landing in university players

props.name: Wrists above the shoulders after contact (÷ standing height; above is positive)
props.bandReference: Keep the platform below shoulder height; let the legs do the work. Provisional band

props.name: Contact height: wrists relative to the hips at contact (÷ standing height; above the hips is positive)
props.bandReference: Play the ball between the knees and the waist; provisional band

props.name: Elbow angle at contact (mean of both arms; 180 = straight)
props.bandReference: Straight arms make a flat platform; provisional band

props.name: Knee bend in the ready position (0 = straight)
props.bandReference: Low, balanced ready position; provisional band

props.name: Stance width in the ready position (feet apart ÷ shoulder width)
props.bandReference: Feet a little wider than the shoulders; provisional band

props.name: Hitting-hand height at contact (÷ standing height)
props.bandReference: Contact high, with the arm reaching up; provisional band

props.name: Hitting hand in front of the hitting shoulder at contact (÷ standing height)
props.bandReference: Contact in front of the hitting shoulder; provisional band

props.name: Hitting-arm elbow angle at contact (180 = straight)
props.bandReference: Reach up with a nearly straight arm; provisional band

props.name: Toss height consistency across serves (interquartile range)
Toss height above the contact point (÷ standing height)
props.bandReference: A low, controlled toss for a float serve; provisional band

props.name: Bar forward of its starting line during the pull (÷ standing height)
props.bandReference: Keep the bar close to the body through the pull; provisional band

props.name: Knee angle at full extension of the pull (180 = straight)
props.bandReference: B4: 6 international men reached about 162-170 deg at full extension

props.name: Press-outs (arms still straightening after the lowest point of the catch)
props.bandReference: G2: finishing with a press-out is an incorrect movement

props.name: Foot steps while recovering from the catch
props.bandReference: G2: finish with the feet and bar in line; a stable catch needs few steps. Provisional band

props.name: Downward bar movements before lockout
props.bandReference: G1 IPF 4.3.1: any downward movement of the bar before the final position

props.name: Bar gap from the shins at lift-off (÷ standing height)
props.bandReference: Bar close to the shins, over the mid-foot; provisional band

props.name: Hips rising faster than the shoulders off the floor (ratio of hip rise to shoulder rise, lift-off to knee)
props.bandReference: Hips and shoulders rise together off the floor; provisional band

props.name: Knee angle at lockout (180 = straight)
props.bandReference: G1 IPF 4.3: knees locked in a straight position at completion

props.name: Bar off the line of the mid-foot at the bottom (÷ standing height)
props.bandReference: Keep the bar over the middle of the foot; provisional band

props.name: Hip joint height relative to the top of the knee at the bottom (÷ standing height; negative = below the knee)
props.bandReference: G1 IPF 4.1: lower until the top surface of the legs at the hip joint is below the top of the knees

props.name: Downward bar movements on the way up
props.bandReference: G1 IPF 4.1: no double bouncing or downward movement during the recovery

props.name: Knees moving inward on the way up (frontal-plane projection angle)
props.bandReference: Knees track over the toes; movement-quality feedback only; provisional band

props.name: Forward trunk lean at the bottom
props.bandReference: B1: 70 men peaked at about 29-31 deg in a high-bar squat; B3: low-bar squats lean further forward. Band allows both

props.name: Turns where the chair tips onto its frame
props.bandReference: G1 14.1.4.2: tipping so that a part other than the wheels or castors touches the floor is a violation

props.name: Chair drift during the turn (÷ standing height)
props.bandReference: Pivot on the spot by pushing one rim and pulling the other. Provisional band

props.name: Time to turn through 180 degrees
props.bandReference: A tight, quick pivot gets the player facing the play. Provisional band; classification affects trunk use

props.name: Time per push cycle at speed
props.bandReference: B5: junior players' push cycle about 0.47 s in a 20 m sprint. Wide band for all classes and levels; class-specific bands are a gap

props.name: Left-right push balance (share of drive from the weaker side)
props.bandReference: B5: symmetry about 49% in junior players; a straight line needs even pushes

props.name: Moments the player lifts off the seat
props.bandReference: G1 31.1.1 (read in summary): raising the buttocks off the seat to gain an advantage is a technical foul

props.name: Sequences of more than two pushes while holding the ball
props.bandReference: G1 25.1.1: no more than two pushes while holding the ball; then dribble, pass or shoot (24.1.3)

props.name: Variation in launch angle between shots (SD)
props.bandReference: B3: launch-angle SDs of about 2-3 deg on swishes at a world championship

props.name: Shooting elbow at the end of the follow-through (180 = straight)
props.bandReference: B1: elbow about 128-151 deg at the finish; extend the arm fully towards the rim

props.name: Ball launch angle above horizontal
props.bandReference: B3: swishes launched at about 59 and 58 deg (classes 1-2) and 55 deg (classes 3-4); B2: about 58 deg in class 1.0; B1: 47-52 deg. Lower-class players need a steeper arc; class-specific bands are a gap

props.name: Moments the player lifts off the seat
props.bandReference: G1 31.1.1 (read in summary): raising the buttocks off the seat to gain an advantage is a technical foul

props.name: Time from level change to the end of the step
props.bandReference: B1: about 0.43-0.47 s from the start of the level change to contact in international and college wrestlers (with a still partner); shadow timing is to the end of the step

props.name: Forward travel of the upper back during the step
props.bandReference: B1: upper back (C7) travelled about 0.42 m forward; international wrestlers moved it forward earlier

props.name: Drop in centre-of-mass height relative to stance height
props.bandReference: B1: centre of mass dropped about 0.17 m (international) and 0.24 m (college) from about 0.72 m, roughly 24% and 33%; international wrestlers stayed higher

props.name: Hip height at the sprawl relative to standing
props.bandReference: Coach-panel draft: hips driven down to the mat

props.name: Hip extension at the sprawl (180 = straight line through hip)
props.bandReference: Coach-panel draft: legs kicked back and spread, hips open

props.name: Time from hips down back to stance
props.bandReference: Coach-panel draft

props.name: Time from first movement to hips down
props.bandReference: Coach-panel draft; B1 shows attacks reach the legs in about 0.43-0.47 s, so the sprawl must be quick

props.name: Feet width relative to shoulder width
props.bandReference: Coach-panel draft: a base a little wider than the shoulders

props.name: Variation in hip height while moving (SD)
props.bandReference: Coach-panel draft: hold the level while moving

props.name: Hip height in stance relative to standing tall
props.bandReference: Coach-panel draft for a staggered crouch stance (B1 describes the stance; no stance-height data found)

props.name: Trunk lean forward from vertical
props.bandReference: Coach-panel draft: chest over the knees, back flat, head up

props.name: Stance and start (two- or three-point) v0.1.0
captureTips: Film side-on, about 5 m away, with the whole body in the stance and the first three steps in frame.
Hold the stance still for at least a second, then start on a signal; do 5 or more starts.

props.name: Forward pass (spiral) v0.1.0
captureTips: Film side-on from the non-throwing side (facing the passer's chest at the stride), about 6 m away, with the drop, stride and release in frame.

props.name: Drop punt v0.1.0
captureTips: Prop the phone side-on about 6-8 m away at hip height, on the kicking-foot side, with the last two steps, the ball drop and the follow-through in frame.
For under-18s, a coach or parent films with consent at training, with other players out of shot where possible.
Kick 5 or more drop punts to a partner or target 15-25 m away, using your usual short run-up; slow motion helps.

props.name: Pace bowling delivery v1.0.0
captureTips: Film side-on from square leg or point, about 10 m away, with the whole run-up and follow-through in frame.
Add a second clip from directly behind the bowler, in line with the stumps.
Use slow-motion (120 or 240 fps) and keep the phone still on a tripod.
Film in good light; avoid netting between the camera and the bowler where possible.

props.name: Kayak forward stroke v0.1.0
captureTips: Film from the bank or a safe platform, side-on about 8-10 m away, so the paddler, the whole paddle and the boat are in frame for at least 10 strokes. A kayak ergometer works too. Never film from the water without a supervisor.

Paddle 20 or more strokes at a steady hard pace; add a short sprint if the paddler trains for racing.

For under-18s, a coach or parent films with consent, with other athletes out of shot where possible. Record the athlete's class (F31-34 or F51-57) with the clip so feedback can be compared fairly.
Throw 6 or more times with the frame tied down as in competition, using the shot for the athlete's class.

props.name: Racing push stroke v0.1.0
captureTips: Film side-on from outside the track, about 10 m from the lane, so the athlete pushes across the frame for at least 20 m with the whole chair, both arms and the trunk in view. Never stand on the track.
For under-18s, a coach or parent films with consent, with other athletes out of shot where possible. Record the athlete's class (for example T54) with the clip so feedback can be compared fairly.
Push at race pace after a rolling start; the helmet must be on whenever the athlete is on the track.

props.name: Precision jump and landing (ground level) v0.1.0
captureTips: Ground level only: a standing jump from the floor to a taped line or a low, flat target on mats or a parkour floor. Film side-on at ground level about 4 m away, with take-off and landing in frame.
For under-18s, sessions are supervised by a qualified parkour coach (Parkour UK standards) and a coach or parent films with consent, with others out of shot where possible.
Do 6 or more jumps to the same line, sticking each landing.

Do 6 or more rolls, alternating shoulders if the coach asks.

props.name: Overhand, sidearm and underhand lacrosse shots in elite male players (PubMed 27981885)
props.note: Read (abstract). 12 elite men. The sidearm shot was faster than overhand and underhand, with no difference in accuracy; no single kinematic or force variable predicted speed or accuracy across shots.

props.name: Peng D, Mao Z, Zhang W, Yu J, Zhang S 2023, In vivo knee biomechanics during badminton lunges at different distances and foot positions, Front Bioeng Biotechnol 11:1320404
props.note: Read. 10 female university singles players; lunges at 1.5 leg lengths and maximum distance, with the foot straight or turned out 20 deg. Knee flexion 57-64 deg reported for the braking phase (initial contact to maximum flexion) and 47-52 deg for recovery; how the per-phase value was taken was not confirmed.

props.name: Surfing paddling and swimming kinematics comparison, Biomechanics and Medicine in Swimming XIII (2018), pp. 59-62
props.note: Abstract read; full text blocked. 14 recreational surfers in a 25 m pool, 60 Hz video in Kinovea: paddling stroke rate about 0.94 Hz, speed about 1.27 m/s and stroke length about 1.7 m over a long maximal effort.

props.name: World Curling, The Rules of Curling and Rules of Competition (1 September 2026)
props.note: R1-R13 read verbatim, the rest in summary. Sheet at least 45.72 m long; hog line 6.401 m from the tee; house radii 1.829, 1.219 and 0.610 m. Eight stones a team, two per player per end. R5(c): right-handers deliver from the hack left of the centre line, left-handers from the right. R5(e): the stone must be clearly released before it reaches the hog line at the delivery end, or it is removed. R8(a): sweeping in any direction, no debris in front of a moving stone, finishing to either side of the stone. R11(e): delivery sticks only in wheelchair events at World Curling competitions. R14 (summary): wheelchair curling: chair stationary at delivery, release before the hog line, delivery stick allowed, no sweeping, mixed-gender teams. R6: free guard zone.

props.name: England Squash support: Is eye protection compulsory for all junior squash? (updated 14 July 2025)
props.note: Read. Juniors (under 19) must wear eye protection in all competitions, including adult events; all ages in doubles; strongly recommended in training. Ordinary glasses are not enough. Standard named: BS EN ISO 18527-2:2021.

props.name: Penichet-Tomas A, Calavia-Carvajal S, Pueo B, Villalon-Gasch L 2025, Kinematic analysis of Olympic and traditional rowing mechanics at different stroke rates, Int J Exerc Sci 18(7):610-621
props.note: Read (abstract). 13 elite national-level women at 18, 24 and 30 strokes per minute; leg catch angle and trunk finish angle changed with stroke rate. No values in the abstract.

props.name: FIE Technical Rules (December 2025)
props.note: Articles up to about t.50 read verbatim; later articles in a summary. Piste 14 m x 1.5 m; on-guard lines 2 m from the centre; rear limits 7 m from the centre. Pools to 5 hits or 3 minutes; direct elimination to 15 hits in three 3-minute periods. Turning the back and using the non-sword hand are forbidden; deliberate body contact (corps-a-corps) annuls the hit. Summary: foil target is the trunk, epee the whole body, sabre above the hips; at sabre, a fleche or any forward step where the rear foot passes the front foot is forbidden. Age categories not defined here.

props.name: NFHS softball 'Pitching 101' presentation (umpire training)
props.licence: facts only; unofficial, no publisher stated
props.note: Read. Feet on the plate within its 24 in; one step forward inside the 24 in; leap (both feet airborne) illegal; crow hop defined as a replant of the pivot foot; hand below the hip and wrist no farther from the body than the elbow at release; no more than 1.5 windmill revolutions. Confirm against the official NFHS / USA Softball / WBSC rulebooks.

props.name: Arroxellas RD, Romano RG, Cymrot R, Blascovi-Assis SM 2017, Bocha adaptada: analise cinematica do arremesso e sua relacao com a realidade virtual, Rev Bras Cienc Esporte 39(2):160-167
props.note: Read. 6 athletes (3 BC2, 3 BC4 women), underarm pendulum throws at 5 m: elbow at release about 136 deg (BC2) and 153 deg (BC4) on average, with wide individual ranges (121-175 deg); wrist marker about 27-47 cm above the floor at release.

props.name: Poulet Y, Brassart F, Simonetti E, Pillet H, Faupin A, Sauret C 2023, Analyzing intra-cycle velocity profile and trunk inclination during wheelchair racing propulsion, Sensors 23(1):58
props.note: Read in full. 8 men (5 T54, 2 T53, 1 T52), 400 m from standstill, IMUs on wheels and trunk. Push cycle 0.50-0.60 s (about 100-120 cycles a minute) at 5.6-8.6 m/s; speed varies 0.48-0.60 m/s within a cycle for most athletes. Mean trunk angle from horizontal 0-44 deg; trunk flexion amplitude averaged 24.8 deg in T54 against 11 deg in T53/T52; larger trunk movement went with larger speed variation (r = 0.82). Authors say video cannot resolve the intra-push speed pattern.

props.name: Pro Snooker Blog, Snooker coaching: striking the ball (2011)
props.note: Read. Accelerate through the cue ball; speed comes from backswing length. Drills: pot the blue into the middle pocket with the cue passing over the pocket; a 45-degree version; a red above the black for speed control. Author credentials not stated.

props.name: Wikipedia, Freestyle wrestling (secondary, citing older FILA rulebooks)
props.note: Read. Two 3-minute periods; win by fall, technical superiority or decision; takedown 2 or more points; exposure 2 or 3 points; 1 point to the opponent for stepping out; 9 m main wrestling area with a 7 m central area and 1.5 m protection area. Verify against the current UWW rules.

props.name: AFL, National Female Community Football Guidelines (2019)
props.note: Read. Girls up to 14 may play mixed or female-only; senior women's football from age 16; come-and-try days use wrap tackles only, with no bumping. Contact situations (tackles, ground balls, aerial contests) are the main focus of safe teaching.

props.name: European Gymnastics, Technical Regulations 2025 (in force 1 January to 31 December 2025)
props.note: Read (Part I, Art. 4). Minimum senior ages in the year of the event: men's artistic 18, women's artistic 16, rhythmic 16, trampoline 17, acrobatic 15, aerobic 18, TeamGym 17. Junior bands: men's artistic 15-18, women's artistic 14-15, rhythmic 14-15, trampoline 13-16. Defers to the FIG statutes and Codes of Points.

props.name: British Rowing technique model presentation (Colin Brown, 10 January 2004; hosted by Leicester Rowing Club)
props.note: Read. On-water model: hang body weight on the handle; shins vertical at the catch with no gap between thighs and body; rock over from the hips; recovery smooth with the body set by half-slide; drive legs then body, back opening when the handle is in front of the knees (about a third through); hands out of the finish at the speed they came in; long strokes; time and control into the catch.

props.name: NFL FLAG, Flag football rules (web summary)
props.note: Read. Boys and girls aged 5-17; 5 v 5 on a 70 x 30 yd field; mouthguard required; 7-yd rush line with up to two rushers; quarterback has 7 seconds; no running across the line by the quarterback; no-run zones; flag guarding (stiff arm, covering the flag, lowering the elbow) is illegal; ball dead when a flag is pulled or falls out.

props.name: Oak National Academy, KS4 PE: Korfball shooting skills (lesson)
props.note: Read. Shoot accurately from around the korf and move quickly to avoid a defended shot; two-handed shots are more accurate, one-handed shots are quicker and harder to block; pump fakes create space; a defender within arm's reach directly in front makes the shot defended.

props.name: Utvic N et al. 2025, Exploring the relationship between shot velocity and goal-scoring performance in competitive goalball, Physical Education and Sport through the Centuries 12(2):5-12
props.note: Read. 15 men (B1-B3), radar in matches: best low rolling shots about 62 km/h (50-74), medium rolling 56, thigh-high 51; no significant link with goals. Authors recommend combining throwing mechanics with auditory decision-making.

props.name: Snowsport England, A beginner's guide to skiing and A beginner's guide to snowboarding
props.note: Read. More than 120 clubs and facilities in England, including five indoor snow centres. Helmet described as important for safety (often included with hire). On outdoor dry slopes a long-sleeved top is essential; gloves and waterproofs recommended, waterproofs particularly on dry slopes.

props.name: Sport Aberdeen, Skate UK group lessons FAQ (updated July 2026)
props.note: Read. Eight Skate UK levels, then four star levels; gradings about every 6 weeks; 30-minute group lessons with a qualified coach. Younger children are advised to wear a helmet for the first few lessons; gloves recommended.

props.name: FIFA 11+ manual; Sadigursky et al. 2017 review
WFDF Rules of Ultimate 2025-2028 (official version, effective 1 January 2025; copy hosted by the French federation)
props.note: Read in full. Non-contact and self-officiated (1.1, 1.11). Games to 15; 5-7 players on the field; mixed games should use an alternating 4:3 ratio (5.4). Points start with a pull (7). After a catch the thrower slows without changing direction and then keeps a pivot point until release; a player catching on the run may release within two more ground contacts without changing direction or speeding up (18.2). Stall count: 'Stalling', 1 to 10 at intervals of at least 1 s, marker within 3 m of the pivot (9.1, 9.3); stall-out if not released before 'ten' (13.2.2). Marking infractions include disc space (closer than one disc diameter to the torso), wrapping, straddle and double team (18.1.1). Players must try to avoid contact (12.6). Field dimensions, disc weight, Spirit scoring and beach or youth rules are in figures or appendices not read.

props.name: Zago M et al. 2021, Fatigue induced by repeated changes of direction in elite female football (soccer) players, Front Bioeng Biotechnol 9:666841
props.note: Read in part. 20 elite women: as they tired, hip and knee bend at the plant fell (knee by about 5-20 deg) and approach speed rose in some. Soccer, used as the closest female cutting evidence.

props.name: Wagner H, Buchecker M, Muller E, Kinematic analysis in team-handball jump throw (ISBS proceedings)
props.note: Read. 26 men (likely the same sample as B2). Release speed 20.0 +/- 2.8 m/s; it correlated with peak trunk forward-tilt speed (392 deg/s, r = 0.62), shoulder internal-rotation speed at release (r = 0.53), peak elbow extension speed (r = 0.51) and performance level (r = -0.80).

props.name: CEC (UGC), B.P.Ed Paper 2, Lecture 30: Kho-Kho II (older rule set)
props.note: Read. A sitting chaser may not leave the square without receiving a kho; the active chaser may not cross the central lane and must keep the direction taken until the free zone (turning the shoulder through more than a right angle is a foul); after a foul the umpire sends the chaser the opposite way; a runner is out if touched by hand or leaving the field; one point per runner out. Turn lengths and squad sizes in this text are older than G3.

props.name: Netball Australia, Woolworths NetSetGO (programme page, FAQ and participants page)
props.note: Read. Ages 5-10 in three tiers: Net (5-6), Set (7-8), Go (9-10). Net uses modified goal-post rings and soft-touch balls; Set and Go mix skills with modified match play; 8-10 week programmes. Ring heights and players per side were not stated.

props.name: UK Department for Transport: National Standard for Cycle Training (June 2018), the basis of Bikeability
props.note: Read. Six roles; Bikeability Level 1 (traffic-free), Level 2 (simple roads and junctions) and Level 3 (busier, more complex roads). Outcomes include checking the cycle (tyres, brakes, chain, fit), setting off and stopping smoothly, looking for hazards ahead and behind before setting off, looking behind over each shoulder while pedalling in a straight line, signalling, and primary and secondary road positions. Helmet: fasten correctly if worn; no recommendation either way. No age bands.

props.name: Deutscher Judo Bund youth regulations 2024 (English)
props.note: Read (table partly garbled). Age groups U11, U13, U15, U18/21; contest 2, 3, 3 and 4 min; minimum grades 8th or 7th kyu; mixed-sex contests allowed only at U11 and U13. Age-by-age technique bans could not be mapped reliably from the table.

props.name: Delecluse C, Coeckelberghs T, Vranken R 2001, Effects of the different position of the feet in slalom and freestyle snowboarding on muscle activity of knee extensors
props.note: Read. 3 male instructors; knee extensors worked harder on heel-edge (backside) turns than toe-edge (frontside), especially in the front leg.

props.name: Mufti & Hidayah 2026, Biomechanical analysis of the underhand lay-up from the right and left sides
props.licence: CC BY-NC 4.0 (page also shows CC BY; ambiguous)
props.note: 10 players; take-off, jump and follow-through angles reported without defining the joint. Low value; not used for bands.

props.name: Simões M, Veloso A, Armada-da-Silva P 2006, A kinematic analysis of rowing performance during a 2000 m ergometer test, ISBS 2006 Salzburg
props.note: Read in full. 10 male rowers about 20 years, Concept2 model C, 100 Hz side video. Knee angle at the catch 71 deg at the start, about 43 deg later in the test (180 = straight). Elbows nearly straight at the catch (162-164 deg). Knee catch position explained about 68% of the variation in mean power.

props.name: Scottish Curling, Junior curling and Inclusive curling pages (undated, read 2026-11-06)
props.note: Read. Over 900 juniors affiliated; Future Leaders programme for ages 14-18; 7 wheelchair curling clubs in Scotland; inclusive programmes for wheelchair users, vision impairment, D/deaf, autistic and learning-disabled curlers, with members aged 8 to 80+.

props.name: Malone LA, Gervais P, Baudin P, Steadward RD 1995, Kinematics of free throw shooting by class 1.0 wheelchair basketball players, ISBS 1995
props.note: Read. Class 1.0 players at the 1994 World Championships: release angle about 58 deg, release height 1.56-1.88 m, ball speed about 7.4 m/s; most leaned the trunk back at release; chairs were angled up to 50 deg to the free-throw line.

props.name: World Squash Federation, World Squash Singles Rules 2025 (effective 1 September 2025)
props.note: Read verbatim (copy hosted by the Dutch federation). Games to 11, win by 2 from 10-all; best of 5 (or 3). Serve (5.7): at contact one foot is on the floor inside the service box with no part of that foot touching a box line; the ball goes straight to the front wall between the service line and the out-line and, unless volleyed, bounces in the opposite back quarter without touching a line. The striker must clear after a reasonable follow-through, giving fair view, access, room to swing and freedom to hit (8.1); swings must be reasonable, and excessive swings are dangerous play (8.9-8.10, 14.6.4). Appendix 4: protective eyewear recommended for all players, mandatory in WSF doubles and junior events. Court and ball specifications are in separate WSF documents (not read).

props.name: Li & Pifer 2026, women's penalty kick pose dataset
Bonnechere et al. 2014, What is the safest sprint starting position for American football players? J Sports Sci Med 13(2):423-429
props.licence: CC licence (label and link differ); facts only
props.note: Read in part. 12 players and 13 controls: body speed 12-15% higher from 3- and 4-point starts than 2-point; 4-point start lowers the field of view and raises vertical head speed vs 3-point. Step length and trunk angle tables not read.

props.name: Farana R and colleagues 2019, Sex differences in elbow and wrist joint loading during the cartwheel and round off with different hand positions performed by young gymnasts, J Sports Sci 37(13):1449-1456
props.note: Read (abstract). 16 young gymnasts (8 girls, 8 boys). Girls had higher normalised loads; more elbow bend went with lower loads, so straight-arm targets are not imposed in the cartwheel.

props.name: Poberaj B 2023, Upper extremity injuries in padel, Aspetar Sports Medicine Journal 12 (targeted topic)
props.note: Read. Used for technique only: strokes have preparation, acceleration, impact and follow-through; energy flows from feet and knees through trunk, shoulder, elbow and wrist to the racket; impact point earlier or later changes speed, direction and accuracy; skilled players keep the wrist extended through backhand impact; the serve is hit below hip height after a bounce. Injury content not used.

props.name: Sigalingging WH et al. 2026, Kajian kinematika gerakan servis atas sepak takraw, Pendas 11(2):360-364
props.note: Read. 8 university players, video in Kinovea: at the serve the hip about 112 deg, knee about 136 deg, ankle about 158 deg; leg swing about 8.7 m/s. Abstract inconsistent with the body; low certainty.

props.name: Bataller-Cervero AV et al. 2022, Attack and defense performance in goalball: a proposal for throwing, balance and acoustic reaction evaluation, Biology 11(8):1234
props.note: Read in part (results table; methods not readable; PMC copy blocked). Ball velocity median 50.7 km/h (33-68); simple acoustic reaction about 0.4 s; complex acoustic reaction with a leg response about 0.6-0.7 s.

props.name: Scottish Squash, Eye Protection Policy HS03-P01 v5.0 (16 January 2023)
props.note: Read. Under-19s must wear approved eyewear at sanctioned events, coaching courses and organised activity, including warm-ups; accredited coaches must enforce it. Accepted standards: BS7930-1, ASTM F803, AS/NZS 4066, CSA P400.

props.name: Prvulovic N, Hadzovic M, Lilic A 2022, A biomechanical analysis of the free throw shooting technique in wheelchair basketball: a pilot study, J Anthropol Sport Phys Educ 6(1):3-6
props.note: Read. 3 men (classes 1.0, 3.0, 4.5), one made shot each, 30 fps phone-grade video: release angle 47-52 deg; elbow about 51-65 deg at release and 128-151 deg at the finish. Pilot only; some labels unclear.

props.name: Thomas et al. 2011, Is there a general motor program for right versus left hand throwing in children? J Biosens Bioelectron S1:001
props.note: Read. About 28 children aged 6-10 (half girls), maximal tennis-ball throws, 250 Hz motion capture. Dominant arm: ball speed about 14 m/s; shoulder abduction about 90 deg and elbow bend about 50 deg at release; hip-shoulder separation about 31 deg; stride and trunk flexion predicted ball speed. (Stride lengths in the table look mis-scaled and are not used.)

props.name: World Dodgeball Federation, Foam Rules 2026
props.note: About half read verbatim. Court 18 x 9 m; 6 on court; 6 foam balls (17.8 cm); two 20-minute halves of sets up to 3 minutes; throws overhand, underhand, sidearm or chest push; a 10-second throw clock (in summary). Goggles need head straps; dangerous jewellery removed or taped; gloves banned unless medical; non-marking shoes.

props.name: Climbing Wall Services, Bouldering Supervision Manual (June 2019)
props.note: Read. Descend by down-climbing where possible; a controlled drop lands on the feet about shoulder-width apart with knees bent and arms up; do not put the arms behind you or rotate or keep the feet together. Mats do not make bouldering safe. Do not stand under climbers. Spotting guides a fall, it does not catch. Teach descent before anyone climbs; drill falling at ground level. Suggested maximum ratio 1:9.

props.name: Milanovich M, Nesbit SM 2014, A three-dimensional kinematic and kinetic study of the college-level female softball swing, J Sports Sci Med 13(1):180-191
props.note: Read in part. 14 female college softball players, tee swings: the bat swings in a plane tilted only slightly from level near impact (summary figures, to verify). Softball, not rounders: used only as a guide for a level swing.

props.name: Archery GB, Rules of Shooting (November 2024 issue)
props.note: Parts 1-4 read verbatim. Juniors (under 18) shooting must be supervised by an adult member with a second adult present (103b); at least two adults whenever shooting is in progress. Draw only at the shooting line; no technique that could send an arrow beyond the safety zone (102). Anyone may call FAST to stop shooting. Waiting line at least 5 yards behind the shooting line; spectators at least 10 yards behind outdoors. Junior groups U12, U14, U15, U16, U18, U21; any archer may shoot any outdoor round. Time limits per end by signal method (e.g. 2.5 minutes for 3 arrows).

props.name: Pryhoda & Sabick 2022, Lower body energy generation, absorption and transfer in youth baseball pitchers, Front Sports Act Living 4:975107
props.note: Read. 23 boys aged 9-13 (ball speed 27.1 +/- 3.9 m/s): stride-leg braking force 0.77 BW; trunk peak power 36 W/kg. Kinetic, not kinematic; used for context.

props.name: BWF Laws of Badminton (2025 edition, adopted 26 Apr 2025; the 2026 edition adopted 25 Apr 2026 takes effect 4 Jan 2027), hosted by worldbadminton.com
props.note: Read both editions. Net 1.524 m at centre, 1.55 m at the posts; best of three games. 2025 Laws: games to 21, two-point lead from 20-all, 30th point wins at 29-all. 2026 Laws (from 4 Jan 2027): games to 15, two-point lead from 14-all, 21st point wins at 20-all. Law 9 is the same in both: both feet in contact and stationary until the service is delivered (9.1.4); the racket first hits the base of the shuttle (9.1.5); whole shuttle below 1.15 m at the instant of being hit (9.1.6); racket moves continuously forward (9.1.7). Faults include touching the net (13.4.1) and a double hit (13.3.7).

props.name: St John Fisher RC Primary School, KS2 PE Knowledge Organiser: Rounders (2025)
props.note: Read. Low authority. Hold the bat correctly, take a batting stance, swing and lean in to hit; bowl underarm to a target controlling height, speed and distance. Underarm throw: swing the arm low and back, then forward, releasing at about waist height. Overarm throw: take the ball back behind the body and push the arm forward over the head. Rounders England Talent Squad is for women and girls.

props.name: British Wrestling, Wrestling 4 Her (2024)
props.note: Read. Programme to grow girls' and women's wrestling; a free place for a female candidate on every coaching course since 2019; Commonwealth Games 2022 legacy project; first female-only competition in June 2022.

props.name: Scottish Disability Sport, Para bowls classification (2018)
props.note: Read. Bowlers may deliver from a wheelchair, kneeling, standing or any stance that helps; blind and partially sighted bowlers may be guided by a sighted director.

props.name: Collins K, Reilly T, Malone S, Keane J, Doran D 2022, Science and hurling: a review, Sports 10(8):118
props.note: Read in part. The sliotar can travel at up to 160 km/h; elite players cover about 7.6 km a match; hurling biomechanics is largely unstudied and the review covers men only.

props.name: Canada Soccer Coach's Tool Kit: FUNdamentals
NFHS Baseball Rules 2026 (hosted copy)
props.licence: NFHS copyright; facts only; third-party copy
props.note: Read in part. Balk (2-3-1) is an illegal pitcher act with runners on base; illegal pitch (2-18) without runners. Batting helmets (1-5-1) required for batters, on-deck batters, runners and young bat/ball shaggers, meeting NOCSAE with ear flaps covering both ears. Windup and set position details seen only as a summary.

props.name: Stroke characteristics are associated with sprint-paddling performance in female and male competitive surfers, Sports Biomechanics (2025), doi 10.1080/14763141.2025.2549137
props.note: Abstract read. 31 competitive surfers (15 women), 15 m pool sprints: longer push distance when accelerating and longer pull distance at speed went with faster times; no single variable was significant for women.

props.name: Wagner H, Pfusterschmied J, von Duvillard SP, Muller E 2011, Performance and kinematics of various throwing techniques in team-handball, J Sports Sci Med 10(1):73-80
props.note: Read in part. 14 male elite players. Ball speed ranked: standing throw with run-up (100%), standing throw without run-up (93%), jump throw (92%), pivot throw (85%).

props.name: Castro Figueredo A, Gonzalez Gonzalez L, Castro Figueredo A 2024, El Beisbol 5 como alternativa de adaptacion y formacion deportiva, Lecturas: Educacion Fisica y Deportes 29(319):119-130
props.note: Read. Observational study of 6 teams at a Cuban national championship: Baseball5 suits beginners as an adapted route into baseball; teach technical fundamentals first, then tactics in stages; the sport is under-studied.

props.name: GAA Learning, Go Games
props.note: Read. Go Games are camogie, hurling and Gaelic football for children up to and including 12, where every child plays the whole game in small-sided formats.

props.name: British Fencing, Domestic variations from FIE rules (updated 6 December 2023)
props.note: Read. 350N jackets and breeches at domestic events; 350N plastrons allowed up to U14 with size 3 or smaller blades, 800N otherwise; organisers may lengthen injury breaks to 10 minutes for U15 and below.

props.name: Levanon & Dapena 1998, Comparison of the kinematics of the full-instep and pass kicks, Med Sci Sports Exerc 30(6)
Renaud S 2014, Kinetics and kinematics of the overhand, hybrid and sidearm shot of lacrosse, MSc thesis, University of Ottawa
props.note: Read in part. 12 experienced men about 27 years. Peak trunk rotation speeds about 350-620 deg/s; rotation power differed between shot types. Women excluded because their sticks differ.

props.name: FIBA Mini-Basketball Rules (August 2005)
props.note: Age 12 and under; ball size 5 (ages 9-12) or size 3 (younger); basket 3.05 m at 11-12 and 2.60 m under 11; free-throw line 4.00 m from the backboard; zone defence forbidden.

props.name: Go Paddling (Paddle UK), Stay safe on the water
props.note: Read. Ten tips for new paddlers: buoyancy aid, correct SUP leash, trips within your ability, paddle with others, check weather, tides and water levels, check kit, tell someone, phone on you, food and water, no alcohol. Learn through a Paddle UK delivery partner or club.

props.name: Williams BK, Kuitunen S, Lunge forces and technique of junior squash players (ISBS proceedings)
props.note: Read. 9 male juniors about 15 years (4 experienced, 5 developing); run about 4 m, lunge, ghost shot, push back. Experienced juniors had a lower loading peak after first contact; forehand and backhand lunges did not differ. No angles given.

props.name: Huang C, Hsu G-S, Biomechanical analysis of gymnastic back handspring, ISBS Proceedings (year to confirm)
props.note: Read. 8 gymnasts vs 8 cheerleaders: cheerleaders took off with less knee and hip extension and a longer hand push-off. Used only to describe tumbling, which has no protocol.

props.name: He Y, Liang M, Fang Y, Fekete G, Baker JS, Gu Y 2023, Lumbar and pelvis movement comparison between cross-court and long-line topspin forehand in table tennis, Front Bioeng Biotechnol 11:1185177
props.note: Read. 16 national-level university men, 200 Hz with a musculoskeletal model. Pelvis axial rotation range 76 deg (cross-court) vs 53 deg (long-line); lumbar lateral bend 35 vs 24 deg; cross-court strokes use more weight transfer. Men only.

props.name: Poulet Y, Loisel J, Sauret C 2022, Analyzing intra-cycle velocity profile during wheelchair racing propulsion: a preliminary study, ISBS Proceedings Archive 40(1):138
props.note: Read. 4 men (2 T54, 2 T53): cycle time 0.58-0.60 s; trunk flexion amplitude 3-35 deg; each athlete has a personal velocity profile.

props.name: Concept2, Drills to improve rowing technique
props.note: Read. Arms-and-body rowing, pause drills, counting the rhythm (drive on 1, recover on 2-4), legs-only rowing; suitable for beginners and as a warm-up.

props.name: BUCS, Rounders Rules (British Universities and Colleges Sport)
props.note: Read. Same no-ball and out rules as G1; 6-9 a side; timed innings; the bowler can only change at the start of a new batter.

props.name: AFL, Laws of Australian Football 2026
props.note: About a third read verbatim (to Law 8), rest in summary. Oval ground 135-185 m by 110-155 m; up to 18 players on the ground; ball circumference 720-730 mm. A kick is contact with any part of the leg below the knee; a handball is holding the ball in one hand and hitting it with the clenched fist of the other; throwing (a scooping motion with the hands) is a free kick (18.13). A mark is a catch from a kick of at least 15 m (summary). A legal tackle is below the shoulders and above the knees; shepherds only within 5 m of the ball; no high contact or pushing in the back.

props.name: Chin et al. 2009, The off-break and 'doosra': kinematic variations of elite and sub-elite bowlers, Sports Biomechanics 8:187-198
props.note: Abstract only: elite off-spinners 75.1 vs 67.1 km/h and 26.7 vs 22.2 rev/s; larger elbow extension in elite bowlers; doosra has a longer stride and lower release.

props.name: Meister DW, Ladd AL, Butler EE et al. 2011, Rotational biomechanics of the elite golf swing: benchmarks for amateurs, J Appl Biomech 27:242-251
props.note: Read. 10 male professionals and 5 male amateurs, 5-iron, 240 Hz. Hard swings: peak X-factor (shoulder line vs pelvis) 56 +/- 4 deg; X-factor at impact 33 +/- 6 deg; peak upper-torso rotation 99 +/- 6 deg; peak pelvis rotation 46 +/- 6 deg; clubhead speed 35.4 m/s. X-factor at impact and peak X-factor correlated with clubhead speed within players (rho 0.94 and 0.90); correlation is not causation.

props.name: Martin et al. 2026, Tennis serve biomechanics, joint load mechanics and overuse injuries: a narrative review, Sports Medicine - Open 12:42
props.note: Abstract only: load depends on skill, energy flow, technique, timing, fatigue and racket; mostly male expert samples; the effect of leg drive and backswing style is unclear; stance (foot-up vs foot-back) has no effect.

props.name: R&A / USGA: Anchoring the club, understanding Rule 10.1b (2023)
props.licence: copyright R&A and USGA; facts only
props.note: Read. Bans strokes with the club or a gripping hand held directly against the body, or a forearm held against the body to make an anchor point. Not an equipment rule: long and mid-length putters stay legal if not anchored. Two strokes in stroke play, loss of hole in match play. The diagram's allowed and not-allowed examples could not be mapped from the text.

props.name: Fox AS, Bonacci J, Saunders N 2020, The relationship between performance of a single-leg squat and leap landing task, Sports Biomechanics 19(4):493-509
props.note: Read (abstract). 32 female netballers; less knee bend and more knee drift inward in a single-leg squat went with the same pattern in a netball leap landing. No values in the abstract.

props.name: British Dodgeball, Rules 1.6.2 (17 September 2024)
props.note: A third read verbatim, rest in summary. Court 16 x 9 m; mixed teams with at most 3 of one gender on court; 5-second throw clock (7.8.1.1). Head shots count as hits (12.1.2) but are sanctioned when direct, under about 4 m, at a static or straight-retreating player; face shots generally not valid at U11-U15 (12.2.2). Thrower out on a catch; catcher returns a team-mate; stepping out of court to dodge or catch is out (8.2.3-8.2.4); kicking or spiking the ball is out.

props.name: FIS, 10 Rules for the Conduct of Skiers and Snowboarders (approved 2002, version 2016)
props.note: Read. 1 respect for others; 2 control of speed and movement to suit ability, terrain, snow, weather and traffic; 3 the person behind chooses a route that does not endanger those ahead; 4 overtake with enough space; 5 look up and down before entering, starting or moving upwards; 6 avoid stopping in narrow or blind places and clear the slope after a fall; 7 climb or walk at the side; 8 obey signs; 9 help at accidents; 10 exchange details after an accident.

props.name: ITF Tennis Play and Stay and Tennis10s
props.note: Read. 10-and-under competition uses slower Red (75% slower, court 10.97-12.8 x 4.88-6.1 m), Orange (50% slower, 17.98-18.29 x 6.4-8.3 m) and Green (25% slower, full court) balls. Age bands per stage only from the rules summary (Red to 8, Orange 8-10, Green 9-10).

props.name: Staniszewski M, Zybko P, Wiszomirska I 2016, Evaluation of laterality in the snowboard basic position, Human Movement 17(2):119-125
props.note: Read. 100 snowboarders surveyed, 34 tested. Regular or goofy stance was not linked to hand, foot or eye dominance; front and rear legs did not differ in one-leg balance or strength. Sideways stances were less stable than neutral.

props.name: Bezodis NE, Willwacher S, Salo AIT 2019, The biomechanics of the track and field sprint start: a narrative review, Sports Med 49:1345-1364
props.licence: CC BY 4.0 (from the publisher page summary; not seen in the verbatim text)
props.note: Read in part (Springer page, first half verbatim). Block spacing bunched <0.3 m, medium 0.3-0.5 m, elongated >0.5 m; rear knee about 90 deg in the set position gave higher block velocity than 115 or 135 deg; typical rear knee 114-121 deg; front and rear hip flexion 41/80 deg (fastest) vs 52/89 deg; block-exit step 1.14 m (men) and 1.07 m (women); first stance 0.210 s (men) and 0.225 s (women) in Diamond League sprinters vs 0.176 and 0.166 s in lower-level groups; step rate about 4 Hz after block exit; front leg gives 66-76% of horizontal block impulse.

props.name: NFL UK and BAFA, strategic partnership announcement
props.note: Read (undated). Aim to grow flag in primary and secondary schools, community teams and universities, with a focus on pathways for women and girls; at the time 470 schools and 28,000 players in 26 UK regions (older than G4).

props.name: British Dodgeball, School Regulations (2 September 2024)
props.note: Read. Foam size 1 balls for U11 (3 balls), cloth size 2 for U13 and U15 (5 balls); at least 2 of 6 players female at U11 set starts; sets up to 2 minutes; no dangerous clothing.

props.name: Ringette Canada (Come Try Ringette), Session plan for adult women beginners
props.note: Read. Skating with knees bent and head up; snowplough stops; stationary and circle passing; ready position with two hands spread on the stick; forehand sweep pass (turn sideways, pull the ring back, release in front of the body, follow through to the target); cone shooting; give-and-go; safety: no body contact, sticks below shoulder height.

props.name: British Fencing, Equipment by activity: safety guidelines (updated 2 October 2026)
props.note: Read. Plastic or foam fencing: sleeved top, legs covered to the knee, plastic face mask or regulation mask. Lessons, beginner classes and sparring: 350N jacket, plastron and breeches, mask with back strap, glove; chest protector compulsory for anyone with breasts and recommended for girls from about 10. Never spar in shorts. U10 and U14 sizes allowed with 350N kit; general training needs an 800N plastron; sabre needs an 800N glove.

props.name: USA Ultimate, Intro Skills and Drills Manual v8 (14 February 2020)
props.note: Read. Backhand: fist grip, palm perpendicular to the ground through release, far rim lower than the near rim; rotating the palm turns the disc over. Forehand: two-finger grip, palm up through release, no swinging across the body. Pancake catch is the safest catch, waist to chin. Marker: balls of the feet, knees bent, hips low, feet about shoulder-width, one disc space from the thrower. Pivot foot usually opposite the throwing hand. Drills: warm-up toss, 3-person break-mark, cutting lines, four-line stack.

props.name: Linthorne & Everett 2006, Release angle for attaining maximum distance in the soccer throw-in, Sports Biomech 5(2)
Song Y, Qu Y, Qu F, Zhao S, Zhou Y-L 2018, A biomechanical analysis of the upper limb on different snooker batting techniques, ISBS Proceedings 36
props.note: Read. 8 professional players, follow vs draw shots. Elbow about 120 deg at address, 71-83 deg at the end of the backswing, about 136 deg at the end; hitting speed 2.5 vs 3.7 m/s; cue angle 2.4 vs 4.5 deg; the shoulder stays basically unchanged.

props.name: WPBSA, Cue Zone into Schools development document
props.note: Read. Schools programme launched 2013; UK pilot in 20 schools plus 15 in Sheffield (3 for disabled pupils), potential reach about 48,800 pupils; 'Functional Snooker' links the game to maths and English. No technique content.

props.name: Hanks M 2018, The effect of stride foot contact orientation on overhand shot kinematics, kinetics and performance outcomes in male lacrosse players, PhD dissertation, Auburn University
props.note: Read (abstract). 15 male players about 17 years. A closed stride-foot orientation gave greater pelvis, trunk and arm angular velocities than in-line or open; ball speed tracked these rotations; aiming for accuracy cost speed.

props.name: Swim England (ASA) Wavepower photography and filming guidance (Wavepower 2016-19 extract)
props.note: Read. Publishing images of under-18s needs parental consent, preferably written; filming children in training is not recommended and, if justified, needs written parental consent and the footage destroyed once used; poolside shots of children in costume should be above the waist only; no photos from behind the blocks or of children climbing out; no cameras or camera phones in changing rooms. The edition is old; check the current Wavepower.

props.name: Bourgain M, Rouch P, Rouillon O, Thoreux P, Sauret C 2022, Golf swing biomechanics: a systematic review and methodological recommendations for kinematics, Sports 10(6):91
props.note: Read in part (92 studies). Phases address, backswing, downswing, follow-through; top of backswing = when clubhead travel turns downward and forward; impact = clubhead meets ball. X-factor about 30 deg (torso vs pelvis) or about 60 deg (shoulder line vs pelvis); downswing lasts about 0.3 s. Values from the unread half (kinematic sequence, knee angles) are not used.

props.name: Wikipedia, Kabaddi
props.note: Read in part. Sub-junior (under 16) court 11 x 8 m; pulling hair or clothing invalidates a tackle; covering the mouth or choking is a foul; IKF founded 2004; Pro Kabaddi League from 2014. Some details conflict with G1 (do-or-die after two vs three empty raids).

props.name: Ladru BJ, Langhout R, Veeger HEJ, Gijssel M, Tak M 2019, Lead knee extension contributes to drag-flick performance in field hockey, Int J Perform Anal Sport 19(4):556-566
props.note: Read (record). 19 elite players, 240 Hz. Lead knee extension velocity was positively associated with ball speed (R2 = 0.13).

props.name: CEC (UGC), B.P.Ed module: Kabaddi
props.note: Read. Fouls include shutting the raider's mouth or throat and violent tackling; green, yellow and red cards; a raid must start within a set time.

props.name: International Wheelchair Basketball Federation, Official Wheelchair Basketball Rules 2024 (valid from 1 November 2024)
props.note: Read in part (Art. 1-29 and parts of 31 onward verbatim; rest in summary). Court 28 x 15 m; five players a side within a 14-point limit; four 10-minute quarters; 24-second clock. Travelling: no more than two pushes while holding the ball (25.1.1); braking is not a push. Dribble: one or two pushes with the ball on the lap, then a dribble (24.1.3). Tipping so that a part other than wheels or castors touches the floor is a violation (14.1.4.2). In summary: lifting off the seat for an advantage (31.1.1) and using a lower limb to steer or brake (36.2.1) are technical fouls. Chair: seat height at most 63 cm (classes 1.0-3.0) or 58 cm (3.5-4.5); anti-tip castors; no brakes or gears; hard braces and helmets banned.

props.name: ISU Special Regulations and Technical Rules, Single and Pair Skating and Ice Dance (2018 edition; copy hosted by Swiss Ice Skating)
props.note: About a third read verbatim; an old edition. Rink 56 x 26 m up to 60 x 30 m; fall deductions (seniors -1 for the first and second fall, rising; juniors -1 per fall); costume and timing deductions. Jump, spin, under-rotation and current age rules were not in the part read.

props.name: Wu Y, Wang H, Deng C, Guo Y, Zhu X 2024, Cushioning mechanism of the metatarsals during landing for the skateboarding ollie maneuver, Front Bioeng Biotechnol 12:1382161
props.note: Read in part. One male skater, 10 ollies averaging 33.7 +/- 4.2 cm jump height; flat-ground landing about 1.7 x body weight.

props.name: Rounders England, Simplified Rules (school copy)
props.note: Read. 6-15 in a team, at most 9 fielding. No-ball if the action is not underarm, the ball passes above the head or below the knee, is wide or straight at the body, bounces, or the bowler's foot leaves the bowling square during the action; half a rounder for two consecutive no-balls to one batter. Batter is out if caught, if a foot goes over the front or back line of the batting square before striking at a good ball, for running inside a post, overtaking or obstruction, or for losing contact with a post while the bowler holds the ball in the square. Full rounder for hitting and reaching 4th post; half rounder for reaching 4th without hitting or 2nd after hitting; backward hits allowed.

props.name: O'Riordan A, Greenhalgh A, Frossard L, Miller S 2017, Biomechanics of seated shot put (conference slides, UK Paralympic Performance Conference)
props.note: Read (text only). Two single-athlete pilots (F55, F34): seat orientation and pole position changed distance and movement pattern (F34: 6.23-6.93 m, SD 0.17-0.28 m); set-up should be individualised. Frame height 75 cm.

props.name: Cricket Australia Community Cricket Junior Pace Bowling Workload Guidelines (2026)
props.note: Read. Under 17: '1, 3, 5' (rest day after a bowling day, max 3 sessions a week, max 5 overs a spell). 17-19: '2, 4, 6'. Match limits by age, e.g. under 11 2 overs a spell and 4 a day.

props.name: Walsh M, Creekmur C, Wojcik J 2006, Force time measures of beginning and skilled skateboarders performing an ollie, ISBS 2006
props.note: Read. 1 skilled skater and 5 beginners. Skilled and trained skaters showed a quick countermovement before the pop; untrained beginners crouched gradually and paused. Landing forces exceeded take-off forces in everyone.

props.name: Sheppard JM, Osborne M, Chapman DW, Andrews M, McNamara P 2013, Technique adjustments influence the performance of sprint paddling in competitive male surfers, Int J Sports Sci Coach 8(1):43-52
props.note: Abstract read. 20 competitive male surfers, 15 m sprint paddles: chest down (low to the board, without much back extension) and a low arm recovery were faster; long or short reach made no difference.

props.name: Kapas and Paul 2022, Change of performance characteristics in different age group of kho kho players (Zenodo)
props.note: Abstract read. 45 girls in three age groups compared on speed, agility and speed endurance; tests not named in the abstract; low to moderate quality.

props.name: Kuch A, Tisserand R, Durand F, Monnet T, Debril J-F 2024, Postural adjustments preceding string release in trained archers, arXiv:2402.12389
props.note: Read in full. 6 elite and 7 sub-elite recurve archers at 70 m, 1000 fps video and force plates. Clicker-to-release 146 ms (elite) vs 156 ms; front-back sway while aiming 2.7 vs 3.6 mm; elite archers more often released early after the clicker.

props.name: Barzykina 2017, The physics of an optimal basketball free throw (arXiv preprint)
props.note: Model: successful angles about 47-57.5 deg at 7.59 m/s; NBA tracking averages about 53-55 deg. Preprint; simulation-based.

props.name: Frederick EC, Determan JJ, Whittlesey SN, Hamill J 2006, Biomechanics of skateboarding: kinetics of the Ollie, J Appl Biomech 22(1):33-40
props.note: Read (abstract). 7 top amateur or professional skaters. Ollie-up take-off peak about 2.2 x body weight; ollie-down landing from 46 cm about 4.7 x body weight within 30-80 ms. The take-off is driven by rapidly rotating the tail into the ground.

props.name: Orth D 2016, Movement pattern and coordination in climbing, PhD thesis (partly read)
props.note: Read in part (chapters 1-2). Uses hip-to-wall angle, jerk, a geometric entropy index of the hip path and an immobility ratio to describe skilled climbing. Values not read.

props.name: Estevan I, Falco C, Freedman Silvernail J, Jandacka D 2015, Comparison of lower limb segments kinematics in a taekwondo kick: an approach to the proximal to distal motion, J Hum Kinet 47:41-49
props.note: Read. 10 black belts (5 men, 5 women), roundhouse kick to sternum height. Peak speed thigh 4.0, shank 7.0, foot 11.9 m/s, reached at 0.60, 0.62 and 0.71 s: a proximal-to-distal sequence.

props.name: Ram J, Singh J 2021, Relationship of selected anthropometric and linear kinematical variables with the performance of toe-touch skill in kabaddi, Physical Education Theory and Methodology 21(4):304-309
props.note: Read. Same 100 raiders: toe touch took about 0.43 s; feet about 86 cm apart; a wider stride and a lower centre of gravity went with better ratings.

props.name: Breaking GB, WDSF Breaking Judges Congress (news, April 2022)
props.note: Read. Breaking GB works through DanceSport England; the three-criteria system is recommended nationally; judges must be over 21.

props.name: Association of British Climbing Walls, New ABC safeguarding guidelines published (21 June 2024)
props.note: Read (announcement). Operational Guidelines Part 3: Safeguarding, developed with the BMC, Mountaineering Ireland and Mountaineering Scotland, informed by the NSPCC. The guidelines themselves are a member download (not read).

props.name: Crum B, Korfball Advisor: the long shot or distance shot (blog, 24 April 2023)
props.note: Read. Coaching opinion drawing on the IKF coaching guide: distance shots from about 7-10 m; feet set for balance (or a step back onto one leg); force flows from the feet up; a 45 deg release is often argued, with good arcs about 25-45 deg; a still head and eyes; key scorers convert about 30% of shots.

props.name: Chen et al. 2024, Kinematic differences between female national and provincial athletes in the tennis serve, PeerJ 12:e18410
props.note: 10 women (5 national, 5 provincial), foot-up serves: first-serve ball speed about 143-145 km/h; ball height at impact about 2.61 m for players about 1.70 m tall (about 1.53 x height); minimum front-knee angle about 114-115 deg.

props.name: Canada Basketball long-term development and NCCP coaching pathway
props.note: Age bands: FUNdamentals 6-9, Learn to Train 8-12, Train to Train 12-16, Train to Compete 15-22. Skill and drill material is behind paid membership; not read.

props.name: Ibrahim et al. 2019/2020, goalkeeper set position and diving, Front Sports Act Living
Jacquot R, Ben Mansour K, Bouillet K, Jehl J-P, Gauchard G 2025, A multi-parameter investigation of elite archery: aiming and follow-through phases, Front Sports Act Living 7:1650300
props.note: Read in part. 8 elite French recurve archers (4 women, 4 men) at 70 m. Aiming lasted about 1.6-3.7 s per arrow by archer and score. Cites earlier work: elite archers held the bow shoulder at about 99 deg of abduction against 107 deg in novices.

props.name: International Powerlifting Federation, Technical Rulebook (effective 1 March 2026; copy hosted by the Irish Powerlifting Federation)
props.note: Read. Squat (4.1): lower until the top surface of the legs at the hip joint is below the top of the knees; one descent; no double bounce or downward movement on the way up; knees locked at the start and finish; no foot movement. Bench (4.2): head, shoulders and buttocks on the bench, feet flat; bar to chest or abdomen, elbows at or below shoulder level; pause, press to locked elbows. Deadlift (4.3): finish erect with knees locked and shoulders back; no downward bar movement before the finish; no supporting the bar on the thighs. Ages (1.1): sub-junior 14-18, junior 19-23; under-14s only at national competitions.

props.name: Disability Bowls England, Introduction to classification in bowls
props.note: Read; undated. B1-B4 vision, B5-B8 physical, L1-L3 learning disability; functional, not by diagnosis; classes mix ambulant and wheelchair bowlers; required for national and international events including the Commonwealth Games.

props.name: Hedbávný P, Hupka D, Sklenaříková J 2013, Analysis of balanced handstands, Studia sportiva 7(1):51-62
props.licence: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0; facts only, no adaptation
props.note: Read in full (Czech). One 12-year-old competitive gymnast, 3D at 100 Hz plus force plate and EMG over a 10 s hold. Hip angle median 171 deg (157-175); trunk-arm (shoulder) angle median 157 deg (149-162). More sway front-to-back than side-to-side; shoulder movement dominated hip movement.

props.name: Honnorat et al. 2025, The influence of age categories on performance parameters during on-court testing in wheelchair basketball players, Front Sports Act Living 7:1576949
props.note: Read. 22 national-level men (juniors and seniors), 20 m sprints with wheel sensors: juniors 5.7 s vs seniors 5.3 s; juniors slower over the first pushes and tired more.

props.name: Marino GW, Biomechanics of power skating: past research, future trends (ISBS proceedings)
props.note: Read. Review. At full speed a stride is about 75-85% single support and 15-25% double support; highly skilled skaters reach 9-10 m/s; positive acceleration lasts at least the first 1.75 s (about 6 m).

props.name: England Squash, Equipment
props.note: Read. Eyewear mandatory for under-19s in any competition and for all ages in doubles. Balls: Pro (double yellow dot), Competition (single yellow dot), Progress (larger, bouncier, black), Max (larger and bouncier, blue dot) for beginners. Squash 57 uses a large-head racket; blue balls for beginners, black for experienced players.

props.name: Bordelon et al. 2022, Peak elbow flexion does not influence peak shoulder distraction force or ball velocity in NCAA Division I softball pitchers, Orthop J Sports Med 10(1)
props.note: Read. 61 female D1 pitchers: peak elbow flexion in acceleration 41.2 +/- 17.8 deg; ball speed 24.6 +/- 1.3 m/s; elbow flexion not related to speed or shoulder distraction force.

props.name: World DanceSport Federation, Breaking Rules and Regulations Manual (Version 4, January 2023)
props.note: Read in part (weights and penalties verbatim). 1v1 battles in rounds, up to 60 s per set; crew battles. Ages: Adult 19+, Youth 16-18, Junior I and II 13-15. Elements: toprock, downrock (footwork, spins, power moves), freezes, transitions, drops. Trivium judging: technique, variety, performance, musicality, creativity, personality. Penalties for crashes, copying and repeats; no physical contact with the opponent; b-girl and b-boy categories.

props.name: Robbins SM, Renaud PJ, MacInnis N, Pearsall DJ 2021, The relationship between trunk rotation and shot speed when performing ice hockey wrist shots, J Sports Sci 39(9):1001-1009
props.note: Reused from sport 11. 20 men: greater trunk rotation away from the target went with faster wrist shots. Ice hockey, used as the closest stick-shot evidence.

props.name: Falloon J, Ball K, MacMahon C, Taylor S 2010, Coordination patterns of preferred and non-preferred kicking of the drop punt kick, ISBS 2010
props.note: Read. 8 elite men: foot speed about 19.1 vs 17.2 m/s and knee angular velocity higher on the preferred leg.

props.name: Olympics.com, Surfing explained: how the new Olympic sport is judged (before Tokyo 2020)
props.note: Read. Five criteria: commitment and degree of difficulty; innovative and progressive manoeuvres; variety; combination of major manoeuvres; speed, power and flow. Five judges score each wave 1-10 to two decimals, dropping highest and lowest; the best two waves count; heats 20-35 minutes.

props.name: World Ringette Federation, Ringette in a nutshell (tournament rules summary)
props.note: Read. A single pass across both blue lines (two-line violation) gives the ring to the opponent; entering the goal crease starts a five-second count; the shot clock resets on a shot that hits the goalie or frame; played in Finland since 1979; World Championships every other year.

props.name: Bhat, Dachen and Hajam 2018, Comparative analysis of selected physical variables among college men kabaddi and kho-kho players, Int J Physiol Nutr Phys Educ 3(2):2266-2270
props.note: Read. 15 university kho kho players: 50 m dash about 6.16 s; shuttle run about 10.25 s. Small sample, a table-text inconsistency; low to moderate quality.

props.name: Mullineaux & Uhl 2009, free-throw release conditions in collegiate players (ISB 2009)
props.note: Reused from sport 02 (basketball). 5 women and 10 men: swish release angle about 50 deg, release height about 2.4 m. Basketball set shot, used only as the nearest evidence for a two-handed set shot at a high target.

props.name: Netball Australia, Coaching the KNEE Program: coaching manual
props.licence: Netball Australia; facts only (no licence stated)
props.note: Read. Warm-up programme in Junior (10-14), Recreational (14+) and Elite versions, 2-3 times a week. Good take-off: feet about shoulder-width, facing forward, hips and knees bent, knees in line with feet, arms drive. Good landing: hips and knees bent, roll through the feet, feet straight, knees in line with feet, trunk stable. Deceleration: several small steps, chest up. External cue: sit back as if into a chair. The manual makes injury-reduction claims; we do not repeat them.

props.name: Garcia-Gimenez A, Pradas de la Fuente F, Castellar Otin C, Carrasco Paez L 2022, Performance outcome measures in padel: a scoping review, Int J Environ Res Public Health 19(7):4395
props.note: Read in part. Rallies about 12.7 s with 15 s rest in high-level play; work-to-rest 0.84; very few biomechanics studies (two found); in one, hand height and heel position related to shot direction. No stroke angles or racket speeds.

props.name: England Football: passing techniques and how to coach shooting
England Netball, Bee Netball
props.note: Read. Bee Netball is England Netball's programme for children aged 5-11, introducing throwing, catching, footwork and shooting. Stage names and per-stage rules were not on the page.

props.name: ISTAF, Law of the Game: Regu and Team event (2013 amendment; Sepak Takraw Federation of India copy)
props.note: Read. Court 13.4 x 6.1 m; service circle radius 0.3 m; net 1.52 m (men) and 1.42 m (women) at the centre. Ball synthetic, 12 holes. Regu of three: Tekong (server), Left and Right Inside. Service: the Tekong's non-kicking foot stays in the circle until the kick (lifting it or stepping out is a fault, 11.1.3); an Inside player throws the ball as soon as the score is called and must not lift a foot or step on lines during the throw (11.1.2); the serve must cross the net and land in court. Play: at most three touches a side; faults for the ball touching the arm (11.3.4), touching the net or post (11.3.6) or entering the opponent's court except on a follow-through (11.3.2). Sets to 21 (up to 25), best of three. Rubber-soled shoes.

props.name: Sport and Recreation Alliance, Spotlight on the England Kabaddi Federation (14 August 2025)
