props.note: Read. England Kabaddi Federation UK is the national governing body. England's men's and women's teams were runners-up at the 2025 Kabaddi World Cup in the West Midlands, the first held in the UK. National style (7 a side) and circle style (12 a side); raids now limited to 30 seconds.

props.name: Jia M, Liu L, Huang R et al. 2024, Correlation analysis between biomechanical characteristics of taekwondo double roundhouse kick and effective scoring of electronic body protector, Front Physiol 14:1269345
props.note: Read in part. 12 male athletes, DAEDO electronic protector. Peak hip-flexion angular velocity of the kicking leg correlated with effective scoring (r = 0.74); foot speed and ankle action predicted score (R2 = 0.87).

props.name: IIHF Rule Book 2026-27, Art. 101 Women's hockey specific playing rules (test subdomain)
props.note: Read. In women's hockey, body checking is allowed when there is a clear intention of playing the puck or gaining possession; otherwise minor, or major plus game misconduct. Same test-subdomain caveat.

props.name: IIHF Rule Book 2026-27, Art. 48 Illegal check to the head or neck (rulebook.iihf.com, test subdomain)
props.note: Read. 'There is no clean check to the head or neck.' Minor penalty at the referee's discretion; major and game misconduct if the player recklessly endangers the opponent; supplementary discipline possible. The page is on a test subdomain; confirm against the published rule book.

props.name: The FIFA 11+ program is effective in preventing injuries in elite male basketball players: a cluster randomized controlled trial, Am J Sports Med 2012
props.note: 121 youth players (mean age 13.5-15.2): overall injuries 0.95 vs 2.16 per 1000 exposures with the warm-up. Author list and DOI not confirmed from the page (commonly cited as Longo et al.).

props.name: Zhang BM, Chu DPK, Hong Y, Biomechanical analysis of the lunge technique in the elite female fencers, ISBS proceedings
props.note: Read. 4 elite women epee fencers; rear knee about 175-177 deg at full extension; time to target about 0.54-0.70 s; centre of mass and blade moved together. Some table units unclear.

props.name: Paddle Scotland, Safety advice
props.note: Read. Wear a fitted buoyancy aid whatever your swimming ability, including on a paddleboard; choose the correct leash for the environment; phone in a waterproof pouch on your person; 999 and ask for the Coastguard on tidal water; avoid offshore winds; take courses before moving water.

props.name: Stuelcken, Portus & Mason 2005, Off-side front foot drives in men's high performance cricket, Sports Biomechanics 4(1):17-35
props.note: Abstract only: 9 international batsmen; front stride and downswing delayed; front foot placed only just before impact; front ankle inside the line of the ball at impact.

props.name: Cheraghi M, Agha Alinejad H, Arshi AR, Shirzad E 2014, Kinematics of straight right punch in boxing, Ann Appl Sport Sci 2(2):39-50
props.note: Read. 8 elite male amateur boxers, 250 Hz. Rear straight: fist speed 7.8 m/s; punch duration 0.31 +/- 0.06 s; hip moves 0.28 m forward; elbow at impact 137 +/- 12 deg (max 143 deg); knee at impact 165 deg; ankle, knee and elbow extension start at about 45%, 60% and 80% of the punch.

props.name: Parkour UK, Level 1 coach qualification (undated)
props.note: Read. One-day course after online modules on coaching fundamentals, safeguarding and first aid; syllabus of jumps, balances, vaults, wall moves and underbars; coaches under 18 assist a qualified coach; aimed at teachers, volunteers, younger coaches and parent helpers.

props.name: Biomechanics of increased spin velocity of flying discs during forehand throws by skilled and unskilled throwers (abstract record)
props.note: Read (abstract; full citation not shown). 10 skilled and 11 unskilled throwers; throw distance tracked disc spin in both groups (r = 0.72-0.79); skilled throwers raised spin through joint torque.

props.name: Rolley T et al. 2023, Anticipatory effects on side-step cutting biomechanics in Women's Australian Football League players, BMJ Open Sport Exerc Med 9(2):e001587
props.note: Read. 16 elite women, 35-55 deg side-steps: approach about 5.4 m/s (planned) vs 5.1 m/s (reacting to a cue); plant-foot contact about 210 vs 233 ms; reacting players braked less and slowed down.

props.name: Cust EE, Ball K, Sweeting AJ, Robertson S 2019, Biomechanical characteristics of elite female Australian rules football preferred and non-preferred drop punt kicks, icSPORTS 2019 pp. 32-37
props.note: Read. 15 elite women, 100 Hz motion capture. Preferred vs non-preferred: foot speed about 18.9 vs 16.2 m/s, ball speed 24.7 vs 21.6 m/s, ball-to-foot speed ratio about 1.3; kicking knee bent about 51 vs 58 deg at contact; support knee bent about 37 vs 41 deg. Cites men's foot speed about 26.5 m/s and men's support-knee bend about 41-43 deg.

props.name: Schiffman J, Zebas C 1997, Kinematic analysis of an elite level fencer, ISBS 1997
props.note: Read (abstract). One international sabre fencer: average lunge 1.24 m; trunk tilted forward about 17 deg; hips moved only about 3 cm up and down during footwork before the lunge.

props.name: Support-foot placement and instep kick, Sci Med Football 2023 7(1)
props.note: numbers not yet read

props.name: World Rowing, Rules of Racing 2025 (Quadrennial Congress redline, 13 January 2025)
props.note: About a third read verbatim (a 2024-vs-2025 redline). Rowing on a machine counts as rowing (Rule 1); coastal, beach sprint and indoor rowing have separate rule books (Rule 2); Under 19 and Under 23 championships exist and categories have eligibility rules (Rules 3, 12). Safety is of paramount concern; rowers at championship regattas must be able to swim 50 m and stay afloat unaided for 3 minutes (Bye-Law to Rule 15). Boat classes (1x, 2x, 2-, 2+, 4x, 4-, 4+, 8+) seen only in a summary. Lightweight categories exist; their limits were not read.

props.name: NFHS: High school football rules changes continue focus on risk minimization (2015)
props.note: Read. Targeting defined as contact to an opponent above the shoulders; spearing is initiating contact with the crown (top) of the helmet; unnecessary or excessive contact with a defenceless player is illegal. A 2015 article, not the current rulebook.

props.name: World Darts Federation, International Youth Challenge Format and Playing Rules (2nd edition, 22 February 2025)
props.note: Read (dartboard and scoring sections missing from the fetch). Age groups U18 and U23; U18 singles split into boys and girls when more than four girls enter. No alcohol for any player, with random tests; no alcohol, tobacco or gambling advertising; enclosed footwear; no earphones.

props.name: Kellis & Katis 2007, Biomechanical characteristics and determinants of instep soccer kick, J Sports Sci Med 6(2)
IKF, The Rules of Korfball 2024: changes and explanation
props.note: Read. Free-pass preparation at most 4 seconds; yellow card is 4 minutes off; watch for contact fouls around the post.

props.name: World Athletics: Competition and Technical Rules applicable to in-competition warnings and disqualifications (2022 edition, hosted by UK Athletics)
props.note: Read. Code list only: TR16.8 false start; TR16.5 aborting, delaying or disturbing the start; TR17.3.1 and TR17.4 lane infringement; TR22.6 hurdles; TR24.7 baton passed outside the takeover zone; TR24.19 starting outside the zone; TR24.8 impeding at the takeover. No numeric thresholds and no jump or throw foul wording.

props.name: Yamashita D, Arakawa H, Wada T, Yumoto K, Fujiyama K, Nagami T, Shimizu S 2020, Whole-body mechanics of double-leg attack in elite and non-elite male freestyle wrestlers, Front Sports Act Living 2:58
props.note: Read (results in summary). 11 international and 9 college wrestlers attacking a still partner, motion capture: attack took about 0.43-0.47 s from the level change to contact; the centre of mass dropped about 0.17 m (international) against 0.24 m (college) from about 0.72 m; the upper body travelled about 0.42 m forward, and international wrestlers moved it forward earlier and pushed harder off the trailing foot. Staggered crouch stance.

props.name: Mazurkiewicz A, Iwańska D, Urbanik C 2018, Biomechanics of the Axel Paulsen figure skating jump, Polish Journal of Sport and Tourism 25(2):3-9
props.note: Read (abstract). One elite junior man; the single Axel was over 19% lower than the double and triple; the ankle bend before take-off mattered most for rotation.

props.name: World Skate, Skateboarding Street and Park Competition Rules (updated April 2025)
props.note: About 60% read verbatim. Park: 2-4 runs of 30-50 s; street: 45-60 s runs plus single-trick attempts; five judges score 0-100, highest and lowest dropped. Minimum age for World Skateboarding Tour events by birth year: 11 in 2025, 12 in 2026, 13 in 2027, 14 from 2028. Helmets compulsory for street athletes under 18 and for all park athletes, in practice and competition. The judging criteria list was not in the part read.

props.name: Wikipedia, 2025 Kho Kho World Cup
props.note: Read. First World Cup, 13-19 January 2025, Indira Gandhi Arena, New Delhi; 23 countries (20 men's and 19 women's teams); India won both titles, Nepal runners-up in both.

props.name: Rusdiana A 2021, 3D kinematics analysis of overhead backhand and forehand smash techniques in badminton, Ann Appl Sport Sci 9(3):e1002
props.licence: no licence statement seen; facts only
props.note: Read. 24 male university players. Forehand smash: shuttle 158 km/h; shoulder external rotation 169 deg in the cocking phase; elbow flexion 102 deg; peak shoulder internal rotation velocity 2111 deg/s; elbow extension velocity 995 deg/s. The paper's text and table disagree on forearm supination.

props.name: USA Pickleball: Rules summary (Rev. 1/1/2025); the Official Rulebook prevails
props.note: Read. Volley serve: arm moving in an upward arc at contact; contact not above waist level; paddle head not above the highest part of the wrist. A drop serve is allowed, and then those elements do not apply. At least one foot behind the baseline; feet not on the court or outside the sideline or centreline extensions; serve diagonally crosscourt; one serve attempt. Two-bounce rule: the serve and the return must each bounce before being played. Non-volley zone: the area within 7 feet of the net on both sides; no volleying while in it, and a fault if momentum after a volley carries the player into it or onto its line; players may be in the zone at other times. A serve touching the non-volley-zone line is short. Games to 11, win by 2. Court and net dimensions not on the page.

props.name: England Touch, signs up as an Association for Physical Education NGB affiliate (4 September 2025)
props.note: Read. Touch joining PE teachers' association to reach schools; schools tournaments grew from 8 teams (2022) to over 100 (2025); a record 450 juniors at the 2025 Junior Nationals.

props.name: Zorko M, Nemec B, Matjačić Z, Olenšek A, Tomazin K, Supej M 2020, Wide skis as a potential knee injury risk factor in alpine skiing, Front Sports Act Living 2:7
props.note: Read in part. 14 intermediate skiers (8 men, 6 women) on a ski-turn simulator at 25 deg inclination and 40 or 60 deg knee flexion. Used only as context for typical turn postures; we make no injury claims.

props.name: Ladies Gaelic Football Association, Playing Rules 2024
props.note: Read. 15 a side; size 4 ball from U13 (Go Games ball below). Handpass with the fist or open hand and a visible striking action; no throwing. Carry for up to 4 steps and play the ball on the 5th; one hop after a catch, or solo toe to hand. Pick-up from standing with the toe or hands. No deliberate bodily contact and no shouldering. Go Games U7-U12, then U14, U16, U18.

props.name: CEC (UGC), B.P.Ed Paper 2, Lecture 29: Kho-Kho I
props.note: Read (text partly garbled). Posts 120-125 cm high; central and cross lanes 30 cm wide; squares 30 x 30 cm. A kho is given by touching the chaser from behind by hand and calling 'KHO' loudly; calling before touching is a foul. The active chaser takes a direction by crossing a cross lane or turning the shoulder line towards a post.

props.name: British Weight Lifting, Guidance for coaches (young people)
props.note: Read. Ratios 1:8 for under-8s and 1:12 for over-8s; never coach alone; a Level 2 BWL coach leads sessions; safeguarding training, first aid and parental consent required; programmes suited to age, maturity, experience and ability.

props.name: Wikipedia, Camogie
props.note: Read. Over 100,000 registered players and about 536 clubs (page flagged as needing an update); first played 1904.

props.name: Green A et al. 2016, Rugby ground pass accuracy and pelvic orientation, S Afr J Sports Med 28(2):51-54
props.note: Reused from sport 13. 16 players: turning the pelvis towards the target made passes far more accurate.

props.name: World Pool-Billiard Association, Recommended Equipment Specifications (2001)
props.note: Read in full. 9-ft table playing surface 100 x 50 in, 8-ft 92 x 46 in; table height 29.25-31 in; balls 2.25 in (57.15 mm); cue at least 40 in, at most 25 oz, tip at most 14 mm.

props.name: Zahradnik D, Jandacka D, Farana R, Uchytil J, Hamill J 2015, Landing patterns after block in volleyball (33rd ISBS Conference, Poitiers)
props.note: Read. 19 elite women, 247 Hz motion capture. Four landing patterns; knee frontal-plane angle at initial contact about 1 deg varus to 5 deg valgus, and at 30 deg knee flexion 5 deg varus to 4 deg valgus. Used to define the knee-alignment fault wording only, never to predict injury.

props.name: World Boxing Competition Rules (in force February 2024, v3.9), hosted by the Norwegian Boxing Federation
props.note: Read verbatim to rule 2.5.2. Age by calendar year of birth: Elite 19-40, U19 17-18, U17 15-16, U15 13-14 (regulated by confederations and national federations), Masters over 40. Three rounds of 3 min (Elite, U19) or 2 min (U17), 1 min rest. Seen only in a machine summary: headguards for U17, U19 and elite women but not elite men; 10 or 12 oz gloves; a scoring blow lands with the knuckle part of the glove; fouls include low blows, hitting the back of the head or neck, holding and butting.

props.name: Athletics Ontario: Common rules for umpires in reporting infractions (IAAF Competition and Technical Rules 2020 edition, June 2021)
props.note: Read (OCR-like text). TR24.3: 4x100 m, 4x200 m and the first two medley changes use a 30 m takeover zone; 4x400 m and longer use 20 m. TR24.7: the baton must be passed within the zone; the pass starts when the receiver first touches it and ends when only the receiver holds it. TR17.3: stay in the allocated lane in lane races; do not step on or inside the kerb on bends in non-lane races; no DQ if pushed out or no material advantage. TR16.7-8: DQ after the first false start. The 0.100 s reaction-time limit is not in this document.

props.name: Koh M, Hin T, Sujae IH 2006, 3D kinematic analysis of the kuda and sila service technique in sepak takraw, ISBS Proceedings 24:807-810
props.note: Read. 9 experienced male players, 240 Hz motion capture: ball speed after contact about 22.8 (instep 'kuda') and 17.6 (inside-foot 'sila') m/s; sila contact in front of and above the head on the inside of the foot; kuda used more hip flexion and abduction.

props.name: Parrington L, Ball K, MacMahon C, Taylor S 2009, Biomechanical analysis of the handball in Australian football, ISBS 2009
props.note: Read. 1 elite man. Fist speed at contact about 9.4-10.4 m/s; a step of about 0.9-1.1 m towards the target, longer for maximal passes; the non-preferred hand kept the elbow almost fixed and used more shoulder movement.

props.name: Mini-basketball rules 2023 (Luxembourg federation)
props.note: National variation: U12 4v4 with a 2.80 m basket, U10 3v3 with 2.60 m, size 5 ball, man-to-man defence only. Shows youth equipment differs by country.

props.name: List R, Bründler J, Lorenzetti S 2012, Influence of stance width and binding angles on tibial rotation and ollie jump height in snowboarding, ISBS 2012
props.note: Read. 10 expert freestyle snowboarders (2 women). Stance widths around shank length and two binding set-ups changed knee twisting patterns but not ollie height. No knee-angle values.

props.name: Iino Y, Kojima T 2008, Kinematics of table tennis topspin forehands: effects of performance level and ball spin (ISBS Conference, Seoul)
props.note: Read. 9 advanced and 8 intermediate collegiate men, 200 fps. Racket speed at impact 19.4-19.6 m/s (advanced) vs 17.9-18.4 m/s (intermediate, not significant); advanced players got more racket speed from lower-trunk rotation and reached a later, sharper racket acceleration (about 0.1 s before impact).

props.name: McGuine & Keene 2006, The effect of a balance training program on the risk of ankle sprains in high school athletes, Am J Sports Med 34(7):1103-1111
props.note: 765 soccer and basketball players (523 girls): ankle sprain rate 1.13 vs 1.87 per 1000 exposures with balance training.

props.name: Worthington, King & Ranson 2013, Relationships between fast bowling technique and ball release speed in cricket, J Appl Biomech
props.note: Cited by the curated pace protocol (front-knee extension through front-foot contact and trunk flexion relate to release speed). Not re-read on 2026-11-05.

props.name: Endo S, Miyanishi T, A biomechanical analysis of competitive and recreational players in relation to the darts throwing technique, ISBS Proceedings pp. 429-432 (year to confirm)
props.note: Read. 9 men (4 competitive, 5 recreational). Competitive players moved the shoulder and elbow about four times less and the body forward-back only about 5 mm (vs 30 mm) in the 0.7 s before release; landing error about 29 vs 81 mm. Competitive players started with more weight on the front leg.

props.name: Gholipour M, Tabrizi A, Farahmand F 2008, Kinematics analysis of lunge fencing using stereophotogrammetry, World J Sport Sci 1(1):32-37
props.note: Read (abstract). 8 male foil fencers, elite and novice. Elite lunges longer (1.17 vs 1.02 m); elite started with less knee bend and extended more.

props.name: Lazzeri M, Kayser BE, Armand S 2016, Kinematic predictors of wrist shot success in floorball/unihockey from two different feet positions, J Sports Sci 34(21):2087-2094
props.note: Abstract read. 10 players, stationary wrist shots from two feet positions: ball speed about 23.5 m/s in both; accuracy better with the feet at a right angle to the target line; speed came from bending the supporting leg, hip and trunk rotation and top-hand wrist action; players who looked at the target were more accurate.

props.name: Table Tennis England: The Laws of Table Tennis 2026-27 (reproduced from the 2026 ITTF statutes, with TTE byelaws), Issue 1, July 2026
props.licence: ITTF / Table Tennis England; facts only
props.note: Read. Table 2.74 x 1.525 m, 76 cm high; net 15.25 cm; ball 40 mm, 2.7 g. Service (2.6): ball rests on the open palm of the stationary free hand; projected near vertically without spin, rising at least 16 cm, struck as it falls; from the start of service until struck the ball is above the playing surface, behind the end line and not hidden from the receiver; the free arm leaves the space between ball and net once the ball is projected. Point lost if the free hand touches the playing surface or the table is moved (2.10.1). Games to 11, two-point lead from 10-all; service changes every 2 points; expedite after 10 minutes.

props.name: Hopper A, Haff EE, Joyce C, Lloyd RS, Haff GG 2017, Neuromuscular training improves lower extremity biomechanics associated with knee injury during landing in 11-13 year old female netball athletes, Frontiers in Physiology 8:883
props.note: Read (abstract). 23 girls aged about 12; drop jump and a single-leg landing; 6 weeks of training changed knee position and landing force. No angle values in the abstract. Used only for movement-quality wording and youth context.

props.name: FIBA Official Basketball Rules 2024 (v1.0, valid from 1 October 2024)
props.note: Read Art. 1-31 verbatim (court 28x15 m, free-throw line 5.80 m, 3-pt arc 6.75 m, travelling Art. 25, dribble Art. 24, act of shooting Art. 15, equipment and jewellery Art. 4.4, bleeding Art. 5.6). Art. 43 free throws (5 s, behind the line, no touching the line until the ball touches the ring) read only as a summary; re-verify. Equipment appendix (basket height, ball sizes) not reached.

props.name: Goalball UK, National Schools Programme (2020)
props.note: Read. School delivery (clubs, teacher training, resources) and school competition for children and young people with a visual impairment; 'a fully inclusive sport which means anybody can play'.

props.name: ECB Fast Bowling Regulations for players aged 19 and below (directive card)
props.note: Read. Max overs per spell / per day: 11 and below 4/8; 12-13 5/10; 14-15 5/12; 16-17 6/15; 18-19 7/18. Rest equal to spell length from the same end. Hard-ball cricket only.

props.name: Cabarkapa et al. 2023, Kinematic differences based on shooting proficiency and distance in female basketball players, J Funct Morphol Kinesiol 8(3):129
props.note: Reused from sport 02. 18 women: proficient shooters released higher (release height about 1.40 x standing height vs 1.28).

props.name: Dewanti A, Nurseto F, Kurniawan C, Priyono D 2025, Contribution of agility and reaction to footwork ability in kabaddi athletes, Aisyah Journal of Physical Education 4(1)
props.note: Read. 24 provincial athletes (12 women, 12 men): agility (r 0.72) and reaction (r 0.54) together explained about 63% of footwork test scores.

props.name: Bohnert 2016, A complete kinematic, kinetic and EMG analysis of the football throw in collegiate quarterbacks (MSc thesis)
props.note: Reused from sport 06. Cites Fleisig 1996: shoulder abduction about 96 deg at stride-foot contact.

props.name: Paralympics Australia, Boccia information sheet (August 2024)
props.note: Read. BC1 and BC2: coordination impairments (BC1 may throw with hands or feet, with an assistant; BC2 throws independently). BC3: the most significant impairment in arms, trunk and legs; uses a ramp and an assistant who sits with their back to play. BC4: limited movement or weakness in all four limbs; independent.

props.name: WBSC, Baseball5 Official Rulebook 2026 (published July 2026; FFBS copy)
props.note: Read (text extraction; sections unnumbered, pages 3-15). Rubber ball only, no bat or glove. Fair territory an 18 m square; bases 13 m apart; 3 m batter's box outside fair territory; no-hit line 4.5 m from home (3 m for U-15); doubled first base. Five players a side, five innings, three outs; mixed competitions need at least two of each gender on defence. The ball is hit with the palm or the fist; the first bounce must land beyond the no-hit line and inside the foul lines; first bounce in foul territory is an out; the batter must stay inside the box until the ball leaves the hand; faking a hit is an out; runners may not slide or dive and must avoid collisions; only kneepads and elbow sleeves allowed as protection.

props.name: Puddle DL, Maulder PS 2013, Ground reaction forces and loading rates associated with parkour and traditional drop landing techniques, J Sports Sci Med 12(1):122-129
props.note: Read. 10 male traceurs, 0.75 m drop onto a force plate: the parkour precision landing (forefoot, heels not touching) and the roll gave about 38-43% lower peak force, about 60-80% longer time to peak force and lower loading rates than a traditional forefoot-to-heel landing; precision and roll did not differ significantly.

props.name: Henderson ME 2004, Biomechanical comparison of netball shooting technique: a six-week jump training intervention, MHSc thesis, Auckland University of Technology
props.note: Read (abstract). 18 premier-grade women from 3 m. Minimum knee angle in the crouch 124 +/- 20 deg (standing shot) and 118 +/- 22 deg (jump shot); shoulder at release 143 +/- 15 deg.

props.name: Morato MP, Menezes RP, Fonseca S, Furtado OLPC 2018, Faster balls increase the probability of scoring a goal in female and male elite goalball, Rev Bras Cienc Esporte 40(4):427-434
props.note: Read. 2008 Paralympic matches, 2,645 throws (39 men, 29 women), 30 Hz video in Kinovea. Mean ball time 0.73 s (men) and 1.01 s (women); goals were faster (0.68 and 0.92 s); faster balls raised scoring odds. Defenders often have under a second, and men about half a second on fast rolling shots. Defenders lie stretched for rolling balls and slightly lifted for bouncing balls.

props.name: Mekala and Anbalagan 2023, Construction of norms for selected game related physical fitness variables of kho-kho players, Int J Physiol Nutr Phys Educ 8(1):257-259
props.note: Read. 500 boys aged 11-14: 30 m dash median about 4.71 s; 6 x 10 m shuttle about 16.7 s. Unusually narrow spreads and an unrelated reference; treat with caution.

props.name: Sherwin IA, Kenny IC, An examination of putting movement and performance variability using standard, belly and long-handled putters (BASES student conference)
props.note: Read. 72 golfers aged 15-75; putter lengths 86, 109 and 132 cm; holed rates from 1.83 m were 73-87% (low handicap) and 75-78% (high handicap); stroke timing differed by putter type. Year not stated.

props.name: fcsnooker coaching pages, in association with Frank Callan (stance, bridge, grip, cue action, sighting, the drill; 2012)
props.note: Read. Balance matters more than a set stance; back leg braced, lean forward, front knee bent. Dominant eye over the cue (or chin central if even-sighted). V bridge pressed firmly into the cloth and kept still. Grip loose enough that the butt does not lift. Keep the cue horizontal through the stroke; at the end of the backswing the tip is about 10-12 cm from the cue ball. Pause at the end of the last backswing; follow through on line. Eyes on the object ball at contact; decide the shot before getting down. Faults: tight grip (scoop), eyes moving early, elbow drift, moving bridge. Author credentials not stated on the pages.

props.name: Kleshnev V 2022, The biomechanics of the recovery phase, row2k Features (BioRow)
props.note: Read. In a large stroke database, legs-trunk-arms in the drive and arms-trunk-legs in the recovery were the most typical sequences; trunk timing in drive and recovery mirrored each other. Not peer-reviewed.

props.name: Shell JR, Robbins SMK, Dixon PC et al. 2017, Skating start propulsion: three-dimensional kinematic analysis of elite male and female ice hockey players, Sports Biomech
props.note: Read. 9 men and 10 women, university varsity, first 7 steps, 240 Hz. Stride rate 1.84 (women) and 1.94 (men) strides/s; step width 0.05-0.33 m; peak speed 7.0 and 7.6 m/s; hip abduction from about 5 deg in swing to 25 deg at push-off; women about 10 deg less hip abduction and 10 deg more knee extension at ice contact.

props.name: Linthorne NP, Stokes TG 2014, Optimum projection angle for attaining maximum distance in a rugby place kick, J Sports Sci Med 13:211-216
props.note: Read. One semi-professional male kicker, 49 maximum kicks: 46.8 m, 26.2 m/s at 30.8 deg. Optimum projection angle for distance about 31 deg (32 deg to clear the crossbar).

props.name: World Rugby news, 17 June 2026: World Rugby lowers legal tackle height in community rugby
props.note: Read. In effect from 1 July 2026 for seasons starting after that date. Ten unions trialled it over two years with more than 150,000 tackles studied; a lower tackle height reduced upright tackles, which are the most likely to cause avoidable head impacts. Elite trial at the Junior World Championship from 27 June 2026.

props.name: Computer simulation on the cueing movements in cue sports: a validation study, PeerJ (doi 10.7717/peerj.16180)
props.note: Read in part; author list not captured. 10 men (national team to recreational). Elbow bend range about 56 deg and shoulder elevation range about 9 deg during back-spin shots.

props.name: Systematic review: biomechanical evolution in longitudinal analysis of lumbar stress injuries in fast bowlers (2026)
props.note: Not opened (browser check). Listed for the lumbar-injury technique evidence (mixed action, shoulder counter-rotation); thresholds not taken from it yet.

props.name: Trunk and shoulder kinematics of rowing displayed by Olympic athletes, Sports Biomechanics 22(9):1095-1107 (2023)
props.note: Read (record). 58 national-team rowers (31 women, 27 men), IMUs at 18, 26 and 32 strokes per minute. Range of motion rose with stroke rate; women had more lumbar, thoracic and shoulder range, with a more extended finish.

props.name: England Darts Organisation, Child protection policy (undated)
props.note: Read. A child is under 18. Parents and players must be told when coaches or officials use video as a coaching aid (3.4). No smoking or drinking alcohol in the company of young people; avoid unobserved one-to-one situations; coaches need child-protection training, first aid and a criminal records check. The policy may be out of date (refers to CRB checks).

props.name: British Fencing, British Youth Championships kit requirements (updated March 2023)
props.note: Read. Age groups U12, U14, U16, U18 with blade sizes (size 2-3 for U12/U14, size 5 for older groups); rigid chest protection compulsory for women and recommended for girls from 10.

props.name: Simsek D, Ertan H, The different release techniques in high level archery: a comparative case study, ISBS proceedings
props.note: Read. One high-level archer; finger-hook type changed body sway around the clicker; a three-finger hook may reduce string deflection. Qualitative.

props.name: USA Basketball Youth Development Guidebook, Second Edition
props.licence: All rights reserved, USA Basketball; facts only; third-party host, confirm the official edition on usab.com
props.note: Levels by skill mastery (Introductory, Foundational, Advanced, Performance) with LTAD ages 6-9, 8-12, 12-15, 14-17, 17+. Skill content (BEEF shooting, triple threat, pivots, jump stop, defensive stance and slide, passes, rebounding) and common errors (elbow flare, pushing the shot) seen only as a summary; re-verify.

props.name: Janura M, Kratochvil J, Lehnert M, Vaverka F 2005, An analysis of the forward stroke as used in a wild water kayak on flat waters, Acta Univ Palacki Olomuc Gymn 35(2):113-117
props.note: Read; numeric table unreadable. 9 juniors on flat water: better paddlers had a shorter pull, higher stroke frequency, more symmetrical hand paths and less forward-back trunk movement.

props.name: USA Bowling, Coaching Phase 2: Beginner Bowler (course outline)
props.note: Read. Eight-week beginner course: athletic stance, one-step delivery with push-away, four- and five-step approaches; on a four-step approach the first step crosses slightly in front so the arm swings in a straight line; finish with the opposite arm out for balance, body facing the target and the ball-side leg behind; 3-6-9 spare system and key pin.

props.name: Lopez de Subijana C, Juarez D, Mallo J, Navarro E, Biomechanical analysis of the penalty-corner drag-flick of elite male and female hockey players
props.licence: facts only (journal and year not in the copy read)
props.note: Read. 1 expert model, 6 elite men and 6 elite women (Spanish national team and first division), 250 Hz. Ball speed 21.9 (men) and 17.9 m/s (women); stance width 1.55 and 1.32 m; drag distance 2.42 and 1.70 m; lead knee 156 and 155 deg at front-foot contact; men followed a pelvis-trunk-stick sequence.

props.name: IFSC Competition Regulations, International Events, version 2.0 (March 2025; copy hosted by Climbing Escalade Canada)
props.note: About two-thirds read verbatim. Lead walls at least 15 m high; 6 minutes per route; only holds used by either hand count; belay checks before starting (knot, harness, rope). Speed: two parallel lanes; start with both hands and one foot on the starting holds and one foot on the pad; reaction under 0.100 s is a false start (summary); times to 1/1000 s. Boulder (summary only): 4-5 minute rotations, zone and top scoring, matting checked before each round. Youth World Championships for U17 and U19.

props.name: Judo Victoria Junior Contest (Shiai) Rules, edition 6, January 2024
props.note: Read. Age groups U9, U11, U13, U15 (minimum age 6). Armlocks, strangles and headlocks are not allowed at U15 and below. U11 and U9: no throws dropping onto one or both knees (e.g. seoi-nage, seoi-otoshi), no techniques that drive the opponent's head into the mat. U9: no sacrifice throws including makikomi. Contests 2-3 min. After a concussion the medical officer has the final say and the player cannot continue.

props.name: Kobayashi Y, Ae M, Miyazaki A, Fujii N 2011, (overarm throwing in elementary school girls), ISBS 2011, Portuguese J Sport Sci 11(Suppl 2):997-1000
props.note: Read. 21 girls in grades 2, 4 and 6: ball speed rose from about 10 to 16 m/s and release height from 1.35 to 1.60 m with age; stride about 0.36 s, throwing phase about 0.28 s.

props.name: ECB Recreational Cricket Safety Guidelines (December 2025 update)
props.note: Read. Helmet with faceguard required when batting against a hard ball and for 16-17s fielding within 8 yards; under-18 keepers standing up need a helmet or face protector; helmets to BS7928:2013, neck protectors strongly advised; concussion e-learning recommended.

props.name: Biomechanical analysis of the late approach and the take off in the indoor women's long jump, J Hum Sport Exerc 16(3) proceedings, 2021
props.note: Read (abstract). 11 jumps, indoor competition, 300 fps, 6.88 +/- 0.23 m. Approach 9.8 +/- 0.3 m/s; take-off velocity 8.3 +/- 0.4 m/s; take-off angle 20.7 +/- 2.3 deg; take-off leg knee 171.2 +/- 4.7 deg at take-off; penultimate step 12.2 +/- 2.8% longer than the last. Authors and DOI not in the fetched text; number of athletes not stated.

props.name: Coleman SG, A three-dimensional kinematic analysis of the volleyball jump serve (ISBS proceedings)
props.note: Read. 11 Great Britain international men, 50 Hz. Centre-of-mass velocity at take-off 2.76 m/s forward and 2.77 m/s up; hand speed at impact 16.3 m/s; ball speed 23.7 m/s. Context only; no band uses it.

props.name: World Rugby Passport: 2026-06 Community Tackle Height law wordings approved (Laws 9.13, 14.1, 14.5a)
props.note: Read. Approved 17 June 2026, in law materials from 1 July 2026. Tacklers must tackle below the sanction line: shoulder line in elite rugby; waist or base of the sternum in community rugby (unions choose). Tackling above the line in open field play is dangerous play (Law 9.13) and a penalty. Game On variations let organisers choose the line and limit two-player tackles.

props.name: NCERT, Health and Physical Education Class 10, Chapter 7: Team Games and Sports II (kabaddi)
props.note: Read (kabaddi section). Squad 10-12; junior boys 20-min halves, junior girls and sub-juniors 15-min halves. Defensive skills named: ankle hold, thigh hold, waist hold, wrist hold, blocking. No revival for bonus points. Governing bodies: IKF, Asian Kabaddi Federation, AKFI (1973).

props.name: Manomai W, Limroongreungrat W 2016, Knee joint biomechanics during different sepaktakraw spike take-off, J Sports Sci Technol 16(2):9-21
props.note: Read. 12 male college players: roll spikes reached the highest ball (about 1.28 times standing height) with more knee rotation at take-off. Used only for the spike nodes, which have no protocol.

props.name: FIH Rules of Hockey including explanations (effective 1 January 2015), hosted by the School Games Federation of India
props.note: Read about half verbatim; an old edition. Up to 11 players on the field including the goalkeeper; pitch 91.40 x 55.00 m; two 35-minute halves. No play with the back of the stick (9.5); no hard forehand hit with the edge (9.6); no lifting the stick over other players' heads (9.2); no intentionally raised hit except a shot at goal, and an unintentionally raised hit is not an offence unless dangerous (9.9); a flick or scoop towards an opponent within 5 m is dangerous; dangerous play is play that causes legitimate evasive action (9.8); field players must not stop, kick or carry the ball with the body (9.11); no obstruction (9.12). The penalty-corner first-shot height (460 mm for a hit) was seen only in a summary. Associations may vary rules for age groups below top leagues.

props.name: Psycharakis SG, Sanders RH 2010, Body roll in swimming: a review, J Sports Sci 28(3):229-236 (summary page)
props.note: Read (summary). Swimmers roll the shoulders much more than the hips; hip roll rises with fatigue; faster swimmers rolled the shoulders less in a 200 m swim; buoyancy drives much of the roll. No angle values read.

props.name: International Cheer Union, Cheerleading Rules 2026
props.note: About half read verbatim (general safety and levels Introductory to Intermediate). Qualified coach supervision; proficiency before progression; emergency plan; no stunts, pyramids, tosses or tumbling on hard, wet or uneven surfaces; soft-soled cheer shoes; no jewellery. Levels Introductory (no tumbling or stunts) to Elite. Jumps are not treated as tumbling. Performance cheer (pom, jazz, hip hop) sections not reached.

props.name: Hanley B 2021, The biomechanics of distance running. In Blagrove and Hayes (eds), The Science and Practice of Middle and Long Distance Running, Routledge, pp. 17-27
props.note: Read about two-thirds verbatim. Cadence 2.75-3.25 Hz (165-195 steps/min) in distance runners; knee flexes about 15-20 deg from first contact to midstance; a very large foot-ahead distance ('overstriding') adds braking; braking at contact is normal; habitual rearfoot strikers should not be told to switch foot strike.

props.name: Mulloy F, Mullineaux DR, Irwin G 2015, Use of the kinematic chain in the fencing attacking lunge, ISBS 2015 Poitiers pp. 1114-1117
props.note: Read. 4 experts and 6 novices. Lunge length 1.12 +/- 0.07 leg lengths (expert) vs 0.83 +/- 0.15 (novice); peak horizontal sword speed 3.2 vs 2.6 m/s; rear knee peak about 171 vs 162 deg; experts sequenced elbow first, then hip, knee and ankle.

props.name: Alway 2016, Kinematic and temporal analysis of overarm throwing in Finnish baseball players (MSc thesis, University of Jyvaskyla)
props.note: Baseball, not cricket. Reviews stride length of about 85-87% of height in overarm throwing. Used only as context for the throw stride band.

props.name: World Lacrosse, Rules differences between women's field and sixes (v2, February 2021)
props.note: Read (table layout garbled in places). Women's field 110 x 60 m with up to 10 on the field including the goalkeeper; four 15-minute periods; no shot clock. A shot taken without regard to an opponent's position is a major foul unless the ball travels at or below knee level.

props.name: Steyn D, Mithrush T, Koentges C, Andrews S, Plourde A 2025, Executing a successful third shot drop in pickleball (SportRxiv preprint 499; arXiv 2501.00163)
props.note: Read. A ball-flight model, checked against six filmed shots; no player kinematics. From the baseline at about knee height (0.75 m), a successful drop needs a launch speed of 10.9-13 m/s and an angle of 15.5-22.5 deg down the line, or 13.3-16 m/s and 12.5-18 deg cross-court; spin is of secondary importance.

props.name: GAA, Gaelic football (rules overview)
props.note: Read. Carry for four steps; the ball must be bounced or soloed (dropped onto the foot and kicked back to the hand) after every four steps; no two bounces in a row; handpass with a striking motion of the hand or fist.

props.name: CISG Amsterdam 2022 concussion consensus (Patricios et al. 2023)
props.note: The engine refers on; it never diagnoses.

props.name: Lees et al. 2010, The biomechanics of kicking in soccer: a review, J Sports Sci 28(8)
props.note: figures taken from an unofficial copy; re-verify against the published paper before promotion

props.name: Seiferheld BE, Frost J, Østergaard TB, Krog MS, Klitgaard KK, de Zee M 2023, Full-body kinematics and vertical ground reaction forces in elite ten-pin bowling: a field study, Sensors 23(19):8284
props.note: Read in part. 6 elite Danish men, five-step approach, 72 deliveries each. Ball speed about 8.4 m/s falling to 8.1 m/s over a session as wrist and elbow bend increased; top of backswing about 1.69 m high; slide-foot peak force about 165% of body weight; about 640 ms to release (start point unclear).

props.name: IFAF International Flag Football Rules 2023 (5 on 5, non-contact)
props.note: Read. Field 50 x 25 yd plus 10-yd end zones; 5 players a side; non-contact (no blocking, tackling or kicking); flag pull ends the play; flag guarding, diving and jumping illegal; rushers start 7 yd from the line; QB cannot run past the line unless the ball was handed off or touched; 7 s to pass; no helmets or pads; women's games use youth-size balls.

props.name: McManus H, Harper L, Finlay MJ 2025, The physical qualities of national league female British American flag football players, Int J Sports Sci Coach (accepted manuscript)
props.note: Read. 14 women in the BAFA women's national league: 20-yd sprint about 3.4 s, pro-agility about 5.4 s, broad jump about 1.9 m; no offence-defence differences. Plays last about 5-6 s (cited).

props.name: Thompson MA, Blair D, Shippen M, Toma S 2024, Biomechanical analysis of elite ice-climbing performance, Biomechanics 4(3):452-459
props.note: Read. 24 elite competitors (16 men, 8 women), video at 120 Hz. Elbows about 151-166 deg at weight bearing on several holds. The top half took less total time (144 vs 232 s) and fewer moves (24 vs 33) on the section; number of rests did not differ. Ice, not rock.

props.name: Genevois et al. 2018, Using inertial sensors to monitor on-court tennis training sessions, ITF Coaching & Sport Science Review 75
props.note: 14 junior boys (13-19): per session 291 forehands, 198 backhands, 54 serves; training serves 39 vs 82 in U15 competition. Recommends varying serve volume between sessions and a regular shoulder rotator programme; no injury threshold established.

props.name: Holdback C, Ibrahim R, Haydon D, Grimshaw P, Kelso R, Pinder RA 2025, The dynamics of seated shot put: a case study example of pole grip optimisation, Front Sports Act Living 7:1509435
props.note: Read. One female F34 athlete, 3 kg shot, Vicon 200 Hz. The trunk provided about 64% of horizontal shot speed and the shoulder 21%; delivery from power position to release about 0.4 s; distance SD 8-16 cm across grips; low pole grip gave more trunk range. Cites Tokyo 2020: 60% of F34 athletes used a pole; F32 pole users threw further.

props.name: ISTAF, Quad Sepaktakraw rules (2015; STFI copy)
props.note: Read. Four a side; server with both feet outside the baseline; other players stationary; same net and ball as the regu event.

props.name: ActiveSG Circle, Equipment and attire for sepak takraw (Singapore)
props.note: Read. Summary of court, net, ball and attire for learners.

props.name: World Aquatics Swimming Rule Quick Reference Infraction Sheet 2023-2025 (in force from 13 July 2023), hosted by East Region Swimming
props.note: Read. Freestyle, backstroke and butterfly: the head must break the surface at or before 15 m after the start and each turn; not completely submerged during the stroke. Breaststroke: at most one butterfly kick before the first breaststroke kick after the start or turn; one arm stroke then one leg kick, in that order; simultaneous arm and leg movements; hands not brought back beyond the hip line during the stroke; head breaks the surface every cycle; no downward butterfly kick during the stroke; two-hand simultaneous touch. Butterfly: simultaneous arms; no alternating or breaststroke kick. Backstroke: on the back except in the turn. The card is a summary, not the full rules. A newer card in force from 13 March 2026 exists but was not read.

props.name: Steer RR, McGregor AH, Bull AMJ 2006, A comparison of kinematics and performance measures of two rowing ergometers, J Sports Sci Med 5(1):52-59
props.note: Read in part. 12 novice male rowers at 18-20 and 28-30 strokes per minute; lumbar-pelvic motion differed between a Concept2 and a WaterRower, so bands may need a per-machine check.

props.name: UK Cheerleading Association, What do I need to coach? and Level 1 Cheerleading Leadership Award
props.note: Read. Qualified coaches only; insurance; DBS checks for adults working with young people; a qualified first-aider at every practice; risk assessment; mats; enough ceiling height for tosses. A Level 1 leadership award (age 12+) lets young leaders assist a qualified coach.

props.name: Sports Management, Grassroots sports: Rounders (2013)
props.note: Read in part. About 24,000 adults played weekly (about 70% women) and nearly 70,000 monthly (Active People Survey); played in 87% of UK schools; many girls drop out after primary school.

props.name: Tsai CL, Huang C, Lin DC, Chang SS, Biomechanical analysis of the upper extremity in three different badminton overhead strokes (ISBS proceedings)
props.note: Read. One world top-2 male player, 500 Hz. Smash shuttle speed 68 m/s and angle -11.5 deg; clear 64 m/s at +10.6 deg; drop 29 m/s. A single player: used for context only, never for bands.

props.name: AoC Sport, Introducing flag football
props.note: Read. Colleges work with BAFA and NFL UK on primary and secondary session plans, game cards, young officials and teacher training (sessions listed November 2026 to February 2027).

props.name: British Weight Lifting, Position statement: youth weightlifting (Kite, Lloyd, Hamill; published 2018)
props.note: Read. The governing body's position: youth weightlifting is appropriate when prescribed and coached by qualified professionals; technique and skill mastery come before load, with load a low priority until technique is consistent; progression built on fundamental movement; BWL runs under-13 competitions judged on technique. It cites studies reporting low injury rates; we do not repeat injury claims.

props.name: Goalball UK, Free goalball resources for secondary schools with PE Office (13 March 2024)
props.note: Read. Free lesson plans and videos for secondary PE.

props.name: ICC Regulations for the Review of Bowlers Reported with Suspected Illegal Bowling Actions
props.note: Read. Art. 2.1: 15-degree elbow-extension limit, arm horizontal to release, measured with the Standard Analysis Protocols at an Accredited Testing Centre. Only such a test can decide legality.

props.name: GAA Learning, Hurling: Striking from the Hand (2024)
props.note: Read. Toss the sliotar from a cupped hand to shoulder height, eyes on the ball; slide the non-dominant hand into the lock position and raise the hurley; step forward with the lead foot and swing down; strike at knee height; transfer weight onto the front leg in the follow-through. Common errors: missing the ball, wrong hand on top, tossing too high or too far in front. Teach both sides from an early age. Drills include hit the cones and striking in pairs.

props.name: Dai B, Layer JS, Hinshaw TJ, Cook RF, Dufek JS 2020, Kinematic analyses of parkour landings from as high as 2.7 meters, J Hum Kinet 72:15-28
props.note: Read. 20 trained traceurs (3 women), video at about 60 Hz. From 0.9 m: soft landings took about 0.38 s from contact against 0.17 s for stiff landings; peak knee flexion about 116 deg (squat), 135 deg (forward) and 120 deg (roll) against 77 deg (stiff); rolls showed the smallest change in vertical speed in the first 100 ms. Only the 0.9 m values are used here, as a guide for ground-level work.

props.name: England Korfball, Equality, Diversity and Inclusion report 2024 (member survey)
props.note: Read. Survey respondents were 55% female; 9% disabled.

props.name: Brown MB 2009, Biomechanical analysis of flatwater sprint kayaking (doctoral thesis, University of Southampton / Chichester)
props.note: Abstract read; full text failed to load. International paddlers had higher stroke rates and scored higher than national and novice paddlers on trunk rotation, leg motion, stroke width and forward reach.

props.name: British Wrestling, Education and learning (2025)
props.note: Read. Level 1 (1 day) and Level 2 (2 days) coaching courses after online theory; referee, safeguarding and anti-doping learning.

props.name: McGuine, Brooks & Hetzel 2011, The effect of lace-up ankle braces on injury rates in high school basketball players, Am J Sports Med 39(9):1840-1848
props.note: 1,460 players: acute ankle injuries 0.47 vs 1.41 per 1000 exposures with braces (HR 0.32); severity unchanged.

props.name: Abdelkader et al. 2021, Kinematical variables of discus throw in para athletics (class F57) and their relationship with achievement, Spormetre 19(3):60-70
props.note: Read; table layout garbled. One female F57 athlete, six throws, 2D video: release angle about 41.5 deg (SD 1.5), within the 35-45 deg range the authors cite; throwing elbow about 153.5 deg at the finish; trunk angle about 12.5 deg (finish) and 22 deg (start); delivery about 0.39 s. Authors advise releasing at shoulder height. Tentative: one athlete.

props.name: IFAF, International Flag Football Rules 2021 (incl. beach and indoor)
props.note: About half read verbatim. Base rule single-sex teams (mixed by national option); flags 15-16 in long. Blocking renamed shielding (5 yd); illegal contact 10 yd (9-1-1). Jumping and diving to avoid a pull are illegal (12-3, 12-6); dipping and spinning legal. 7-second pass clock; no-run zones inside the 5 yd line. Ball sizes for under-13 and under-16.

props.name: School Games, SEND boccia format (July 2026)
props.note: Read. 'Boccia 12s': two teams of three, ages 7-16, mixed, primarily for pupils with special educational needs and disabilities but open to all; the jack must cross the V line; adaptations include moving the throwing line, bigger targets and softer balls; players stay seated behind the line.

props.name: Miller SA, A biomechanical comparison between shooting technique in basketball and netball, ISBS proceedings pp. 358-361 (year not confirmed, about 1994)
props.note: Read. England senior women's team, 5 scoring shots, 3D video at 25 Hz. At release: ball speed 3.7 +/- 0.4 m/s, release angle 80 +/- 9 deg (much steeper than basketball, 49 deg), elbow 156 +/- 7 deg, shoulder 145 +/- 9 deg.

props.name: Olympics.com, Kabaddi: how to play India's 4000-year-old indigenous sport (rules explainer)
props.note: Read. Court 13 x 10 m (men), 12 x 8 m (women); 1 m lobbies; baulk line 3.75 m from the mid line (3 m women) and bonus line 1 m beyond it. 7 a side; halves of 20 min (men) and 15 min (women). One raider chants kabaddi; touch points, tackle points, all out worth 2 extra. Bonus point when one foot crosses the bonus line with the trailing foot in the air and at least 6 defenders on court. Pro Kabaddi League: 30-second raids, do-or-die raids, super raids and super tackles. Played on mats.

props.name: Goodin JR 2015, Comparison of external kinetic and kinematic variables between high-bar and low-bar back squats across a range of loads, MA thesis, East Tennessee State University
props.note: Read in part. 6 trained men. High-bar squats moved the bar faster and further; low-bar squats used a wider stance and, per the literature reviewed, a more forward trunk. Bands allow for both bar positions.

props.name: Cabarkapa et al. 2022, Differences in biomechanical characteristics between made and missed jump shots in male basketball players, Biomechanics 2(3):352-360
props.note: 29 recreational males. Release angle made vs missed: 2-pt 55.5 vs 54 deg, 3-pt 53 vs 48 deg (p=0.002); knee about 104-110 deg included angle at the lowest point; elbow height greater on made shots. Table values from a summary; verify.

props.name: Civita A, Fiori S, Romani G, A smartphone-based acquisition system for hips rotation fluency assessment, arXiv:1512.01260
props.note: Read. One expert, one intermediate and one novice climber on two tasks; hip-rotation jerk was lowest in the expert (about 0.4-0.7 million) and highest in the novice (0.8-3.2 million). No statistics.

props.name: Walker J, Bissas A, Paradisis GP et al. 2021, Kinematic factors associated with start performance in World-class male sprinters, J Biomech 124:110554
props.note: Read (post-print). 8 men's 60 m finalists, 2018 World Indoors, 150 Hz. Block time 0.34 +/- 0.02 s; first ground contact (GC1) 0.175 +/- 0.014 s; trunk angle (from horizontal) 39 +/- 3 deg at GC1 touchdown and 43 +/- 3 deg at take-off; shank angle 35 +/- 3 deg at touchdown and 26 +/- 3 deg at take-off; thigh separation at GC1 take-off 102 +/- 7 deg; touchdown distance -0.12 m (foot behind the centre of mass). A lower trunk angle (r = -0.59) and wider thigh separation (r = 0.62) at take-off went with better acceleration. Men only.

props.name: Wagner H, Buchecker M, von Duvillard SP, Muller E 2010, Kinematic description of elite vs. low level players in team-handball jump throw, J Sports Sci Med 9:15-23
props.note: Read (abstract). 26 men of different levels; elite players had higher ball release speed, shoulder internal-rotation speed at release and trunk-flexion speed at release.

props.name: Sinclair J, Bottoms L, Taylor PJ, Mahmood K 2017, Effects of shoes on kinetics and kinematics of the squash forward lunge in male players, Kinesiology 49(2):178-184
props.note: Read in full. 12 male university players. Peak knee flexion in the forehand lunge about 107-112 +/- 15-17 deg; knee about 29-33 deg bent at foot strike; peak hip flexion about 84-88 deg. Shoes made no difference to joint angles.

props.name: Chen Z, He D, Fang J, Chen X, Liu Y, Zhong X, Hu X 2026, Toward personalized darts training: a data-driven framework based on skeleton-based biomechanical analysis and motion modeling, arXiv:2604.01130
props.note: Read in part (some numbers from a summary). 7 players (4 professional), 2,396 throws, markerless depth-camera skeleton. Elbow bend at release ranged widely between players (about 27-81 deg), so personal baselines matter; trunk sway around release about 1-3 mm in professionals vs 4-8 mm in non-professionals. Flags deviations by z-score against the player's own best throws.

props.name: Robertson I et al., A pilot biomechanical assessment of curling deliveries: toe sliding vs flatfoot sliding (manuscript, BMJ Open Sport Exerc Med)
props.note: Read. 11 curlers, motion capture and insoles: knee joint forces in toe slides were about twice those in flatfoot slides; the authors suggest coaches promote the flatfoot slide where a curler can use either.

props.name: World Gymnastics (FIG), Women's Artistic Gymnastics Code of Points 2025-2028 (approved February 2024; published 1 April 2025)
props.note: Read in part; the deduction table lost its layout, so values are not verified. Handstands on bars are judged on deviation from vertical in bands of more than 10-30 deg, 30-45 deg and over 45 deg. Without a fall, landing deductions are capped at 0.80. Faults include bent arms or knees, legs apart, extra steps, very large steps, deep squat and extra arm swings. The Technical Regulations take precedence.

props.name: Greater lower limb flexion in gymnastic landings is associated with reduced landing force: a repeated measures study, Sports Biomechanics 14(1):45-56 (2015)
props.note: Read (abstract). 21 elite women's artistic gymnasts. Landings with more hip, knee and ankle bend had lower and later peak landing force; authors suggest encouraging more bend.

props.name: Malone LA, Gervais P, Steadward RD 1999, Parameters of ball release in wheelchair basketball free throw shooting, ISBS 1999
props.note: Read. Swishes at a world championship by class: release height 1.62, 1.60, 1.79 and 1.84 m and launch angle 59, 58, 55 and 55 deg for classes 1-4; lower-class players released lower, faster and steeper. Classification explained 40% of the variation in release height.

props.name: Sayers MGL 2011, Kinematic analysis of line-out throwing in elite international rugby union, J Sports Sci Med 10(3):553-558
props.note: Read in part. 3 elite international hookers, 30 throws to 6, 10 and 15 m. Release speed 8.3, 9.3 and 10.4 m/s; shoulder flexion at the end of the backswing 143-154 deg. The most accurate thrower kept the pelvis close to neutral; the others rotated it forward nearly 40 deg. Tiny sample.

props.name: R&A / USGA Rules of Golf (2023 edition), Rule 10: Preparing for and making a stroke
props.licence: R&A Rules Limited and USGA; facts only
props.note: Read. 10.1a: fairly strike the ball with the clubhead, momentary contact only, no pushing, scraping or scooping. 10.1b: do not anchor the club, directly (club or gripping hand held against the body, except against a hand or forearm) or through a forearm anchor point; merely touching the body or clothing is not a breach. 10.1c: no stance deliberately astride or touching the line of play behind the ball. Breach of 10.1: two penalty strokes in stroke play. 10.2b(4): the caddie must not stand behind the player to help with aim.

props.name: Greater Sport, British Wheelchair Basketball launch new programme to double participation (January 2021)
props.note: Read. 'Inspire a Generation' aimed to double participation over four years with Sport England funding, through six-week community taster sessions.

props.name: The Depot Climbing Centre Manchester, Conditions of use (2018)
props.note: Read. One wall's rules: descend by down-climbing or at least a controlled fall; never stand under a climber; under-18s supervised by a registered adult unless assessed and parent-authorised for unsupervised climbing, only from age 14; under-18s always supervised on auto-belays; novices must not belay without supervision.

props.name: Yoon S, Kim JH, Park JH, Ryu J, Park SK, Kim JN 2017, Effects of counter-rotation position on knee/hip angulation, centre of mass inclination and edging angle in simulated alpine skiing, Korean J Sport Biomech 27(2):91-97
props.note: Read. 12 male instructors and racers on a lab slope. With the upper body counter-rotated (facing the outside of the turn) the edge angle was 28 +/- 3 deg, against 16 +/- 5 deg neutral and 9 +/- 4 deg rotated with the turn; centre-of-mass inclination about 26-29 deg; hip angulation largest in counter-rotation.

props.name: Wong DWC, Lee WCC, Lam WK 2020, Biomechanics of table tennis: a systematic scoping review of playing levels and maneuvers, Appl Sci 10(15):5203
props.note: Read in part (abstract and sample table). 29 studies; higher-level players use shoulder and wrist power better through the full-body kinetic chain; backspin, long-line, sidespin and pen-hold strokes are under-studied. Tables of values not readable.

props.name: Goalball UK, Coaching courses (October 2026)
props.note: Read. School Leaders Award (4 hours, with the Youth Sport Trust); Club Leaders Award (one day; under-16s qualify as assistant leaders); eLearning module with UK Coaching and British Blind Sport. Covers guiding a visually impaired person, marking a court and basic attack and defence.

props.name: Hewett et al. 2005, Biomechanical measures of neuromuscular control and valgus loading of the knee, Am J Sports Med
props.note: Reused. Defines the 'knee moves inward' movement-quality fault; never used to predict injury.

props.name: GAA, Clubs reminded about rules and guidance around hurling helmets and sliotars (16 March 2026); Camogie Association, Player safety and helmets
props.note: Read. Hurling rule 4.2(i): a helmet meeting IS 355 is required in all hurling games and practice sessions; modified helmets are not covered by the injury fund. Fluorescent sliotars recommended from minor upwards.

props.name: Wikipedia, Greco-Roman wrestling (secondary)
props.note: Read. Holds below the waist are forbidden, the main difference from freestyle; age groups U15, U17, U20, U23 and seniors.

props.name: Goalball UK, Guide to Goalball (30 June 2025)
props.note: Read. Played in silence so players can hear the ball. Underarm shots from a straight run-up or a rotation; smooth, bounce, skippy and spin shots; balls up to about 60 km/h. Defenders start in a ready position, push out to hands and feet and shift according to where the shot comes from. Players wear knee and elbow pads, boxes, shin pads and chest plates. Coach is 'the eyes of the team'. Court tape has string underneath for orientation.

props.name: Himawan MKN, Rilastia D, Syafei M, Nugroho R, Budihardjo B 2018, Biomechanical analysis of snatch technique in conjunction to kinematic motion of Olympic weightlifters, ISPHE 2018
props.note: Read. 6 male international lifters at 80-90% of best, 60 fps video. Knees reached about 162-170 deg at full extension in the second pull; peak bar speeds about 2.4-3.4 m/s. No bar-path numbers.

props.name: Boccia UK, Latest boccia activity across the UK (February 2026)
props.note: Read. Boccia England talent plan 2025-2029 for athletes aged 14-23 in education; Northern Ireland schools project (14 more schools equipped, 20 teachers trained) and a girls-in-boccia day.

props.name: Camogie Association, Official Guide Part 2: Official Playing Rules (2021-2024 edition)
props.note: Read. 15 a side (12-a-side format also); pitch 130-145 x 80-90 m; sliotar 90-110 g, 21 cm. Helmet with facial guard (IS 355) compulsory in games and training (7.2). One-handed handpass with a clear striking action; carry for at most 4 steps; lift with the hurley or feet, not the hand; no two-handed catch. No deliberate shouldering; minimal side-on contact only. A 2024-2027 edition (effective May 2025) exists and was seen in part.

props.name: Ji X, Al Tamimi Z, Gao X, Piovesan D 2025, The impact of draw weight on archers' posture and injury risk through motion capture analysis, Applied Sciences 15(2):879
props.note: Read in part. 13 students (7 men, 6 women), recurve at three draw weights with a GoPro and IMUs. At release the draw shoulder was abducted over 90 deg and the draw elbow flexed about 155 deg; heavier bows changed trunk posture, more so in women. We make no injury claims.

props.name: AFL, Junior Rules (May 2024)
props.note: Read in full. Age groups from U8; ball size 1 at U8 rising to size 4 (girls) or 5 (boys U15+). No tackling at U8; wrap tackle only at U9-U10 with no bumping or shepherding; full tackling from U11. Marks: any distance up to U10, 10 m at U11-U12, 15 m from U13. No kicking off the ground up to U12. Separate U15 and U16-18 girls' competitions with size 4 ball; every player plays 50-75% of the game.

props.name: ICC Men's Test Match Playing Conditions, Clause 21: No ball (2017)
props.note: Read. 21.5.2: some part of the front foot, grounded or raised, must land behind the popping crease. 21.5.1: back foot within and not touching the return crease. 21.2: no Illegal Bowling Action (elbow extension over 15 degrees from arm-horizontal to release; hyperextension discounted).

props.name: Buckeridge E, LeVangie MC, Stetter B, Nigg SR, Nigg BM 2015, An on-ice measurement approach to analyse the biomechanics of ice hockey skating, PLoS ONE 10(5):e0127324
props.note: Read. 9 varsity and 9 recreational players, 30 m sprints: 4.42 s vs 4.95 s. Higher-calibre skaters used more hip extension in acceleration strides and more knee flexion at ice contact at steady speed. Angles only in figures.

props.name: Lee MJC, Chong D 2018, Differences in the mechanics of elite ten-pin bowlers when performing under varying levels of anxieties, ISBS 2018 pp. 318-321
props.note: Read. 11 elite right-handed bowlers, five-step approach. Ball speed about 7.6 m/s; peak ball height about 1.43 m; under pressure the slide was slightly faster and strike rate fell (about 46% to 31%).

props.name: Wikipedia, England Kabaddi Federation UK
props.note: Read. Governs kabaddi and the UK Kabaddi league; about 18 clubs, mostly in London, the Midlands and the South East. Page carries a maintenance banner.

props.name: Bertozzi F, Porcelli S, Marzorati M, Pilotto AM, Galli M, Sforza C, Zago M 2022, Whole-body kinematics during a simulated sprint in flat-water kayakers, Eur J Sport Sci 22(6):817-825
props.note: Read. 11 national-level juniors (3 female, about 16.5 years), 500 m ergometer sprint, motion capture: about 60 strokes a minute; shoulder elevation above 40 deg at full forward reach; trunk flexion range was the smallest of all joints; shoulder, trunk and hip changes with fatigue related to slower times.

props.name: Jeong IS, Heo WS, Ozkaya G, Kim JH, Lee KK 2016, Relationship between the sequential movement, muscle co-contraction and kinematic variables of flying disc backhand throwing, ISBS 2016
props.note: Read. 5 male players, 50 backhands, Vicon 200 Hz. Disc speed 24.0 +/- 2.7 m/s. A shorter delay between shoulder and elbow peak speeds (mean about 40 ms) went with faster discs (r = -0.71); more forearm co-contraction went with straighter flights.

props.name: Balkó Š, Balkó I, Süss V 2014, Analysis of movement structure of the fencing lunge in two different performance-related groups of fencers, Studia sportiva 8(1):85-92
props.note: Read (Czech with English abstract). 7 elite and 7 novice fencers. All elite fencers started the arm before the front foot (by about 142 ms); novices started the leg first (by about 160 ms). Elbow extension from 90 to 180 deg took about 417 ms (elite) vs 563 ms (novice); elite reaction time about 66 ms faster; elite rear knees reached full extension at the end of the lunge (7 of 7 vs 3 of 7).

props.name: MacDonald M, Baker JS, Gu Y, Ugbolue UC 2025, Biomechanical analyses of the handstand: a systematic review, Frontiers in Sports and Active Living 7:1694648
props.note: Read (abstract). 21 studies. Gymnasts hold a fixed body shape and balance mainly with the wrists; when that fails, shoulders, hips and elbows join in. Closing the eyes and flexing the neck reduce stability; stronger gymnasts balance better.

props.name: World Dodgeball Federation, Quick Start Rules U11 Foam (2026)
props.note: Read. 6 players, 4 balls on the centre line, sets up to 2 minutes, 10-second throw clock; sanctions for dangerous head shots; no kicking or spiking.

props.name: Yeon E-J, Ryu J-K 2012, The kinematic analysis of fouette a la seconde in cheerleading, Korean J Appl Biomech 22(2):173-181
props.note: Abstract read. 3 national-team cheerleaders; unstable releve and hip and knee angles affected turn quality. No numbers in the abstract.

props.name: Ball K 2008, Biomechanical considerations of distance kicking in Australian Rules football, Sports Biomechanics 7(1):10-23
props.note: Abstract read. 28 elite players: longer kicks went with higher foot speed and shank speed at contact, a longer last step, higher contact height and ball position relative to the support foot.

props.name: Bottoms L, Greenhalgh A, Sinclair J 2013, Kinematic determinants of weapon velocity during the fencing lunge in experienced epee fencers, Acta Bioeng Biomech 15(4):109-113
props.note: Read. 14 club epee fencers (9 men, 5 women). Front knee flexed about 92 +/- 8 deg at the end of the lunge; rear knee extended to about 7 deg of flexion; rear-knee range of motion and hip flexion predicted sword speed.

props.name: British Gymnastics (UK national governing body), website
props.note: Read (home, about, safe sport pages). Lists artistic, rhythmic, trampoline, DMT, tumbling, acrobatic, aerobic, TeamGym, disability and recreational gymnastics. Awards, coaching supervision, filming guidance and participation figures were not found on the pages read.

props.name: Skateboard GB / Skateboard England, FAQs
props.note: Read. Always wear a helmet; pads and guards recommended while learning. Learn to balance and push before tricks. Coaches should hold the Skateboard GB Level 1 qualification, be DBS-checked and safeguarding-trained. About 750,000 people skateboarded in some form in the UK in 2020; over 1,600 UK skateparks; many indoor parks run girls' nights.

props.name: Serrien B, Witterzeel E, Baeyens J-P 2018, The uncontrolled manifold concept reveals that the structure of postural control in recurve archery shooting is related to accuracy, J Funct Morphol Kinesiol 3(3):48
props.note: Read in part. 6 national-team recurve archers, 90 shots at 18 m. Accurate shots showed better-coordinated arm joints during aiming; simple marker consistency did not separate accuracy in elite archers (cited).

props.name: Waddell DB, Gowitzke BA, Biomechanical principles applied to badminton power strokes (ISBS proceedings)
props.note: Read. Narrative review. The power stroke takes about a tenth of a second; forearm pronation is the key action; contact is late in the unweighting phase of a jump smash.

props.name: World Netball, Rules of Netball (2024 edition)
props.note: Rules 1 to 18.12 read verbatim (copy hosted by Netball Hamilton); Rules 18.13 onward, 19 and 21 seen only in a summary. Court 30.5 x 15.25 m in three thirds; goal circle radius 4.9 m; post 3.05 m; ring internal diameter 380 mm; ball 690-710 mm, 400-450 g. Seven positions (GS, GA, WA, C, WD, GD, GK) with set playing areas. Footwork (Rule 13): after a one-foot landing a player may step, pivot or jump but must pass or shoot before regrounding the landing foot; no dragging, sliding or hopping. Pass or shoot within 3 seconds (11.4, 9.6b). Defenders keep 0.9 m from the landing foot of the player with the ball (Rule 16). Contact that interferes is penalised (Rule 17). Only GS and GA shoot, from inside the goal circle (Rule 9). No piercings; short nails; hair tied back (3.12). No effective date found in the text.

props.name: Huang T-Y, Hamill J, Yang H, Tang W-T 2024, Upper-limb joint kinematics analysis of accuracy dart throwing at different vertical targets between different level dart players, J Hum Sport Exerc 19(3):722-736
props.note: Read. 8 advanced and 8 intermediate players, 200 Hz motion capture. Shoulder elevation changed only about 6.5-7 deg during the throw and the shoulder rose about 6-10 mm; elbow straightened about 59-62 deg, from a bend of about 69-72 deg at release; dart speed about 5.8-6.1 m/s. Advanced players rotated the shoulder much less at release (about 44-53 vs 94-133 deg/s) and snapped the wrist faster.

props.name: Lin C-W, Su F-C, Lin C-F 2019, Kinematic analysis of postural stability during ballet turns (pirouettes) in experienced and novice dancers, Front Bioeng Biotechnol 7:290
props.note: Read in part. 13 experienced and 13 novice girls and young women, single pirouettes en dehors. Maximum forward tilt during the turn about 5.4 deg (experienced) vs 7.2 deg (novice); tilt varied about 1.4 vs 2.6 deg in the ending; novices overshot in preparation and kept adjusting on landing.

props.name: Paddle UK, Watersports Participation Survey shows growth in paddlesports (2025 survey)
props.note: Read. Paddlesports participation 24% of UK adults, up from 18% in 2023; 16-34 year olds most active; nearly one in ten reported difficulty in open water; formal training linked to safer behaviour. No split by craft or sex on this page.

props.name: Giustino V and colleagues 2024, Kinematic analysis of the back squat at different load intensities in powerlifters and weightlifters, Front Sports Act Living 6:1454309
props.note: Read in part. 17 experienced lifters (12 men, 5 women), low-bar squat filmed side-on at 60 fps with free software. As load rose, the hips flexed slightly less at the bottom and ascent speed fell; knee and ankle angles at the bottom did not change. Shows a single side-on phone camera is a workable method.

props.name: Brown SR, Brughelli M, Hume P 2015, Carrying a ball can influence sidestepping mechanics in rugby, ISBS 2015 pp. 543-546
props.note: Abstract read. 18 male rugby players, 45 deg side-steps: carrying a ball increased knee and hip adduction (about 15-18%).

props.name: BaseballSoftballUK, Baseball5 (2026)
props.note: Read. Two teams of five; no equipment beyond a rubber ball; BSUK develops Baseball5 in the UK, with the first games in 2019. No schools figures given.

props.name: Hong Kong Education Bureau, Baseball5 rules infographic (based on the 2024 rulebook)
props.note: Read. School PE resource: hit with a fist or palm; younger age groups get a second chance after an illegal hit or foul ball.

props.name: Independent Coach Education, Rounders England launches values-based curriculum to support schools
props.note: Read. KS2 and KS3 curriculum resources (running, sending, receiving, striking, gameplay); Ready Rounders for ages 7-11 (triangular pitch, rotating positions). Rounders England describes rounders as a cross-generational, mixed-gender game for all abilities.

props.name: Koga A, Bai X, Jia Y, Liu J 2025, Lower limb biomechanical differences between jumps with different number of rotations in youth figure skaters, Front Bioeng Biotechnol 13:1606817
props.note: Read. 11 youth skaters about 12 years (8 girls). Waltz jump: take-off knee about 162 deg, landing knee about 124 deg (about 56 deg of bend), landing hip about 108 deg, flight about 0.36 s, height about 0.18 m, take-off vertical speed 1.8 m/s. Single Axel: flight 0.40 s, height 0.24 m. Jump distance fell as rotations rose. Text and table disagree on one flight-time comparison.

props.name: Athletics Canada, World Para Athletics rules summary for officials (October 2023, from WPA rules February 2023)
props.note: Read; no rule numbers. Wheelchair racing: helmet compulsory in all events and whenever on the track, including warm-up; at 'Set' both hands on the push rim and still; steering and braking must work; no part of the chair behind the rear tyres; the overtaking athlete is responsible for clearance and the overtaken athlete must not obstruct. Seated throws: the ischial tuberosity must not leave the seat; officials do not transfer or strap athletes; one assistant for F31-33 and F51-54; six attempts. Universal relay: two men and two women across four impairment groups. Class groups: T/F11-13 vision, T/F20 intellectual, T33-34 and T51-54 wheelchair racing, T/F35-38 coordination, T42-47 and T61-64 limb impairment, F31-34 and F51-57 seated throws.

props.name: Thomas & Yen 2025, Influence of three drills on pelvic motion in the baseball swing: a pilot study, Asian J Sports Med 16(3):e164794
props.note: Read. 9 NCAA D1 men: at contact pelvic rotation 75.5 +/- 2.7 deg (79.6 after a back-ball drill); hand-pelvis distance 47.8 +/- 1.2 cm (50.7 after a step-down drill).

props.name: World Athletics Age Group Specifications (hosted by Scottish Athletics, January 2026)
props.note: Read. Age groups U12, U14, U16, U18, U20 and senior. Implement masses and hurdle heights by age and sex (copied into graph.yaml formats). Shot: girls 2-2.72 / 2.72 / 3 / 3 / 4 kg; boys 2-2.72 / 3 / 4 / 5 / 6 / 7.26 kg. Discus, javelin, hammer and hurdle heights also listed.

props.name: World Lacrosse, Women's Field Officiating Manual v1.0 (11 February 2024)
props.note: About a third read verbatim, the rest in a summary. Officials watch whether a shooter touches or steps over the goal-circle line on a shot; defenders may stay in the goal circle up to 5 seconds; shooting space, dangerous shot, dangerous propel and checks toward the head are major fouls.

props.name: Junior Darts Corporation, Safeguarding and Courses pages
props.note: Read. JDC runs junior tours, competitions and community academies for under-18s; DBS checks and yearly safeguarding training; an academy coaching certificate and a venue and coach accreditation programme (no content published). No technique content or age bands.

props.name: Charles University bachelor thesis 2023, Effect of shooting technique on accuracy and ball velocity in floorball players
props.note: Abstract read. 2 male and 2 female top youth players; drag, wrist, 'golf' and slap shots at a 4 m target: ball speeds differed between techniques, the golf (full swing) shot being fastest.

props.name: Reid, Elliott & Crespo 2013, Mechanics and learning practices associated with the tennis forehand: a review, J Sports Sci Med 12(2):225-231
props.licence: CC licence (page label and link differ); facts only
props.note: Mature backswing: hips about 90 deg and shoulders about 110 deg to the baseline, shoulder-pelvis separation 20-30 deg; about 90% of advanced forehands use an open stance. Elbow angle and impact-height values seen only as a summary.

props.name: McCabe C 2008, Effects of 50 m and 400 m race paces on three-dimensional kinematics and linear kinetics of sprint and distance front crawl swimmers (PhD thesis, University of Edinburgh)
props.note: Read in part. 15 national and international men; stroke length, stroke frequency, stroke index, speed and phase durations all change between sprint and distance pace. Results chapter not read; literature values seen only in a summary are not used.

props.name: Lozowski, Atack & Mahaffey 2021, Kinematic attributes associated with overarm throwing performance in cricket (ISBS Proceedings 39)
props.note: Abstract only: 16 cricketers; vertical release angle, stride length, trunk flexion velocity and forward trunk tilt at release predicted throw speed; horizontal release angle predicted accuracy; straight approach quickest.

props.name: Baker ML, Epari DR, Lorenzetti S et al. 2017, Knee injury risk factors in golf: a systematic review, Sports Med 47:2621-2639
props.note: Read in part. Lead knee flexion at the top of the backswing 35 +/- 5 deg in men vs 17 +/- 6 deg in women (cited study); the lead knee takes more load than the trail knee. Used to avoid a single knee target across sexes; never used to predict injury.

props.name: Koshida S, Ishii T, Matsuda T, Hashimoto T 2015, Biomechanics of judo breakfall for osoto-gari in adolescent judokas (33rd ISBS Conference, Poitiers)
props.note: Read. 5 adolescent boys vs adult data. Neck flexion rises to about 15-20 deg and drops sharply at the end of the fall; head moments did not differ from adults. Used for structure only; never to predict injury.

props.name: Couceiro M, Dias G, Araujo D et al. 2022, The re-organization of action in golf putting under different task constraints, J Men's Health 18(1):26
props.note: Read. 10 skilled right-handed men (handicap 2.3), 30 putts at each of 1-4 m, 100 Hz putter sensor. Backswing 569-604 ms; downswing 276-328 ms (shorter for longer putts); face angle at impact -0.04 to -0.51 deg; cites a 270-370 ms downswing band linked with success. Backswing:downswing ratio 1.8-2.2 is our calculation from the table means.

props.name: British Tenpin Bowling Association, About Youth Bowling England
props.note: Read. Youth Bowling England was set up within the BTBA in March 2020, with youth bowling clubs, a youth tour and Youth Team England; club coaches are BTBA-licensed and insured. No age groups or participation figures stated.

props.name: IBSA Goalball Rules and Regulations 2025 (v1.0, 1 January 2025)
props.note: Read verbatim to about Rule 25, the rest in summary. Court 18 x 9 m in six 3 m areas: Team Area (orientation and landing areas), neutral area; lines taped over string for orientation by touch (1.4). Goals 9 m wide, 1.3 m high. Ball 1.25 kg with bells. Three players a side, two 12-minute halves. All players on court wear eyeshades for the whole half (6.2), touching them only with the referee's permission (13.3); eye patches at sanctioned championships (6.4). Sport class B1, B2 or B3 for IBSA competition (7.2). High ball: the ball must touch the court on or before the high ball line at the front of the thrower's Team Area (24.1). Long ball: it must also touch the neutral area (25.1, partly summary). Ten seconds from first defensive contact to get the ball over the centre line (31, summary). Illegal defence: first defensive contact must be by a player with part of the body in their Team Area (27, summary). Padding no more than 10 cm from the body (5.6).
