props.name: British Ice Skating, Skate UK Fundamental Skills levels 1-8
props.note: Read. For all ages; eight levels with adapted versions for disabled skaters. Level 1: marching, sit and stand, two-foot glide with a dip, snowplough stops. Level 2: curves, T-stop, backward marching, two-foot turns, lemons. Level 3: forward stroking with a correct push and glide, backward snowplough stop, one-foot glides on inside and outside edges. Level 4: chassés, backward stroking, 3-second forward edge glides, two-foot three-turn. Assistants must be over 16 and trained.

props.name: Yu J, Li M, Chen Z 2025, Comparative study on bilateral lower extremity joint mechanics and muscle synergy patterns in Axel jumps between elite and amateur single skaters, Front Bioeng Biotechnol 13:1639807
props.note: Read. 16 male skaters (8 elite, 8 amateur), double Axel. Elite skaters showed less hip flexion and abduction on one side and fewer muscle synergies. Literature cited: triple Axel rotation up to about 5 rev/s.

props.name: Millour G, Duc S, Puel F, Bertucci W 2019, Comparison of static and dynamic methods based on knee kinematics to determine optimal saddle height in cycling, Acta Bioeng Biomech 21(4)
props.note: Read. 26 male cyclists aged 9-53 (8 children, 18 adults), 2D video at 60 Hz, 80 rpm. Knee flexion at bottom dead centre: 30 +/- 9 deg static vs 38 +/- 5 deg while pedalling (adults 38 +/- 4; children 40 +/- 6). Proposes 33-43 deg at bottom dead centre during pedalling, vs the static 25-35 deg rule.

props.name: IFF news, Study on the use of protective eyewear published in Finland (7 May 2021)
props.note: Read. 4,860 adult players surveyed: two-thirds rarely or never wore eyewear (fogging the main reason); women wore it more; about a quarter had had an eye injury. Finland requires approved eyewear for younger players in official matches; IFF recommends member associations make it mandatory.

props.name: Middleton K, Webster K, Birse S, McClelland J 2020, Frontal plane alignment during forehand and backhand lawn bowls deliveries, ISBS Proceedings Archive 38(1):121
props.note: Read. 18 international bowlers (12 men, 6 women), draws to a jack at 27 m, 20-camera motion capture. At release: trunk lateral flexion about 30 deg (forehand) and 19 deg (backhand); pelvis obliquity 19 and 12 deg; backhand delivered more upright; arm angles the same on both hands.

props.name: AFL, Coaching Tackle Curriculum (2024)
props.note: Read. Tackling taught in stages: none at U8, wrap tackle from U9, full tackling from U11; cues get low, body on body, head safe. Used only to describe tackling, which has no protocol.

props.name: British Dodgeball, Status Report 2019 (from Sport England Active Lives and other surveys)
props.note: Read. 613,000 children aged 5-16 (8.7%) played in the last week; 2nd most-played team sport in schools; occasional adult players about 41% female; a third of children wanted to play more dodgeball.

props.name: Parrington L, Ball K, MacMahon C 2012, Square to the target? Coaching cues and technical analysis of the Australian football handball, ISBS 2012
props.note: Read. 4 elite men, 8 handballs each at a 5 m target. Hits vs misses: pelvis about 15-16 deg and shoulders 22-23 deg from square (little difference); fist path closer to straight at the target in hits (about 83 vs 78 deg; moderate effect, not significant); misses had slightly higher fist speed.

props.name: Federation of International Touch, Playing Rules 5th Edition (England Touch copy)
props.note: Read. Field 70 x 50 m plus 7 m in-goals; 6 on the field; mixed teams have at most 3 men and at least 1 woman on the field (5.4); two 20-minute halves. A touch needs only minimum force; excess force is misconduct. Six touches then changeover. Rollball (13.1): standing on the mark facing the opponents' try line, place the ball between the feet and step over it, roll it back no more than 1 m or pass a foot over it, without delay, on the mark. Defenders retire 7 m at a rollball and 10 m at a tap. No forward pass, knock or throw (11.1). Tap: ball placed on the mark, released, tapped with the foot and moved no more than 1 m.

props.name: The FA heading guidance and youth heading chart; Blyth et al. 2025 review
props.note: U12 limits differ between two FA pages; confirm with The FA

props.name: Sanders, Felton & King 2018, Kinematic parameters contributing to the production of spin in elite finger spin bowling, J Sports Sci
props.note: Read. 23 elite male finger spinners: spin 1,685 +/- 170 rpm; pelvis-shoulder separation at front-foot contact 20.9 +/- 9.8 deg (r=0.52 with spin); pelvis orientation at FFC and release best predictors; elbow extension 3.65 +/- 3.24 deg (max 10.5); front knee flexes 9.5 +/- 17 deg FFC to release, not related to spin.

props.name: IKF, Rule 6.3: to shoot from a defended position (web page)
props.note: Read. A shot is defended when a defender is actively trying to block the ball, is within arm's length, is nearer the post than the attacker and faces the attacker; exceptions for jumping shots and play at the post.

props.name: Kong PW, Pan JW, Chu DPK, Cheung PM, Lau PWC 2021, Acquiring expertise in precision sport: what can we learn from an elite snooker player? Physical Activity and Health 5(1):98-106
props.note: Abstract read. 1 elite man; cueing is mainly elbow bend and straighten with little wrist; practice strokes and the final stroke follow almost the same path; slight lean onto the front foot.

props.name: Bergamini E et al. 2015, Wheelchair propulsion biomechanics in junior basketball players: a method for the evaluation of the efficacy of a specific training program, BioMed Res Int 2015:275965
props.note: Read. 12 junior players (10 boys, 2 girls), 20 m sprint: push cycle about 0.47 s (about 114 pushes a minute) and left-right symmetry about 49%; training raised push frequency and force.

props.name: USA Hockey Official Playing Rules: 2011-13 rule change summary (Rule 604, body checking classifications)
props.note: Read. Rule 604 prohibits body checking in the 12-and-under classification (Progressive Checking Skill Development Program); no body check may be delivered in a non-checking classification. Dated and superseded; the current rule book was not read.

props.name: Steele JR, Furze L 1994, Effect of match play on the kinematics of one-handed stationary netball shooting, ISBS 1994 proceedings
props.note: Read. 10 highly skilled state-league shooters (sex not stated), defended standing shot from 3.0 m, 100 Hz side view. At the end of knee flexion: knee angle 125 +/- 13 deg (range 97-149), elbow 86 +/- 15 deg, shoulder 147 +/- 16 deg. Trunk moved only about 3 deg from the crouch to release. No change after a match.

props.name: RFU, Under 8s rules (tag rugby; club copy, 2025)
props.note: Read. Up to 6 a side on at most 45 x 22 m; tags 38 x 5 cm, one over each hip; the ball carrier may not fend off or guard the tags; pass within 3 seconds or about 3 strides; at most 6 tags per possession; no tackling, contact or kicking; forward pass gives a free pass.

props.name: World Surf League, Surf judging explained
props.note: Read; undated. Same five criteria; speed, power and flow are the main pillars, judged against the day's conditions; manoeuvres on the steepest part of the wave and varied combinations score higher.

props.name: British Weight Lifting, Technical and Competition Rules and Regulations 2025 (based on the IWF rules; in effect from August 2025)
props.note: Read. Snatch: one movement from the platform to full arm extension overhead, splitting or squatting, finishing with arms and legs extended. Clean and jerk: one movement to the shoulders, then motionless before the jerk. Faults for all lifts: pulling from the hang, touching the platform with anything but the feet, pausing during arm extension, finishing with a press-out, bending and re-extending the elbows during recovery, uneven or incomplete arm extension, not finishing with feet and bar in line, knees not fully extended. Age groups: development under 12 (under 10, under 12), youth 13-17, junior 15-20.

props.name: Hanley B, Thomas AL, Tucker CB 2022, Spatiotemporal and joint kinematic differences between footstrike patterns in male and female 10,000 m athletes, ISBS Proceedings 40:263-266
props.note: Read. 53 men and 33 women, European 10,000 m Cup 2021, lap 15. Cadence 3.04-3.19 Hz; contact 0.179-0.203 s; knee at initial contact 154-158 deg; hip-ankle distance at contact 0.22-0.27 m; no speed, step length or cadence difference between foot-strike groups; rearfoot strikers had longer contacts. Longer hip-ankle distance went with faster speed in women (r = 0.58): foot-ahead is not a fault in itself.

props.name: Freitas et al. 2025, Kinematic and neuromuscular responses to different visual focus conditions in stand-up paddleboarding, PeerJ 13:e19362
props.note: Read. 14 recreational men on calm water, video in Kinovea: stroke frequency 0.52-0.65 Hz (about 31-39 a minute), stroke length about 1.7-1.9 m; looking freely ahead gave the highest speed and stroke frequency, compared with looking at the board nose.

props.name: Pavlasová K, Bizovská L, Gába A, Farana R, Janura M 2025, Biomechanics of landing in gymnasts: a scoping review, Frontiers in Sports and Active Living 7:1602058
props.note: Read in part. 8 studies, 212 participants aged 8-25. Cites a knee bend above about 63 deg as a soft landing and below it as a stiff landing; female gymnasts land more upright.

props.name: Fu, Cobley, Sanders 2022, (coordination of overarm throwing in early adolescents), Scand J Med Sci Sports 32(12):1747-1756
props.note: Read in part. Year 7 pupils: skilled throwers sequenced pelvis, trunk, shoulder and elbow in order; boys were over-represented in the skilled group, so girls need more practice opportunity rather than different targets.

props.name: School Games (Manchester Schools PE), Tag Rugby Rules (Years 7-8)
props.note: Read. 8 on the pitch; two Velcro tags worn outside the shirt; only the ball carrier can be tagged; pass within 3 seconds of a tag; tagger holds the tag up and stands back; no diving over the line; no scrums, kicks or line-outs.

props.name: Scottish Disability Sport, Boccia violation summary (2025 update, World Boccia rules 2025-2028)
props.note: Read. Retraction if a ball is released before the colour indication or before the jack, or two balls at once; athletes must be seated with at least one buttock on the seat at release; nothing may touch the court outside the athlete's own box at release; the ramp may not overhang the throwing line; BC3 must swing the ramp at least 20 cm left and right before the jack, penalty balls and tie-breaks; penalty if a ramp operator looks into play; seat height above 66 cm (BC1, BC2, BC4) is penalised. Individual events split by gender; pairs need one man and one woman.

props.name: Fu Y-C, Dabbs NC, Garner JC 2015, Comparison of linear and angular swing velocities with differently weighted warm-up bats in softball players, ISBS 2015 pp. 588-591
props.note: Read. 10 female college softball players: peak bat-end speed about 24.7 m/s, about 0.3 s from start to peak. Softball, not rounders.

props.name: US Youth Soccer Skills School Manual (2017)
Klous M, Müller E, Schwameder H 2007, Lower extremity joint loading in carved ski and snowboard turns, ISBS 2007
props.note: Read. 2 skiers and 2 snowboarders. The outside ski leg carried far more load than the inside leg through the turn; snowboard front and rear legs shared load more evenly; knee range was larger in skiing than in snowboarding.

props.name: Ringette Canada officials, Rule fundamentals: Ringette 101 (rules version 2024)
props.note: Read. A 6-inch rubber ring and straight sticks with a specialised tip; ring carriers may not carry the ring from one zone to another; 30-second shot clock; no intentional body contact; stoppages restart with a free pass or goalkeeper ring.

props.name: Ball K 2012, Application of biomechanical kicking research, ISBS 2012 pp. 79-82
props.note: Read. Elite Australian footballers' punt kicks (closest studied kick to the Gaelic kick from the hands): foot speed about 22 vs 19 m/s (preferred vs non-preferred); support knee bent about 22 deg at foot strike, about 49 deg at most and about 41-43 deg at ball contact. Less support-knee bend went with faster feet.

props.name: Sinclair J, Taylor PJ, Shadwell G and colleagues 2022, Two-experiment examination of habitual and manipulated foot placement angles on the kinetics, kinematics and muscle forces of the barbell back squat in male lifters, Sensors 22:6999
props.note: Read. 70 male lifters, high-bar back squat at a moderate load, 3D motion capture. Peak trunk lean about 29-31 deg, hip flexion about 95-100 deg, knee flexion about 118-122 deg, knees travelling forward about 44-48% of shank length; foot angle made little difference.

props.name: Concept2 New Zealand, Understanding rowing technique: the recovery sequence (23 February 2018)
props.note: Read. Recovery arms, body, legs; legs stay down until the handle passes the knees; a common guide is about 1 s on the drive to 2 s on the recovery; at high rates the hands leave the finish at the speed they came in.

props.name: Pletcher et al. 2025, Measures of joint kinematic reliability during repeated softball pitching, Biomechanics 5(1):3
props.note: Read in part. 14 female high-school and college pitchers: stride knee and drive knee angles are the most reliable (ICC up to 0.99), pitching elbow the least (CV 27%). Mean angles (stride knee about 77 deg) seen only in a summary.

props.name: Association of British Climbing Walls, Code of Practice (BMC-approved)
props.note: Read. A minimum standard for all walls: users told the risks (BMC participation statement); risk assessments cover child protection; novices supervised by a competent person; safety induction recommended before unsupervised bouldering; impact surfaces fit for purpose; instruction by appropriately qualified instructors.

props.name: Tran & Silverberg 2008, Optimal release conditions for the free throw in men's basketball, J Sports Sci 26(11):1147-55
props.note: Not opened. Optimum about 52 degrees, about 3 Hz backspin, aim at the back of the rim; release height worth about 5% accuracy per 0.152 m above 2.0 m (all as cited by B2, B3 and B4).

props.name: Okazaki & Rodacki 2012, Increased distance of shooting on basketball jump shot, J Sports Sci Med 11:231-237
props.licence: CC licence (page says BY-NC-ND); facts only
props.note: 10 expert males. With distance, release height fell (2.46 to 2.33 m), release speed rose (4.39 to 6.89 m/s) and release angle fell; elbow, knee and trunk at release did not change significantly. Joint-angle tables not read.

props.name: Fong Yan A, Smith RM, Hiller C, Sinclair PJ 2013, Kinematic changes in a dance jump landing due to different shoes, ISB Congress 2013
props.note: Read. 16 trained female dancers, sautés in second position. Peak knee bend on landing was over 60 deg in every shoe condition.

props.name: Kobayashi Y, Ae M, Miyazaki A, Fujii N, Iiboshi A, A biomechanical study on improvement in the overarm throwing technique of elementary school children, ISBS proceedings pp. 614-617
props.note: Read. 32 twelve-year-olds: three 45-minute lessons improved throw distance (boys 28 to 32 m, girls 16 to 17 m); the improved thrower had the shoulder abducted about 90 deg.

props.name: FIVB Official Volleyball Rules 2025-2028 (French edition, v04), approved by the 39th FIVB World Congress 2024, for competitions starting after 1 January 2025
props.note: Read verbatim to rule 4.3 only (translated from French). Court 18 x 9 m with a free zone of at least 3 m; attack line 3 m from the centre line; net 2.43 m (men) and 2.24 m (women); up to 12 players on the match sheet (14 in FIVB senior competitions); three team touches plus the block contact. Scoring, service, attack-hit, libero, block and net rules were only seen in a machine summary and are not used for rule metrics (gap VB-03). The English edition could not be fetched.

props.name: Samsudin M 2024, Analisis teknik floorball slap shoot: berbasis 2D analisis biomekanika (S1 thesis, Universitas Pendidikan Indonesia)
props.note: Abstract read. 12 provincial-level men, slap shots: facing the ball rather than the goal gave higher ball speed; pelvic angle was the main factor (hip-flexion values to verify in the full text).

props.name: Concept2 New Zealand, Understanding rowing technique: catch, drive and finish (12 February 2018)
props.note: Read. Drive sequence legs, body, arms; using the back and arms early interrupts the leg drive; the body takes over at about 80% leg extension; finish with a strong core, hip angle about 100 deg, handle drawn to the chest; light, quick catch; neck tall, shoulders down.

props.name: Peploe 2016, The kinematics of batting against fast bowling in cricket (PhD thesis, Loughborough University)
props.note: Partly read: 31 batters, forward drive and pull; longest hitters show more front-elbow extension, wrist uncocking and pelvis-thorax separation; cites stance width 0.46 +/- 0.08 m in international batsmen. Result chapters not reached.

props.name: SportsPose dataset (Technical University of Denmark)
props.licence: custom academic licence; no commercial use
props.note: 176k 3D poses, 24 subjects, 5 activities (sports not confirmed). Benchmarking only.

props.name: Dos'Santos et al. 2018, The angle-velocity trade-off in change of direction, Sports Med
Kong PW, Pan JW, Komar J, Yang C 2021, Shot performance and cue stick kinematics of top spin shots in cue sports players of various playing levels, ISBS Proceedings 39(1):49-52
props.note: Read. 25 men (13 skilled, 12 less skilled), 10 top-spin shots each. Cue tip speed about 1.0-1.3 m/s; cue angle at impact under 4 deg for everyone; the only significant difference was shot-to-shot variability of the error (4.7 vs 6.5 cm).

props.name: England Lacrosse, Statement on personal equipment (5 February 2020; copy on a club website)
props.note: Read. All players in men's, women's, mixed and indoor lacrosse must wear an approved mouthguard at all times in a game and remove jewellery. Eyewear and headgear are not mentioned. Not on an England Lacrosse domain; check against the official site.

props.name: Glasgow Ultimate, Introduction to Ultimate: lessons 1 and 2
props.note: Read (lessons 1 and 2). Backhand: show the back of the hand to the receiver, snap the wrist rather than swing the arm, low flat throws with spin. Forehand: hips and chest facing the receiver, step wide and sink into the pivot, push the elbow forward and flick the wrist; faults include swinging across the body and a side-on stance. Always catch with two hands; clap catch preferred. Travel includes running with the disc or dragging the pivot. Beginners play 3-4 a side, then 5 a side; mixed play is common; stall 10 s outdoors, 8 s indoors.

props.name: World Darts Federation, Playing and Tournament Rules (20th revised edition, 28 February 2018)
props.note: Read. Darts at most 30.5 cm long and 50 g, thrown one at a time by and from the hand, three per throw (1.01-1.03). Bull centre 1.73 m above the floor; oche 38 mm high and 610 mm long; 2.37 m horizontal to the board face, 2.93 m diagonal (6.01-6.03). Feet must stay behind the oche and behind its imaginary extension when throwing from the side; first breach a warning, then darts thrown in breach do not score (6.04-6.06). Straight start, double finish, bust rule, bull 50, outer bull 25. Member bodies may change board height and oche length for disabled players' events (6.08). Youth events limited by age; ranked events smoke-free, no alcohol in the playing area.

props.name: IFAF, Flag Football Rules 2017
props.note: About half read verbatim. 5 v 5, non-contact; field 50 yd plus two 10 yd end zones, 25 yd wide; two 20-minute halves. Two flags, one on each hip, never covered; shirts tucked in. Flag guarding: covering the flag with a hand, elbow, leg or ball, diving or stretching a hand towards the defender. Rushers start 7 yd from the line with a hand raised. Quarterback has 7 seconds to pass and may not run past the line unless the ball changed hands. Ball carrier is down on a flag pull or when a knee or other body part touches the ground.

props.name: NBA stats glossary and play-type names
props.note: Not opened; used for skill names and aliases only.

props.name: World Pool-Billiard Association, Rules of Play (effective 21 October 2026)
props.note: Read verbatim to Section 2.14, rest in summary. Games include 8-ball, 9-ball, 10-ball, 14.1 straight pool and blackball. Fouls include no foot on the floor at the moment the tip strikes the cue ball (3.4), double hit (3.7) and push shot (3.8). A referee may impose a shot clock for slow play (3.14). No age or junior rules.

props.name: WPBSA, Official Rules of the Games of Snooker and English Billiards (revised May 2022)
props.note: Snooker Sections 1-3 read verbatim. Playing area 3569 x 1778 mm (11 ft 8.5 in x 5 ft 10 in), balls 52.5 mm, cue at least 914 mm. Reds 1, colours 2-7 (147 maximum break follows). A stroke is made with the tip only, struck once and not pushed. Fouls include striking with both feet off the floor (wheelchair players exempt), push strokes, jump shots, striking the cue ball more than once, and touching a ball in play with the body, clothing or equipment. Snooker Shootout uses a shot clock (seen only in summary).

props.name: Labbe et al. 2025, Kinematic sequencing of the football pass using inertial motion analysis, Int J Sports Phys Ther 20(8):1214-1221
props.note: Reused from sport 06. 8 male high-school and college quarterbacks: stride knee 29-46 deg peaking at release; shoulder abduction peak 112 deg; trunk side-bend 2-9 deg away from the throwing arm. Tackle football with a full-size ball.

props.name: MCC Laws of Cricket (2017 Code), Law 21 No ball
props.note: Page body not retrieved; the same wording was read in G2 (ICC clause 21 follows Law 21).

props.name: Manchester Schools PE, Rounders Rules: Primary (2017)
props.note: Read. Primary competition: squad of 15, 9 play, 6-minute innings, at least 2 bowlers; half a rounder for each no-ball; batters wait in a safe area behind the batting square; a batter who drops the bat is out.

props.name: MLB and USA Baseball Pitch Smart guidelines for youth and adolescent pitchers
props.licence: MLB Advanced Media, all rights reserved; facts only
props.note: Read. Daily max pitches: 9-10 75, 11-12 85, 13-14 95, 15-16 95, 17-18 105, with rest days by count (e.g. ages 9-14: 1-20 pitches no rest, 21-35 one day, 36-50 two, 51-65 three, 66+ four). No pitching three days in a row; at least 4 months off throwing a year; avoid catching while not pitching; breaking balls only after a consistent fastball and changeup (13-14).

props.name: Atack A, Trewartha G, Bezodis N, Support leg mechanics in rugby place kicking (conference abstract, St Mary's University repository)
props.note: Read. 33 experienced kickers, 240 Hz. The support leg mostly absorbs energy through contact; inaccurate kickers did more hip-extensor work early in support. No position or angle values.

props.name: Seifert L, Orth D, Boulanger J, Dovgalecs V, Hérault R, Davids K 2014, Climbing skill and complexity of climbing wall design: assessment of jerk as a novel indicator of performance fluency, J Appl Biomech 30(5):619-625
props.note: Read (author PDF). 6 intermediate climbers (about 21 years, grade 6a), 10 m top-rope routes over four sessions. Hip jerk (less smooth movement) was higher on the harder route and fell with practice; exploratory hold touches fell from 9 to 3 on the harder route across sessions.

props.name: Wikipedia, Cheerleading in the United Kingdom
props.note: Read in part. SportCheer UK is the ICU-recognised body; over 89,000 athletes in the UK (BBC 2023); about 37% of schools offer cheer. Age grid: Tiny 3-6, Mini 5-8, Youth 7-11, Junior 8-14, Senior 11+, Open 17+; all-girl and co-ed divisions; dance styles pom, jazz, hip hop, lyrical.

props.name: Skateboard GB, Skatepark etiquette
props.note: Read (introduction only; the poster is an image that could not be read). Describes an unwritten code of conduct at skateparks.

props.name: NFL UK, Get involved with NFL Flag UK and Ireland
props.note: Read (undated). NFL Flag is the main form of the game in UK and Irish schools; '120,000 people and over 1000 schools'; free teacher training and equipment packs; BAFA runs youth leagues.

props.name: Kim K, Cho J, Choi H, Song J 2025, Bow stability and postural sway during aiming and shooting in elite compound archery, Sports Biomechanics 24(8):2205-2218
props.note: Read (abstract). International compound archers: less bow movement and less body sway while aiming went with better accuracy; after release, sway did not relate to accuracy and the authors favour a smooth, consistent follow-through.

props.name: Millar S 2004, Kinematics of drop punt kicking in Australian Rules football: comparison of skilled and less skilled kicking, MAppSc thesis, Victoria University
props.note: Read in part. 6 skilled vs 6 less-skilled elite players: groups differed in timing rather than the size of angles; skilled kickers had a firmer (more pointed) foot at contact; knee bent about 30-50 deg at contact.

props.name: Opta event definitions; Wyscout glossary; StatsBomb open-data spec
WPBSA, Coaching qualifications and levels; Junior snooker; Women's snooker (web pages)
props.note: Read. Three coaching levels: Level 1 WPBSA Snooker Coach (one day, basics, includes child protection training), 1st4sport Level 2 (novice and intermediate players), Level 3 (advanced, from 2020). World Women's Snooker is open to women and girls of all ages, with over 170 players from about 30 countries, and its tour is a qualification route to the World Snooker Tour. The EPSB runs junior events down to under-14 and a Junior Elite Performance Programme.

props.name: Hamdan N, Suwarganda E, Wilson B 2012, Factors correlated with sepak takraw serve speed, ISBS Proceedings 30:413-416
props.note: Read. 7 Malaysian national players, 50 Hz video and radar: serve speed about 18.3 m/s; ball contact about 2.2 m high (within-player variation only 2-4%); foot speed about 11.7 m/s; higher contact went with lower ball speed in 6 of 7 players; technique should be individualised.

props.name: Koshida S, Matsuda T, Ishii T, Hashimoto T, Kinematics of judo backward breakfall: comparison between novice and experienced judokas (ISBS proceedings)
props.note: Read. 11 experienced and 13 novice university men. Knee and trunk-flexion patterns differed (experienced extend the knee faster); head, neck and hip kinematics did not; neck flexion peaks at about 40% of the fall.

props.name: News On AIR, 1st edition of Kho Kho World Cup begins in Delhi (13 January 2025)
props.note: Read. Confirms the first edition in New Delhi; says teams from 20 countries (conflicts with G4's 23).

props.name: International Floorball Federation, Rules of the Game 2026 (valid from 1 July 2026)
props.note: Read verbatim to rule 502, rest in summary. Rink 40 x 20 m; up to six on the rink (five field players and a goalkeeper without a stick); 3 x 20 minutes; stick blade hook at most 30 mm. In summary: raising the stick blade above waist height in the backswing or follow-through is a free hit (507.3); playing the ball above knee height is a free hit (507.4); hitting, lifting or kicking an opponent's stick, kicking the ball dangerously, playing with the head and playing while on both knees or a hand are fouls; only shoulder-to-shoulder pushing is allowed. Preface: IFF advises protective goggles should be mandatory under 17 and recommended under 19; goggles must be IFF-marked (405.2).

props.name: Ferrer-Roca V, Roig A, Galilea P, Garcia-Lopez J 2012, Influence of saddle height on lower limb kinematics in well-trained cyclists: static versus dynamic evaluation in bike fitting, J Strength Cond Res 26(11):3025-3029
props.note: Read. 23 high-level male road cyclists. Recommended saddle height 106-109% of inseam was missed by 56.5%; dynamic knee angle 30-40 deg at maximum extension suggested; proposes 108.6-110.4% of inseam. Bibliographic details taken from a citing paper.

props.name: Curling Canada, Summary of rule changes 2022-2026
props.note: Read. Sweeping must not leave debris in front of a moving stone and the final motion finishes outside its path; stick, wheelchair and vision-impaired rules are in separate sections (not read).

props.name: Ibrahim R, Faber GS, Kingma I, van Dieen JH 2017, Kinematic analysis of the drag flick in field hockey, Sports Biomech 16(1):45-57
props.note: Read (abstract). 10 elite players, 150 Hz. A near proximal-to-distal sequence; trunk axial rotation and lateral bend towards the target and the wrists were the main contributors to stick speed.

props.name: Surfing England, home page, Coaching Hub and Surf Coach Progression Award (2026)
props.note: Read. National governing body recognised by Sport England, UK Sport and the ISA. Surf Instructor qualification; Surf Coach Progression Award (needs a Level 1 instructor qualification and a lifeguard qualification); Inclusive Coaching course in development; national coach register from 2028. Junior Surf Series 2026 and U12/U14 national championships at an inland surf lake (October 2026). No participation figures.

props.name: GB Snowsport / School Games, VI Skiing challenge cards
props.note: Read. Sports-hall cards for visually impaired pupils. Snowplough: tips of the feet in, tails out, slight pressure on the inside of the feet, to slow or stop. Parallel turn left: heavy right (outside) foot, light left foot, lean into the turn.

props.name: ACL evidence: Hewett 2005; Della Villa 2020; Achenbach 2024 (women); Crossley 2020
props.note: used for fault definitions and safety wording only; never for injury prediction

props.name: Stuelcken, Ferdinands & Sinclair 2010, Three-dimensional trunk kinematics and low back pain in elite female fast bowlers, J Appl Biomech
props.note: Not opened. The only women's fast-bowling technique source found; needed for women's bands.

props.name: Futsal Laws of the Game 2025-26 (FIFA); FIFA Training Centre beach soccer tutorials
props.note: futsal kick-in and format rules; beach soccer: https://www.fifatrainingcentre.com/en/practice/beach-soccer/block-1/passing.php

props.name: FIG, Code of Points in Parkour 2025-2028 (published April 2024, in force 1 January 2025)
props.note: Read. Speed (timed run A to B, to 1/1000 s; missing a checkpoint disqualifies) and Freestyle (run of skill, style, fluidity and mastery; 20-45 s; three Execution and three Difficulty judges; Execution out of 15 covering safety, landing quality and flow). Deductions for landings where the feet do not obviously touch the floor first, and for stutter steps and stops. Athletes are responsible for their own risk assessment. No age groups or course-height limits in the text.

props.name: Fortenbaugh, Fleisig & Andrews 2009, Baseball pitching biomechanics in relation to injury risk and performance, Sports Health 1(4):314-320 (borrowed from the baseball_softball sub-graph)
props.note: Borrowed for the overhand throw: shoulder abducted about 90 deg at foot contact and release; stride foot about 19 deg closed. Pitching from a mound, not infield throws; used as a guide only.

props.name: IHF Rules of the Game, Indoor Handball (1 March 2022; some provisions from 1 July 2022)
props.note: Read about a third verbatim. Court 40 x 20 m; goal-area line at 6 m, free-throw line 3 m outside it, 7 m line, 4 m goalkeeper line. Only the goalkeeper may enter the goal area; a player may enter after playing the ball if it does not disadvantage the opponents (6:3a). Players may take at most 3 steps with the ball (7:3) and hold it at most 3 seconds (7:2); no touching the ball twice after controlling it unless it has touched the floor, another player or the goal (7:7). Ball sizes: size 3 for men and male youth 16+ (58-60 cm); size 2 for women, female youth 14+ and male youth 12-16 (54-56 cm); size 1 for female youth 8-14 and male youth 8-12 (50-52 cm). Passive play, the 7 m throw procedure and Rule 8 (actions toward the opponent) were seen only in a summary.

props.name: BISFed (now World Boccia), International Boccia Rules 2021-2024 v1 (Boccia Canada copy)
props.note: Read verbatim to about a quarter, rest in summary. Court 12.5 x 6 m with six throwing boxes; six red, six blue and a white jack; balls 275 g +/- 12 g, 270 mm +/- 8 mm. Individual: 4 ends of 6 balls; pairs 4 ends of 3; teams 6 ends of 2. Time per end varies by class (in summary: BC1 5 min, BC2 4, BC3 6, BC4 4). BC3 athletes use a ramp with a ramp operator who stays in the box and may not look into the playing area during an end (3.5.1); BC1 and some BC4 foot players may have a sport assistant. 'Propel' covers throwing, kicking or releasing from a ramp.

props.name: World Bowls, Laws of the Sport of Bowls, Crystal Mark 4th edition (Bowls South Africa copy)
props.note: Laws 1-38 read verbatim, the rest in summary. Mat centred on the rink with the mat line at least 2 m from the rear ditch and 25 m from the front ditch (6.1.1). At delivery all or part of one foot on or above the mat (7.1); wheelchair users all or part of one wheel (7.2); first foot fault is a warning, later ones make the bowl dead (8.1-8.2). Jack improperly delivered if it rests in the ditch, outside the rink or less than 23 m from the mat line (10.1; 21 m allowed domestically, 10.5). Bowl dead if a non-toucher in the ditch, under 14 m from the mat line, or outside a side boundary (17.1). Non-delivering players at the mat end stand at least 1 m behind the mat (12.1.1). Delivery is an underarm release from the hand or an approved device (C.3). Singles 2-4 bowls each; pairs 2-4; triples 2-3; fours 2. In summary: aids for players with disabilities, including assistants and a centre-line string for blind and partially sighted players, support devices and kneeling deliveries (41.2-41.8).

props.name: International Korfball Federation, The Rules of Korfball 2023 (valid from 1 September 2023)
props.note: Read to rule 5.8 verbatim, rest in summary. Field 40 x 20 m in two zones; korf top 3.50 m high; ball size 5. Four men and four women, two of each in each zone; zones and roles switch after every two goals; two halves of 25 minutes; 25-second attack clock. Controlled contact is allowed, uncontrolled contact is not. Prohibited: running with the ball (6.1: in summary, a player may not still hold the ball when a third foot lands), playing alone, shooting from a defended position, handing the ball, hindering an opposite-sex player who is shooting (6.6, heading only), playing with the foot, pushing or holding. An IKF update takes effect on 1 September 2026 (not read).

props.name: Yanai T, Mechanics of body roll in front-crawl swimming (ISBS proceedings)
props.note: Read. 11 male competitive swimmers at sprint speed, breathing every two cycles. Roll angular momentum is larger towards the breathing side; stroke frequency about 0.63 Hz (about 38 cycles per minute) and kick frequency 1.92 Hz.

props.name: CricShot10: cricket batting shot video dataset (Sen et al. 2021, Sensors 21(8):2846)
props.licence: conflicting: repo shows CC0-1.0 but README says research use only; YouTube-sourced video
props.note: 10 shot classes (cover, defence, flick, hook, late cut, lofted, pull, square cut, straight, sweep). Names only; not for commercial training.

props.name: Ringette Canada, What is ringette (2026)
props.note: Read. Created in Canada in 1963; hollow rubber ring; straight sticks; 30-second shot clock; no intentional body contact; goalie cages with tight bars so a stick cannot get through.

props.name: IWBF, Quick rule guide (web page)
props.note: Read. Same basket height and court as standing basketball; players may not use their legs or feet on the floor to steer; players are classified by function from 1.0 to 4.5 points.

props.name: Hsieh YY, Huang CF 2012, Differences between male and female players in the sagittal plane biomechanics during volleyball spike landing (30th ISBS Conference, Melbourne)
props.note: Read. 8 men and 8 women, university level, 300 Hz. Jump height 0.71 m (men) and 0.51 m (women). Knee flexion 15 and 13 deg at initial contact; peak 73 and 71 deg; vertical force about 4.5-4.8 body weights.

props.name: RNLI, Rip currents
props.note: Read; undated. Choose a lifeguarded beach and swim between the red-and-yellow flags; in a rip, do not fight it, stay with your board (or Float to Live), swim parallel to the shore, raise a hand and shout; call 999 or 112 and ask for the Coastguard. Rips usually 1-2 mph, up to 4-5 mph.

props.name: O'Donovan DP 2011, Kinematics of throwing in Paralympic boccia athletes with cerebral palsy (MPE thesis, University of Otago)
props.note: Abstract read. 4 athletes with cerebral palsy (BC1, BC2), 80 throws at 3-9 m: very little variation in hand path and release point; athletes traded release speed against angle; no clear kinematic difference between successful and unsuccessful throws.

props.name: World Archery Rulebook, Book 3: Target Archery (version effective 27 January 2026)
props.note: Chapters 9-18 read verbatim. Ends of 3 or 6 arrows; 40 s per arrow (30 s or 20 s at ranking events and in alternate shooting). Athletes shoot standing, unsupported, with the head over the shooting line at full draw (10.4). Draw only on the shooting line, with the bow pointing at the athlete's own target (10.9); no technique that could send an arrow beyond the safety zone if released (10.10); repeated dangerous technique leads to disqualification. Only those shooting are on the line; others stay behind the waiting line. Five or more sound signals stop all shooting in an emergency. Distances and age classes are in other books (not read).

props.name: Scottish Darts Association, Playing Rules (updated 11 August 2013)
props.note: Read. Same board height and 2.37 m distance; a player who persists in overstepping the throw line after a challenge scores zero for that throw.

props.name: BWF Shuttle Time: Schools Badminton Teachers' Manual (English, hosted by the Hellenic Badminton Federation)
props.licence: BWF; no licence stated; facts only
props.note: Read about three-quarters verbatim. Forehand V-grip and backhand thumb grip; lunge like a large stride, lead foot points at the shuttle, heel first, lead knee and foot point the same way, rear knee slightly bent; progress lunge, then chasse and lunge, then split step, chasse and lunge. High serve: sideways stance, weight on the rear leg, hit under the shuttle in front and to the side. Low backhand serve: short relaxed thumb grip, racket out in front, swing forwards slowly. Badminton is a safe, low-impact sport for children; teachers control intensity. Overhead hitting pages were only summarised, not read.

props.name: Scottish Gymnastics, Photography Policy
props.note: Read. Covers still and video by members, parents and crews on any device. No images of children in provocative poses or partial undress beyond the sporting activity; no images that focus on the groin in split positions; if in doubt, do not share. Accreditation needed for dedicated cameras at events. Says nothing on consent, analysis video or storage. Undated.

props.name: Leitz RS 2015, The relationship between core stability related measures and performance in adolescent all-star cheerleaders, MSc thesis, Georgia Southern University
props.note: Read in part. 50 girls aged 10-18. Toe-touch scored on the angle between the legs at peak height: level 175-195 deg, hyperextended above 195, below level under 175. Landings scored stick, small, medium or large error.

props.name: Jiao Y, Li H, Liu H, Qu Y 2020, Upper extremity kinematics of an elite snooker player on stop shots, ISBS Proceedings 38(1):132-136
props.note: Read. 1 elite professional man, 3 stop shots, 200 Hz motion capture. Whole stroke about 1.7 s. Shoulder flexion range about 23 deg over the stroke and about 8 deg from end of backswing to contact; elbow range about 61 deg; shoulder moved about 4 cm. Very repeatable (curve similarity above 0.98 for shoulder, elbow and wrist).

props.name: Jacquier-Bret & Gorce 2024, Kinematics characteristics of key points of interest during the tennis serve: systematic review and meta-analysis, Front Sports Act Living 6:1432030
props.note: 27 studies. Trophy: trunk inclination 25.0 +/- 7.1 deg, front knee flexion 64.5 +/- 9.7, back knee 67.4 +/- 16.4. Racket low point: shoulder lateral rotation 130.1 +/- 26.5. Impact: shoulder elevation 110.7 +/- 16.9, elbow flexion 30.1 +/- 15.9. Uses the Kovacs & Ellenbecker 8-stage model.

props.name: UK Ultimate, Ultimate for schools and teachers (teacher training)
props.note: Read. For Key Stage 2 upwards; boys and girls play together and players referee themselves through Spirit of the Game; Young Leader Award from years 5-6. No participation figures stated.

props.name: Lam WK, Wong DWC, Lee WCC 2020, Biomechanics of lower limb in badminton lunge: a systematic scoping review, PeerJ 8:e10300
props.note: Read in part. 20 studies, 314 players (264 men, 50 women). Lunges can load about 2.5 times body weight; skilled players had shorter foot contact times and larger foot-strike angles. Table values were not readable.

props.name: Scottish Athletics, Seated throws information paper (May 2024)
props.note: Read. Seated throws are for athletes who cannot stand or have balance or stability difficulties; F31-34 coordination impairments, F51-57 limb deficiency or spinal cord injury. Frame set-up: plumb line to check nothing is over the rim; usually four non-elastic ratchet straps tightened together so the frame does not move; ideally five people to secure it; assistant sits away from the athlete. Implement table by class for Open/U20 and U17 (for example shot 2-4 kg, discus 1 kg, club 397 g). No technique guidance.

props.name: Ridgway ME, Hamilton N, Spiking technique of elite and recreational female volleyball players (ISBS proceedings)
props.note: Read (OCR text). 6 elite and 3 recreational women, 100 Hz 2D film. Jump height 51.6 cm (elite) vs 38.1 cm (recreational); flight time 0.63 vs 0.56 s; knee angle at the end of the approach about 110 deg in both groups (angle convention not stated); elite players had a shorter set-up knee bend and faster knee extension. Year not shown.

props.name: USA Pickleball Official Rulebook, section 4.A (serve), as cited by the engine's curated pickleball.serve@1.0.0 protocol
props.note: Not re-read on 2026-11-05. The curated protocol cites rule 4.A.7 (contact below the navel, paddle head below the wrist, upward arc) and 4.A.4 (feet behind the baseline). The 2025 summary (G1) says 'waist level'; check the current rulebook's wording (gap PB-03).

props.name: Borgonovo-Santos M, Telles T, Nessler J, Peduzzi de Castro M, Fernandes RJ, Vilas-Boas JP 2021, Are the kinetics and kinematics of the surf pop-up related to the anthropometric characteristics of the surfer?, Sensors 21(5):1783
props.note: Read (later sections in summary). 23 male surfers on land, a board outline over force plates, motion capture: pop-up 1.20 s (SD 0.19): push-up about 0.71 s, reaching about 0.48 s; hands about 0.46 m apart; feet about 0.63 m apart on landing; knees about 100 deg at peak landing force; front foot took about 61-72% of the load; arms and legs shared load evenly.

props.name: Kim MH, Park JC, Byun KS 2019, A comparative analysis of the kinematical characteristics of forehand and backhand flying disc throwing, Journal of Digital Convergence 17(12):555-563
props.note: Read. 5 right-handed male players, 200 Hz. The forehand uses the arm and wrist more (wrist range 79 +/- 7 vs 35 +/- 10 deg; elbow 89 vs 74 deg); the backhand uses the trunk and pelvis more (trunk rotation range 151 +/- 15 vs 136 +/- 20 deg; pelvis 125 +/- 13 vs 88 +/- 24 deg). Wrist angle at release 125 deg (forehand) vs 160 deg (backhand).

props.name: World Bowling, Statutes and Playing Rules (September 2019; copy hosted by the Asian Bowling Federation)
props.note: About a third read verbatim; playing rules seen in a summary. Ten frames; strike = all pins with the first ball (10 plus the next two balls); spare = all pins with two balls (10 plus the next ball); 300 is a perfect game. Foul (2.8): any part of the body touching on or beyond the foul line during or after a delivery; the delivery counts but scores no pins. World Youth Championships held every second year. Ball and lane specifications not in the part read.

props.name: World Lacrosse, Sixes Rule Book 2026-2028 (version 2.0, May 2026)
props.note: About 40% read verbatim, the rest in a summary. Field 70 x 36 m; goals 1.83 x 1.83 m; crease radius 3 m; six on the field (five plus a goalkeeper); four 8-minute quarters; 30-second shot clock. Ball 19.7-20.3 cm, 142-149 g. Sticks: women 90-110 cm, men 100-110 cm. Attackers may not enter the opponents' crease (6.16.1). Mouthguards required for all; men wear helmets and gloves; women's eyewear mandatory at World Lacrosse events from the 2027 Sixes Worlds. Summary only: body checking prohibited in any form in sixes (8.3.1); slashing and cross-checks prohibited; dangerous propel and follow-through are fouls.

props.name: British Rowing, Safety: Capsize training (Stephen Worley, Honorary Rowing Safety Adviser)
props.note: Read. Check the water and boat (heel restraints, hatches, seat); anchored safety boats with throw lines; buoyancy aids for anyone who wants or needs one; complete British Rowing's capsize online module; do not swim with the boat but climb onto it and paddle to the bank; practise self-rescue, buddy rescue and being rescued. Undated.

props.name: Bowls England, Coaching and Bowling with a disability pages (2025-2026)
props.note: Read in part. Coach Bowls is the only nationally recognised bowls coaching qualification in England; para lawn bowls at Glasgow 2026; disability open days and classification clinics. No participation figures on these pages.

props.name: Ringette Canada, How to play (October 2024)
props.note: Read. Six a side (two defence, two forwards, a centre, a goalie); the ring cannot be skated over a blue line and must be passed over both blue lines to a teammate; only three players per team (plus the defending goalie) inside each free-play line; no player but the goalie may enter the goal crease; no body contact, slashing, hitting or tripping (2-4 minute penalties); play starts with a free pass from the centre circle within 5 seconds; two halves of 15-25 minutes.

props.name: Tighe A, Kenny IC 2015, A qualitative biomechanical analysis of the punt kick in Gaelic football comparing dominant and non-dominant kicking legs, GAA Games Development Conference
props.note: Read. 20 elite Gaelic footballers, 4 kicks per leg at a 10 m target: 90% of dominant-leg kicks vs 50% of non-dominant kicks rated as expert technique; the kicking arm, non-kicking arm and support leg differed most.

props.name: Wu T, Pearsall DJ, Russell PJ, Imanaka Y 2015, Kinematic comparisons between forward and backward skating in hockey, ISBS Proceedings 33:1324-1327 (borrowed)
props.note: Read. 7 male club hockey players, 60 Hz video: at skate contact knee about 96 deg and hip about 85 deg; at propulsion knee about 137 deg, hip about 128 deg and trunk about 27 deg above horizontal; forward speed about 10 m/s. Borrowed for the ringette stride; women and juniors not studied.

props.name: Team England, What sports and events are at the Glasgow 2026 Commonwealth Games
props.note: Read for sport 47 and the third-20 list. Para athletics is on the Glasgow 2026 programme, including para jumps and throws.

props.name: Klitgaard KK, Andersen CH, Adler AT, de Zee M 2017, A kinematic analysis of ten-pin bowling technique of elite bowlers, ISB 2017 abstract
props.note: Read. 9 elite men; very consistent technique; knee and hip extend and the body rises just before release, after the lowest point of the swing.

props.name: Haar S, van Assel CM, Faisal AA, Kinematic signatures of learning that emerge in a real-world motor skill task (bioRxiv 612218, v3)
props.note: Read. 30 novices (12 women, 18 men), 300 pool shots each with a motion suit. Most movement and variance was in the cueing shoulder; large shoulder variance was a sign of being a novice. Accuracy plateaued after about 200 shots; people who varied more at first learned faster.

props.name: Hockey Alberta Information Bulletin 21-10 (2 June 2022): U18 non-body checking at Tiers 4-6
props.note: Read. In Alberta minor leagues from 2022-23, U15 and U18 Tiers 4-6 are non-body checking; U15 AAA/AA/Tiers 1-3 and U18 AAA/AA/Tiers 1-3 allow body checking. Provincial only; no Hockey Canada national document was read.

props.name: World Para Athletics Rules and Regulations 2024, Rules 34-37 (seated throws), Athletics Australia copy (March 2024)
props.note: Read. Frame seat at most 75 cm high including cushioning (35.1a); bar a single straight piece; no part of the frame may move during the throw (35.1f); frame, bar and footplates inside the vertical plane of the circle rim (35.4); WPA-approved tie-downs (34). Time to throw: 4 min F32-34 and F54-57, 5 min F31 and F51-53 (35.5). Both legs in contact with the seat from the back of the knee to the back of the buttock (36.1a) and the seated position held until the implement lands (36.1b); leaving the seated position from taking the implement until landing is a fault (36.3). Fouls: implement lands on or outside the sector line, or a holding strap touched outside the rim (35.9). F31-33 and F51-53 may tape a hand to the pole (34.5-34.6). Club for F31/32 and F51 (37.1).

props.name: Paddle UK and RNLI, PaddleSafe campaign (about June 2025)
props.note: Read; undated. Five key messages: always wear a buoyancy aid, tell someone where you are going, carry a phone, check the weather, know your limits. About half of paddleboard incidents attended by the RNLI involved being swept out to sea or offshore winds.

props.name: Liu Y, Zhu Z, Chen X, Deng C, Ma X, Zhao B 2022, Biomechanics of the lead straight punch of different level boxers, Front Physiol 13:1015154
props.note: Read. 16 men (elite and junior). Elite vs junior lead straight: peak fist speed 7.16 vs 6.32 m/s; peak force 1508 vs 1035 N; lead-leg peak force 19.7 vs 13.3 N/kg; punch contact time about 43-45 ms. Better boxers push harder with the lead leg.

props.name: International Padel Federation (FIP): Rules of Padel (review of application 1 January 2026; revised Acapulco, 28 November 2025)
props.note: Read. Court 10 x 20 m; service lines 6.95 m from the net; net 0.88 m at the centre and 0.92 m at the ends; end walls 3 m plus 1 m of fence. Service (Rule 6): bounce the ball within the service box; strike it at or below waist height with at least one foot on the ground; do not touch the service line or the imaginary centre line; the ball must bounce in the diagonal box; second serve allowed. Fault if the serve bounces in the box and then hits the metal fence (7.1e). After bouncing on the opponent's side the ball stays in play off walls and fence (12.3, 14.1c); hitting the opponent's walls or fence without a bounce loses the point (13.1g); touching the net loses the point (13.1a).

props.name: darts-uk.co.uk, Youth darts (personal site, David King)
props.note: Read. Not a governing body. Says children should be supervised by an adult; young players can start with a lower board and move to 1.73 m by the early teens; a wheelchair board at 1.37 m; round-the-clock as a basic practice game.

props.name: Williams BK, Sanders RH, Ryu JH, Graham-Smith P, Sinclair PJ 2020, The kinematic differences between accurate and inaccurate squash forehand drives for athletes of different skill levels, J Sports Sci 38(10):1115-1123
props.note: Read in full. 18 male academy players (9 highly skilled, about 23 years; 9 less skilled, about 15 years); 180 forehand drives, Vicon 200 Hz. Highly skilled players had more wrist extension at impact (46 vs 31 deg), more shoulder elevation, a flatter racket face (119 vs 123-125 deg), forward racket speed about 25 vs 24 m/s, and much less shot-to-shot variation (racket speed SD about 1.0 vs 1.4-2.3 m/s). Accurate and inaccurate shots barely differed within a player.

props.name: Schram B, Furness J, Kemp-Smith K, Sharp J, Cristini M, Harvie D, Keogh J, Sheppard J, Climstein M 2019, A biomechanical analysis of the stand-up paddle board stroke: a comparative study, PeerJ 7:e8006
props.note: Read. 7 experienced and 19 inexperienced paddlers on a SUP ergometer, motion capture: experienced paddlers used more hip flexion range (66 vs 50 deg), less shoulder range (57 vs 79 deg) and a straighter lower arm (elbow flexion minimum 6 vs 25 deg); trunk flexion range similar (about 5-6 deg).

props.name: Wikipedia, Kho kho (secondary)
props.note: Read. Field 27 x 16 m, poles 24 m apart, free zones behind the poles; 12 players in the field per side in batches of three runners; chasing side 9 on the field (8 sitting in the central lane facing alternate sides, 1 active); the sitting chaser must not rise before receiving the kho; direction kept until the free zone; turns of 9 minutes, two turns each. Ultimate Kho Kho (2022 league, used at the 2025 World Cup) is seven-a-side with 7-minute turns.

props.name: How to pitch according to the Rules (fastpitch coaching handout)
props.note: Read. Both feet on the rubber; present the ball for at least 1 s; pivot foot stays in contact (crow hop illegal under the rules it follows); underhand release with the wrist no farther from the body than the elbow. Differs from G3 on revolutions (one full circle) and crow hop wording.

props.name: Zacharias E, Robak N, Passmore S 2024, An examination of studies related to the sport of curling: a scoping review, Front Sports Act Living 6:1291241
props.note: Read (second half in summary). 94 studies: experienced sweepers apply more downward force; women showed more hip flexibility in the slide; experienced curlers took longer over the whole delivery; many sweeping methods lack evidence.

props.name: United World Wrestling, International Wrestling Rules (December 2025 edition, in force 1 January 2026), cover letter
props.note: Only the cover letter could be read; the rule text did not extract. Changes in force from 1 January 2026, including clarifications on stepping out when a defender goes down on the knees (Art. 38) and on passivity for U15, U17 and veterans (Art. 46).

props.name: Government of Western Australia, Sports dimensions guide: darts (citing Darts Australia playing rules, August 2015)
props.note: Read. Board and distance as WDF; boards at least 3 m apart; an encroachment line 1.5 m behind the oche where the opponent stands; only officials may be in front of the thrower.

props.name: Sawacha Z, Spolaor F, Negretto M, Cobelli C 2013, Biomechanical analysis of squat and counter movement jump in skaters, ISB 2013 poster
props.note: Read. 5 professional skaters vs 5 controls: skaters jumped higher with longer flight. Values not in the text read.

props.name: ITF Rules of Tennis (2026 edition)
props.licence: ITF, all rights reserved; facts only
props.note: Rules 1-31 read verbatim: court 23.77 x 8.23 m (doubles 10.97 m), net 0.914 m at the centre, service line 6.40 m from the net; Rule 16 the ball is released by hand and hit before it lands; Rule 18 foot fault (no walking or running, no touching the baseline or court, no touching outside the sideline or centre-mark extensions). Appendices (balls, 10-and-under rackets) seen only as a summary.

props.name: Kerwin DG, Trewartha G 2001, Strategies for maintaining a handstand in the anterior-posterior direction, Med Sci Sports Exerc 33(7):1182-1188
props.note: Read (abstract). Six handstand balances. Wrist torque dominated in many trials; better balances used wrist and shoulder with little hip; hips mattered more in less successful balances.

props.name: WP Cycling: UCI rules 1.3.013 and 1.3.022 (quoting UCI Cycling Regulations)
props.note: Read. 1.3.013: the peak of the saddle must be at least 5 cm behind a vertical line through the bottom bracket spindle (track sprint exempt, but never in front of it). 1.3.022: traditional handlebars only, within set limits. Secondary source; the UCI regulations themselves and extension limits were not read.

props.name: Tran KB, Yano S, Kondo T 2019, Coordination of human movements resulting in motor strategies exploited by skilled players during a throwing task, PLoS ONE 14(10):e0223837
props.note: Read in part. 8 experts (6 men, 2 women), 42 throws each at 2.37 m. Success 52-69%; vertical error about 13-18 mm; release-timing windows of only about 2-8 ms, and release-time variation about 1-2 ms. Faster darts went with wider timing windows. These timings are too fine for phone video.

props.name: Falcon Boat Club (Oxford), Swim tests, cold water and capsize drills v1.6 (December 2023)
props.note: Read. One club's junior policy, not national guidance: juniors show a 100 m swim, 5 m underwater, 5-minute float and 2-minute tread; those who have not passed wear a buoyancy aid; capsize drill within 6 months of joining, in water above 15 C with two adults present.

props.name: Parkour UK, Parkour coaching standards (2025 revision)
props.note: Read. Ratios 1:12 indoors and 1:8 outdoors in public spaces (risk assessment may lower, never raise); open sessions restricted to age 12+ and supervised; a first-aider on site; site-specific briefing before each session; pre-activity questionnaires and parental consent under 18; coaches under 18 may not coach independently; schools and playgrounds listed as environments.

props.name: Farana R and colleagues 2018, Technique selection in young female gymnasts: elbow and wrist joint loading during the cartwheel and round-off, Eur J Sport Sci
props.note: Read (abstract). 17 young female gymnasts; parallel, T-shape and reverse hand positions. Parallel and reverse placements produced higher elbow and wrist loads than the T-shape (large effects).

props.name: Ram J, Singh J, Singh B, Gogoi H, Rather NM 2022, Relationship of selected physical and angular kinematical variables with the performance of toe-touch skill in kabaddi, Physical Education Theory and Methodology 22(4):516-521
props.note: Read. 100 male raiders aged 18-25, 240 fps video. Median angles in the toe touch: leading knee about 173 deg (almost straight), leading ankle about 137 deg, hip about 149 deg; a more extended leading ankle went with better coach ratings (rs 0.33).

props.name: Yanagi H, Miyakoshi K, Fukuoka M, Yamamoto N 2012, Development of curling brush for measuring force exerted during sweeping, ISBS Proceedings 30:354-356
props.note: Read. 3 sweepers (1 experienced), instrumented brush: mean downward force about 185 N in maximal 10 s trials; the experienced curler's peaks were higher. Coaches can use downward force to assess sweeping.

props.name: Bowls Canada, Para bowls classification (about 2025)
props.note: Read. B5: restricted grip and upper-limb function, balance or coordination, may need a splinting device; B6 and B7: reduced balance; B8: minimal impairment. No classification needed for club play.

props.question: Through contact, does the racket move forward and slightly across the ball with an open face (slice), rather than down like a smash?

props.name: bounce_in_box
props.question: Is the ball bounced behind the service line, on the server's own side of the court?

props.name: lands_in_diagonal_box
props.question: Does the serve land in the diagonally opposite service box? (Practice check only; the referee decides.)

props.name: shoulder_height
props.question: Does the discus leave the hand at about shoulder height, with the arm long and the discus flat?

props.name: bar_hold
props.question: Is the non-throwing hand holding the bar (or strapped or taped to it) steadily through the throw?

props.name: frame_in_circle
props.question: Do the frame, bar and footplates all appear to stay inside the edge of the throwing circle?

props.name: helmet
props.question: Is the athlete wearing a helmet?

props.name: feet_first_balls
props.question: Do the feet clearly touch the floor first, landing on the balls of the feet with the heels following?

props.name: diagonal_roll
props.question: Rate 1-5: does the roll travel diagonally from one shoulder across the back to the opposite hip, with the head tucked to the side and not touching the mat?

props.name: hand_and_foot
props.question: Does the traceur place one hand (and for a safety vault, one foot) on the obstacle with the body travelling sideways-on over it, eyes on the landing?

props.name: paddle_face_open
props.question: At contact, is the paddle face slightly open (tilted up), lifting the ball gently over the net?

props.name: lands_in_kitchen
props.question: Does the ball bounce inside the opponents' non-volley zone (kitchen)?

props.name: ready_paddle_up
props.question: Before the volley, is the paddle held up in front of the chest in a ready position?

props.name: ball_drop_or_volley
props.question: Across these frames before contact, is the ball released from the hand and struck out of the air (volley serve), or does it bounce before contact (drop serve)?

props.name: eyes_on_contact
props.question: At contact, is the player's head still with the eyes on the contact point?

props.name: grip_continental
props.question: Does the paddle grip look like a continental (handshake) grip, an eastern forehand grip, or is it unclear?

props.name: sweep_pass
props.question: Does the passer turn side-on, sweep the ring from back to front, release it in front of the body and follow through towards the target?

props.name: follow_through
props.question: Does the shooter keep the stick below shoulder height and follow through towards the target after release?

props.name: head_up
props.question: Is the skater's head up, knees bent, with the stick held in front and below shoulder height?

props.name: carry_bat
props.question: After hitting, does the batter keep hold of the bat (or place it down safely) rather than throwing it as they start to run?

props.name: opposite_foot_step
props.question: As the ball is released, is the bowler stepping forward onto the foot opposite the bowling hand, with the arm swinging below the shoulder?

props.name: eyes_on_target
props.question: At release, is the fielder looking at the target post or partner?

props.name: shoulders_relaxed
props.question: At the catch, are the shoulders relaxed and down, with the neck tall (not hunched up to the ears)?

props.name: hands_level
props.question: As the handle passes over the knees, does it move in a straight, level line (not lifted up over the knees)?

props.name: follow_through_line
props.question: Does the kicking leg follow through along the line towards the posts?

props.name: head_over_ball
props.question: At contact, is the kicker's head still and looking down at the ball?

props.name: hands_follow_target
props.question: After release, do the hands finish pointing at the target?

props.name: no_backswing
props.question: Does the passer sweep the ball straight towards the target without first drawing it back (a wind-up)?

props.name: feet_set
props.question: Are the thrower's feet set and still at release, rather than stepping forward?

props.name: two_hands_release
props.question: Do both hands release the ball together, with the ball spinning on a straight line towards the target?

props.name: flat_inside_foot
props.question: Is the ball struck with the flat inside of the foot, with the kicking knee turned out and the support knee slightly bent?

props.name: square_to_net
props.question: Is the setter balanced and facing the net, lifting the ball with the inside of the foot?

props.name: thrower_feet
props.question: Does the thrower keep both feet still inside the quarter circle, off the lines, while throwing?

props.name: front_foot_forward
props.question: While pushing, is the front foot turned to point forward on the front bolts (not across the board)?

props.name: helmet
props.question: Is the skater wearing a helmet?

props.name: feet_over_bolts
props.question: On landing, are both feet over the bolts of the board?

props.name: helmet
props.question: Is the skater wearing a helmet?

props.name: skis_parallel
props.question: At the middle of the turn, are the skis parallel (not in a wedge)?

props.name: helmet
props.question: Is the skier wearing a helmet?

props.name: looking_ahead
props.question: As the rider changes edge, is the head up and looking towards the next turn rather than down at the board?

props.name: racket_up
props.question: As the player moves into the lunge, is the racket up and prepared before the front foot lands?

props.name: front_wall_target
props.question: Does the serve hit the front wall above the service line and land in the opposite back quarter of the court?

props.name: compact_follow_through
props.question: After impact, does the racket finish in a compact follow-through (not swinging wide across the body)?

props.name: eyewear
props.question: Is the player wearing squash eye protection (goggles) over the eyes?

props.name: board_trim
props.question: Is the board level in the water, with the nose just clear of the surface (not pushing water or pointing up)?

props.name: flow
props.question: Rate 1-5: does the surfer carry speed smoothly through the bottom turn and up the face without stalling?

props.name: head_lead
props.question: Rate 1-5: do the surfer's head and shoulders turn first, looking up the wave towards where the turn will go?

props.name: hands_and_feet
props.question: Are the hands placed flat beside the chest for the push, and do both feet land on the board's centre line, sideways to the nose?

props.name: feet_turned_out
props.question: During the kick, are the feet turned out (flexed) so the soles push the water back?

props.name: head_breaks_surface
props.question: In each stroke cycle, does part of the head come above the water?

props.name: breathing_sides
props.question: Does the swimmer breathe to both sides across the clip, or only one side?

props.name: entry_in_line
props.question: Does each hand enter the water in front of its own shoulder, rather than crossing over the centre line?

props.name: head_between_arms
props.question: In the streamline, is the head tucked between the arms rather than lifted to look forward?

props.name: bat_angle
props.question: At contact, is the bat face slightly closed (tilted forward) rather than open to the ceiling?

props.name: follow_through_target
props.question: Does the bat finish pointing towards where the ball is going?

props.name: brush_upward
props.question: Through contact, does the bat move forward and upward with the bat face closed (tilted over the ball)?

props.name: recover_ready
props.question: After the follow-through, does the player return quickly to a balanced ready position?

props.name: ball_not_hidden
props.question: Is the ball visible to the receiver until it is struck, with the free arm moved out of the space between the ball and the net? (Practice check only; the umpire decides.)

props.name: open_palm
props.question: Before the toss, is the ball resting on a flat, open palm with the fingers together and the thumb free (not cupped or held in the fingers)?

props.name: both_hands_on_racket
props.question: Are both hands on the racket handle at contact, with the non-dominant hand above the dominant hand?

props.name: finish_over_shoulder
props.question: Does the racket finish high over the dominant shoulder, with the chest facing the net?

props.name: finish_over_shoulder
props.question: Does the racket finish over or around the opposite shoulder?

props.name: grip_type
props.question: Which forehand grip is used: eastern, semi-western, western, or continental? Answer only from what is visible.

props.name: stance_type
props.question: Is the stance at contact open, semi-open, neutral (square) or closed?

props.name: first_step_direction
props.question: Is the first step taken towards the ball (for example a turn and crossover or a pivot), rather than a step backwards?

props.name: split_timed_with_opponent
props.question: Does the player land the split step at about the moment the opponent (or feeder) hits the ball? Answer 'unclear' if the opponent is not visible.

props.name: continental_grip
props.question: Is the racket held with a continental (hammer) grip rather than a forehand (frying-pan) grip? Answer only from what is visible.

props.name: lands_inside_court
props.question: After contact, does the server land on the front foot inside the court, moving forward?

props.name: tossing_arm_extended
props.question: At the trophy position, is the tossing arm extended up towards the ball?

props.name: push_away_with_step
props.question: Does the ball move out (push-away) together with the first or second step, rather than before the feet move?

props.name: thumb_out_first
props.question: At release, does the thumb come out of the ball before the fingers?

props.name: finish_position
props.question: After release, is the bowler balanced on the slide foot with the ball-side leg behind and the opposite arm out to the side?

props.name: hands_out
props.question: Before receiving the pass, did the player show hands out towards the passer as a target?

props.name: ball_between_feet
props.question: Is the ball placed on the ground between the player's feet before they step over it?

props.name: ball_in_two_hands
props.question: During the step, is the ball held in two hands in front of the body, ready to pass?

props.name: hands_low
props.question: Is the marker's arms out and hands low and wide, without wrapping around the thrower?

props.name: flat_release
props.question: At release, is the disc flat or with the far edge slightly lower, rather than tilted up?

props.name: across_body
props.question: After release, does the throwing arm finish out in front or on the throwing side, rather than swinging across the body?

props.name: both_arms_swing
props.question: During the take-off, do both arms swing back and then forcefully up?

props.name: two_foot_landing
props.question: Does the player land on both feet at about the same time?

props.name: facing_target
props.question: At contact, is the platform angled towards the target (the setter's position)?

props.name: hands_joined
props.question: At contact, are the hands joined with the thumbs side by side, and does the ball meet the forearms rather than the hands or wrists?

props.name: behind_end_line
props.question: At contact, are both feet behind the end line without touching it? (Practice check only; officials decide faults.)

props.name: firm_hand
props.question: At contact, is the hand firm and flat, hitting the middle of the ball with a short follow-through?

props.name: elbows_locked_overhead
props.question: At the finish, are both elbows locked with the bar over the back of the neck and the feet in line?

props.name: neutral_back
props.question: As the bar leaves the floor, does the back stay in a long, neutral position rather than rounding?

props.name: safety_set_up
props.question: Is there a spotter or are safety bars set in the rack?

props.name: feet_on_footrest
props.question: Do the player's feet stay on the footrest during the turn (not touching the floor)?

props.name: ball_on_lap
props.question: While pushing with the ball, is it resting on the lap (not held between the knees)?

props.name: chair_angle
props.question: Is the chair set at a consistent angle to the free-throw line, turned so the shooting arm lines up with the basket?

props.name: head_and_back
props.question: At the end of the step, is the head up and the back straight (not looking down), with the lead knee bent under the body?

props.name: sprawl_shape
props.question: At the sprawl, are the hips on or near the mat, legs back and wide, on the toes, with the head up?

props.name: head_up
props.question: Is the wrestler's head up with eyes forward, elbows in and hands in front?
